Where a former relevant child to whom this section applies is not receiving advice and support under this section, the local authority must offer such advice and support\u2014(a) as soon as possible after he or she reaches the age of 21, and(b) at least once in every 12 months.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3218"},{"id":"3220","label":"Children in care - advice on promotion of educational achievement of children formerly in care","desc":"A local authority in England must make advice and information available for the purpose of promoting the educational achievement of each relevant child educated in their area. The advice and information must be made available to\u2014(a) any person who has parental responsibility for the child,(b) the member of staff at the child's school designated under section 20A of the Children and Young Persons Act 2008 or by virtue of section 2E of the Academies Act 2010, and(c) any other person that the local authority consider appropriate. A local authority in England must appoint at least one person for the purpose of discharging the duty imposed by subsection and the person appointed for that purpose must be an officer employed by the authority or another local authority in England.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3220"},{"id":"2010","label":"Children in care - care orders and care plans","desc":"Where an application is made on which a care order might be made with respect to a child, the appropriate local authority must, within such time as the court may direct, prepare a plan (a care plan) for the future care of the child.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2010"},{"id":"3221","label":"Children in care - corporate parenting principles","desc":"A local authority must in relation to looked after children and former looked after young people under 25, have regard to the need to (a) act in the best interests, and promote the physical and mental health and well-being, of those children and young people;(b) encourage those children and young people to express their views, wishes and feelings;(c) take into account the views, wishes and feelings of those children and young people;(d) help those children and young people gain access to, and make the best use of, services provided by the local authority and its relevant partners;(e) promote high aspirations, and seek to secure the best outcomes, for those children and young people;(f) for those children and young people to be safe, and for stability in their home lives, relationships and education or work;(g) prepare those children and young people for adulthood and independent living","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3221"},{"id":"2011","label":"Children in care - effect of care order","desc":"Where a care order is made with respect to a child it shall be the duty of the local authority designated by the order to receive the child into their care and to keep him in their care while the order remains in force","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2011"},{"id":"3222","label":"Children in care - guidance on corporate parenting principles","desc":"A local authority must have regard to any guidance issued by the Secretary of State in performing its duty under section 1.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3222"},{"id":"3223","label":"Children in care - local offer for care leavers","desc":"A local authority must having consulted relevant persons, publish and keep up to date information about\u2014(a) services which the local authority offers for care leavers as a result of its functions under the Children Act 1989;(b) other services which the local authority offers that may assist care leavers in, or in preparing for, adulthood and independent living.This information is to be known as a local offer for care leavers.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3223"},{"id":"2012","label":"Children in care - parental contact etc. with children in care","desc":"Where a child is in the care of a local authority, the authority shall allow the child reasonable contact with his parents; any guardian; any person who has parental responsibility for him; where there was a residence order in force with respect to the child immediately before the care order was made, the person in whose favour the order was made; and where, immediately before the care order was made, a person had care of the child by virtue of an order made in the exercise of the High Court's inherent jurisdiction with respect to children, that person.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2012"},{"id":"3219","label":"Children in care - promotion of educational achievement of children formerly in care","desc":"A local authority in England may do anything else that they consider appropriate with a view to promoting the educational achievement of relevant children educated in their area.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/3219"},{"id":"2408","label":"Children with medical conditions - support","desc":"The appropriate authority for a school to which this section applies must make arrangements for supporting pupils at the school with medical conditions. In meeting this duty the appropriate authority must have regard to guidance issued by the Secretary of State.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2408"},{"id":"186","label":"Children's centres - consultation on provision, changes or closure","desc":"A local authority must consult as it thinks appropriate having regard to guidance from the Secretary of State before making arrangements for children's centres.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/186"},{"id":"187","label":"Children's centres - provision of services","desc":"A local authority must consider whether each of the early childhood services to be provided by them should be provided through children's centres.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/187"},{"id":"201","label":"Children's centres - publication of Chief Inspector's report","desc":"A local authority may distribute or publish a report which it receives from the Chief Inspector regarding children's centres.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/201"},{"id":"202","label":"Children's centres - written statement on Chief Inspector's report","desc":"A local authority may prepare and publish a written statement when a Chief Inspector's Report is received and have regard to the guidance of the Secretary of State when so doing.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/202"},{"id":"3702","label":"Children's homes - access to communication","desc":"The registered person must ensure that children are provided at all reasonable times with access to the following facilities which they may use without reference to persons working in the home\u2014(a) a telephone on which to make and receive telephone calls in private; and(b) facilities to send and receive post and, if the necessary facilities are provided for the use of children, electronic mail, in private.The registered person must ensure that a disabled child accommodated in the home is provided with access to such aids and equipment as the child may require as a result of the child's disability in order to facilitate the child's communication with other persons.If the registered person considers it to be necessary for the purpose of safeguarding or promoting the welfare of a child, the registered person may impose conditions, prohibitions or restrictions upon a child's\u2014(a) contact with parents, friends or relatives; or(b) access to communications No measure may be imposed by the registered person under unless\u2014(a) the child's placing authority consents to the imposition of the measure; or(b) the measure is imposed in an emergency, and full details are given to the placing authority within 24 hours of its imposition.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3702"},{"id":"3579","label":"Children's homes - appointment of independent person","desc":"he registered provider must appoint, at the registered provider\u2019s expense, a person (\u201cthe independent person\u201d) to visit and report on the children\u2019s home carried on by the registered provider.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3579"},{"id":"3573","label":"Children's homes - behaviour management policies and records","desc":"The registered person must prepare and implement a policy (\u201cthe behaviour management policy\u201d) which sets out how appropriate behaviour is to be promoted in the children\u2019s home and the measures of control, discipline and restraint which may be used in relation to children in the home.The registered person must keep the behaviour management policy under review and, where appropriate, revise it.The register person must ensure that procedures in regulations are followed after any use of a measure of control, discipline or restraint in relation to a child in the home.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3573"},{"id":"3574","label":"Children's homes - children's case records","desc":"The registered person must maintain records (\u201ccase records\u201d) for each child which include the information and documents listed in Schedule 3 in relation to each child, are kept up to date and are signed and dated by the author of each entry.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3574"},{"id":"3584","label":"Children's homes - complaints and representations","desc":"Subject to paragraph (6) of this regulation, the registered person must establish a procedure for considering complaints made by or on behalf of children.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3584"},{"id":"3566","label":"Children's homes - compliance with standards","desc":"A local authority in respect of a qualifying children\u2019s home, must comply with the following standards:- Quality standards for children's homes - Engaging with the wider system to ensure children's needs are met- The quality and purpose of care standard- The children's views, wishes and feelings standard- The education standard- The enjoyment and achievement standard- The health and well-being standard- The positive relationships standard- The protection of children standard- The leadership and management standard- The care planning standard and must have regard to the statements of standards published under section 23 of the Care Standards Act 2000","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3566"},{"id":"3701","label":"Children's homes - contact with other persons","desc":"The registered person must ensure that suitable facilities are provided within the children's home for any child accommodated there to meet privately at any reasonable time with the child's parents, friends, relatives or any of the following persons\u2014 (a) a solicitor or other adviser or advocate acting for the child;(b) an officer of the Children and Family Court Advisory and Support Service appointed for the child;(c) a social worker assigned to the child;(d) a person authorised by HMCI;(e) a person authorised by the local authority in whose area the home is located;(f) an independent visitor for looked after children(g) a person authorised by the Secretary of State to conduct an inspection in relation to the home and the children there;(h) a person appointed under the Children Act 1989 Representations Procedure (England) Regulations 2006;(i) an independent person visiting the home under regulation 44.The registered person must keep a record of any meeting carried out.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3701"},{"id":"3571","label":"Children's homes - employment of staff","desc":"(1) The registered person must ensure that each employee completes an appropriate induction, ensure that each permanent appointment of an employee is subject to the satisfactory completion of a period of probation andprovide each employee with a job description outlining the employee\u2019s responsibilities.(2) The registered person must operate a disciplinary procedure which, in particular provides for the suspension from work of an employee if necessary in the interests of the safety or welfare of children and provides that the failure on the part of an employee to report an incident of abuse, or suspected abuse, whether past or present, in relation to a child to the appropriate person is a ground on which disciplinary proceedings may be instituted.(3) For the purposes of this regulation, \u201cthe appropriate person\u201d is the registered person, an officer of HMCI, an officer of the local authority in whose area the home is located or a police officer.(4) The registered person must ensure that all employees undertake appropriate continuing professional development, receive practice-related supervision by a person with appropriate experience and have their performance and fitness to perform their roles appraised at least once every year.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3571"},{"id":"3583","label":"Children's homes - financial position","desc":"The registered provider must carry on the children\u2019s home in such manner as is likely to ensure that the home will be financially viable for the purpose of achieving the aims and objectives set out in the statement of purpose.(2) The registered person must\u2014(a)ensure that adequate financial records are maintained and kept up to date in respect of the home; and(b)supply a copy of the financial records and most recent accounts to HMCI at HMCI\u2019s request.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3583"},{"id":"3570","label":"Children's homes - fitness of workers","desc":"The registered person must recruit staff using recruitment procedures that are designed to ensure children\u2019s safety.The registered person may only employ an individual to work at the children\u2019s home or if an individual is employed by a person other than the registered person to work at the home in a position in which the individual may have regular contact with children, allow that individual to work at the home if the individual satisfies the requirements of these regulations.The registered person must take reasonable steps to ensure that any individual who is working at the home and who does not fall within the requirements of these regulations is appropriately supervised while carrying out the individual\u2019s duties.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3570"},{"id":"3577","label":"Children's homes - notice of absence","desc":"If the person who is in day-to-day charge of the children\u2019s home proposes to be absent from the home for a continuous period of 28 days or more, the registered person must give notice in writing to HMCI of the proposed absence and must comply with regulations regarding the timing and content of such notice.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3577"},{"id":"3578","label":"Children's homes - notice of changes","desc":"The registered person must give notice in writing to HMCI, as soon as it is reasonably practicable to do so, if any of the events described in these regulations take place or are expected by the registered person to take place.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3578"},{"id":"3585","label":"Children's homes - notification of a serious event","desc":"If a child dies, the registered person must without delay notify HMCI, the placing authority, the Secretary of State, the local authority in whose area the children\u2019s home is located, the clinical commissioning group for the area in which the home is located, if the child was accommodated in a secure children\u2019s home, the Prisons and Probation Ombudsman for England and Wales (\u201cthe PPO\u201d) and each other relevant person.If a child accommodated in a secure children\u2019s home dies, the registered person must allow the PPO to investigate the death.If there is a referral of a person working in the home pursuant to section 35 (Regulated activity providers: duty to refer) of the Safeguarding Vulnerable Groups Act 2006(1), the registered person must without delay notify HMCI, the placing authority and each other relevant person.The registered person must notify HMCI and each other relevant person without delay if:(a)a child is involved in or subject to, or is suspected of being involved in or subject to, sexual exploitation;(b)an incident requiring police involvement occurs in relation to a child which the registered person considers to be serious(c)there is an allegation of abuse against the home or a person working there;(d)a child protection enquiry involving a child is instigated or concludes (in which case, the notification must include the outcome of the child protection enquiry)(e)there is any other incident relating to a child which the registered person considers to be serious.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3585"},{"id":"3586","label":"Children's homes - notification of children admitted or discharged","desc":"The registered person must notify, without delay, the local authority for the area in which the children\u2019s home is located of every admission of a child into the home and every discharge of a child from the home.A notification under this regulation must be in writing and must include all information specified in these regulations.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3586"},{"id":"3587","label":"Children's homes - notification of offences","desc":"If the registered provider, the registered manager, the responsible individual (if one is nominated), if the registered provider is an organisation, any director of that organisation or if the registered provider is a partnership, any partner in that partnership. is convicted of a criminal offence, whether in England and Wales or elsewhere, that person must without delay give notice in writing to HMCI of:(a)the date and place of the conviction(b)the offence(c)the penalty imposed for the offence","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3587"},{"id":"3575","label":"Children's homes - other records","desc":"The registered person must maintain in the home the records in Schedule 4, ensure that the records are kept up to date and retain the records for at least 15 years from the date of the last entry.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3575"},{"id":"3572","label":"Children's homes - policies for the protection of children","desc":"The registered person must prepare and implement a policy which is intended to safeguard children accommodated in the children\u2019s home from abuse or neglect and sets out the procedure to be followed in the event of an allegation of abuse or neglect.The registered person must prepare and implement a policy for the prevention of bullying in the home, which must in particular set out the procedure for dealing with an allegation of bullying.The registered person must prepare and implement a policy (\u201cthe missing child policy\u201d) setting out the steps taken, and to be taken, to prevent children from being absent without permission and the procedures to be followed, and the roles and responsibilities of persons working at the home, in relation to a child who is, or has been, so absent.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3572"},{"id":"3567","label":"Children's homes - regard to statements of standards","desc":"A local authority in respect of a qualifying children\u2019s home, must comply with the following matters which relate to standards for a children\u2019s home:- Statement of purpose- Placement plan for looked after child- Placement plan for a child who is not looked after- Behaviour management and discipline- Restraint and deprivation of liberty- Privacy and access- Contact and access to communications- Medicines- Monitoring and surveillance- Fire precautions","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3567"},{"id":"3568","label":"Children's homes - registered persons","desc":"A local authority in respect of a qualifying children\u2019s home, must comply with the following matters which relate to registered persons:- Fitness of registered provider- Appointment of manager- Fitness of manager- Continuing professional development: registered person and responsible individual.- Compliance with regulations","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3568"},{"id":"3582","label":"Children's homes - review of premises","desc":"The registered person must review the appropriateness and suitability of the location of the premises used for the purposes of the children\u2019s home at least once in each calendar year taking into account the requirement in regulation 12(2)(c) (the protection of children standard).","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3582"},{"id":"3581","label":"Children's homes - review of quality of care","desc":"The registered person must complete a review of the quality of care provided for children (\u201ca quality of care review\u201d) at least once every 6 months in accordance with the requirements of these regulations. Following the review the registered person must produce a written report and must supply HMCI with a copy and make a copy of the quality of care review report available on request to a placing authority.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3581"},{"id":"3569","label":"Children's homes - staffing","desc":"The registered person must ensure that the employment of any person on a temporary basis at the children\u2019s home does not prevent children from receiving such continuity of care as is reasonable to meet their needs.(2) The registered person must ensure that\u2014(a)at all times, at least one person on duty at the home has a suitable first aid qualification;(b)any person who works as a nurse at the home is a registered nurse.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3569"},{"id":"3576","label":"Children's homes - storage of records","desc":"The registered person must ensure that the items specified in these regulations, which may be kept in electronic form, are kept in an accessible manner.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3576"},{"id":"3580","label":"Children's homes - visits and reports","desc":"The registered person must use reasonable endeavours to ensure that an independent person visits the children's home at least once each month.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3580"},{"id":"3588","label":"Children's services inspections - publication of report","desc":"A local authority in England which has received a copy of a report under section 137 of the Education and Inspections Act must, within 30 working days of receiving the report, publish it by:(a)sending a copy of the report to each of the authority\u2019s relevant partners under section 10 of the Children Act 2004(2), any person or body with whom the authority has made arrangements under section 10(1)(c) of the Children Act 2004, such of the authority\u2019s Board partners under section 13 of the Children Act 2004 as do not fall within the recipients already identified, at least one newspaper circulating in the area of that authority and at least one radio station serving that area(b)making a copy of the report available for inspection free of charge at the offices of the local authority(c)supplying a copy of the report to a member of the public on demand on payment of a reasonable fee.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3588"},{"id":"3589","label":"Children's services inspections - written statement","desc":"A local authority in England which has received a copy of a report under section 137 of the Act must, within 70 working days of receiving that report or as soon as is reasonably practicable, publish a written statement of action which they propose to take in the light of the report (a \u201cwritten statement\u201d) by:(a) sending a copy of the written statement to the Chief Inspector and the Secretary of State(b) sending a copy of the written statement to the persons or bodies to whom a copy of the report of the inspection was sent by virtue of regulation 2(a)(c) making a copy of the written statement available for inspection free of charge at the offices of the authority(d) supplying a copy of the written statement to a member of the public on demand on payment of a reasonable fee.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3589"},{"id":"55","label":"Children's social care - arrangements for discharge of care functions","desc":"A local authority may enter into an agreement with a body corporate to enable that body to exercise some of the Authority's care functions.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/55"},{"id":"56","label":"Children's social care - designated school staff member for looked after children","desc":"A Governing Body of a maintained school must designate a member of the staff at the school as having responsibility for promoting the educational achievement of registered pupils at the school who are being looked after by a local authority","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/56"},{"id":"180","label":"Christmas Day trading - enforcement of prohibition","desc":"A local authority shall be under a duty to enforce the prohibition of opening by large stores on Christmas Day and to appoint inspectors for this purpose.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/180"},{"id":"2338","label":"Civil aviation - provision of aerodromes and facilities at aerodromes","desc":"A local authority may do one or both of the following things, namely (a) with the consent of the Secretary of State and subject to such conditions as he may impose, establish and maintain aerodromes; (b) make arrangements with the person owning or managing an aerodrome in Great Britain whereby the local authority provide and maintain facilities for civil aviation at that aerodrome and may carry on ancillary business.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2338"},{"id":"215","label":"Civil partnership - civil partnership registrars","desc":"A civil partnership registrar is an individual who is designated by a registration authority as a civil partnership registrar for its area. It is the duty of each registration authority to ensure that there is a sufficient number of civil partnership registrars for its area to carry out in that area the functions of civil partnership registrars.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/215"},{"id":"214","label":"Civil partnership - issue of schedule","desc":"As soon as the waiting period in relation to each notice of proposed civil partnership has expired, the registration authority in whose area it is proposed that the registration take place is under a duty, at the request of one or both of the proposed civil partners, to issue a document to be known as a civil partnership schedule. The authority may refuse where it has reasonable grounds for suspecting that a relevant decision was made incorrectly because of the provision of false information or evidence.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/214"},{"id":"213","label":"Civil partnership - power to shorten waiting period","desc":"A local authority must comply with regulations relating to the Registrar General's power to shorten the waiting period.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/213"},{"id":"212","label":"Civil partnership - public display of information","desc":"A local authority must place the relevant information on public display for the prescribed period.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/212"},{"id":"210","label":"Civil partnership - publication of notice","desc":"A local authority must record the prescribed information from the notice of partnership on to the register.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/210"},{"id":"211","label":"Civil partnership - requirement for specified evidence","desc":"A local authority may require specified evidence before issuing a civil partnership schedule.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/211"},{"id":"757","label":"Clean air - adaptation of fireplaces in private dwellings","desc":"A local authority may, in relation to a smoke control area, serve a notice requiring the adaption of a fireplace in a private dwelling and may give grants in certain circumstances.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/757"},{"id":"770","label":"Clean air - authority defaulting on functions","desc":"A local authority must comply with directions from the Secretary of State when exercising his default powers under the Act.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/770"},{"id":"755","label":"Clean air - directed smoke control areas","desc":"A local authority must comply with any direction from the secretary of state to make an area a smoke control area.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/755"},{"id":"753","label":"Clean air - discretionary smoke control areas","desc":"A local authority may by order declare the whole or part of its area to be a smoke control area.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/753"},{"id":"747","label":"Clean air - exemption from requirements regarding grit and dust emissions from a furnace","desc":"A local authority may relax the application of section 6(1) relating to the emission of grit and dust from furnaces in certain circumstances.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/747"},{"id":"756","label":"Clean air - exemptions relating to prohibition of smoke emission in particular areas","desc":"A local authority must comply with any direction from the secretary of state that the prohibition under section 20 with regard to smoke control areas should be suspended or relaxed.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/756"},{"id":"766","label":"Clean air - general provisions as to enforcement","desc":"A local authority must enforce certain provisions of the Act.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/766"},{"id":"758","label":"Clean air - grants for adaptation of fireplaces","desc":"A local authority may, give a grant towards adaptations to fireplaces in churches, chapels and buildings used by charities.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/758"},{"id":"752","label":"Clean air - height of chimneys","desc":"A local authority must consider granting approval to the height of chimneys in certain circumstances and must give written reasons where that approval is denied.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/752"},{"id":"751","label":"Clean air - information about furnaces and fuel consumed","desc":"A local authority may request information about the furnace and the type of fuel burned for certain purposes.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/751"},{"id":"767","label":"Clean air - institution of proceedings","desc":"A local authority may bring proceedings under certain provisions of the Act.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/767"},{"id":"771","label":"Clean air - joint exercise of local authority functions","desc":"Two or more local authorities may act jointly for certain purposes under the Act.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/771"},{"id":"750","label":"Clean air - measurement of grit, dust and fumes by local authorities","desc":"A local authority must, in certain circumstances, take measurements of grit, dust and fumes emanating from a furnace.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/750"},{"id":"769","label":"Clean air - notice to require information","desc":"A local authority may serve a notice to require information in relation to certain of its functions under the Act.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/769"},{"id":"749","label":"Clean air - notification of decision on application for arrestment plant","desc":"A local authority must, when determining an application under sections 6 or 8 of the Act, give a reasoned, written decision.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/749"},{"id":"765","label":"Clean air - notification of offences","desc":"A local authority must notify occupiers of certain premises of offences relating to emissions of smoke in certain circumstances.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/765"},{"id":"748","label":"Clean air - requirement to fit arrestment plant for burning solid fuel","desc":"A local authority must consider requests for approval of an arrestment plant where a domestic furnace is used in a building to burn pulverised fuel or to burn, at a rate of 1.02 tonnes an hour or more, solid fuel in any other form or solid waste,","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/748"},{"id":"768","label":"Clean air - rights of entry and inspection","desc":"An officer authorised by a local authority has the powers of entry and inspection for certain purposes under the Act.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/768"},{"id":"754","label":"Clean air - smoke control orders","desc":"A local authority may issue smoke control orders in a smoke control area.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/754"},{"id":"59","label":"Climate change - single use carrier bags","desc":"A local authority must administer the Single Use of Carrier Bags Regulations.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/59"},{"id":"57","label":"Climate change report in England","desc":"An authority is required to prepare a report on the current and predicted impact of climate change in relation to the authority's functions when and how directed by the Secretary of State. The report may include proposals and policies for adapting to climate change, time-scales for introducing those proposals and policies and an assessment of the progress made by the authority towards implementing the policies and proposals set out in previous reports.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/57"},{"id":"58","label":"Climate change report in Wales","desc":"A local authority must prepare report on climate change in relation to the delegated functions of Welsh ministers when and in the manner directed by the Welsh Ministers.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/58"},{"id":"93","label":"Coastal defence - delegation of coastal erosion risk management function","desc":"A coast protection authority may, with the appropriate consent, arrange for a person to exercise a coastal erosion risk management function on its behalf.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/93"},{"id":"94","label":"Coastal erosion - risk management function exercised on behalf of Environment Agency","desc":"A local authority may undertake coastal erosion risk management function on behalf of the Environment Agency if delegation is agreed.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/94"},{"id":"1666","label":"Coastal protection - application to Minister for authority to do work","desc":"A local authority may apply to the Minister to facilitate coastal protection work.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/1666"},{"id":"1656","label":"Coastal protection - charges","desc":"A local authority may levy and recover charges for coastal protection work in certain circumstances.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/1656"},{"id":"1660","label":"Coastal protection - compensation for depreciation in value of land","desc":"A local authority must pay compensation in certain circumstances where the value of a person's interest in land has depreciated or that any person has suffered damage by being disturbed in his enjoyment of land, in consequence of the carrying out of coast protection work by the authority.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1660"},{"id":"1657","label":"Coastal protection - compulsory acquisition of land","desc":"A local authority may compulsorily acquire land if authorised by the appropriate national authority to do so.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/1657"},{"id":"1667","label":"Coastal protection - default powers of Minister","desc":"A local authority must comply with an order form the Minister utilising his default powers where they have failed to take sufficient measures for the protection of any land in their area.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1667"},{"id":"1653","label":"Coastal protection - erosion work","desc":"A local authority may carry out coastal protection erosion work in certain circumstances and having taken certain prescribed steps.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/1653"},{"id":"1655","label":"Coastal protection - implementation of schemes of works","desc":"Where a works scheme prepared by an authority is confirmed by the Minister the authority shall have power to take all necessary steps for carrying out the work provided for by the scheme subject to any provisions in regulations.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/1655"},{"id":"1661","label":"Coastal protection - incidental purposes land","desc":"A local authority may treat land acquired for the purposes of coastal protection.as incidental purposes land under the Local Government Act 1972","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/1661"},{"id":"1664","label":"Coastal protection - information on ownership of land","desc":"A local authority may require information regarding ownership of land for purposes connected with coastal protection.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/1664"},{"id":"1663","label":"Coastal protection - powers of entry and inspection","desc":"A person duly authorised by a local authority may enter land for certain purposes connected with coastal protection.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/1663"},{"id":"1654","label":"Coastal protection - preparation of schemes of works","desc":"A local authority must prepare schemes of work to carry out certain works providing for coast protection in certain circumstances which must be approved by the appropriate authority. The authority must take account of legislation when completing the scheme of works.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1654"},{"id":"1659","label":"Coastal protection - prohibition of excavation on or under the seashore","desc":"A local authority may make an order (which they must enforce) prohibiting the excavation of materials on or under the seashore in certain areas and may issue licences allowing such works in such areas.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/1659"},{"id":"1665","label":"Coastal protection - right of passage","desc":"A local authority may require the right of passage over land by agreement or by compulsion for the purposes of coastal protection work.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/1665"},{"id":"1662","label":"Coastal protection - sale of severed materials","desc":"A local authority may sell unclaimed materials which they have severed from the land as part of coastal protection work.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/1662"},{"id":"1658","label":"Coastal protection - unauthorised works","desc":"A local authority may by notice demand the removal or re-instatement of unauthorised coast protectionworks, carry out that work themselves in certain circumstances and prosecute an offence.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/1658"},{"id":"3919","label":"Combined authorities - alternative mayoral title for existing combined authority","desc":"A mayoral authority may by resolution in accordance with this sectionchange the title by which the mayor for the area of the authority is to be known to an approved alternative title allowed for by this section.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/3919"},{"id":"3918","label":"Combined authorities - alternative mayoral titles","desc":"At the first meeting of the authority after the order made under section 107A comes into force, the authority must, by a resolution in accordance with this section\u2014(a) provide that the mayor for the area of the authority is to be known by the title of mayor, or(b) change the title by which the mayor for the area of the authority is to be known to an alternative title allowed by this section.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3918"},{"id":"3910","label":"Combined authorities - associate members","desc":"A combined authority may appoint an individual to be a member (\"an associate member\") of the combined authority.The associate members of a combined authority are to be non-voting members of the authority.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/3910"},{"id":"3016","label":"Combined authorities - deputy Mayor","desc":"The Mayor of a combined local authority must appoint a deputy mayor","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3016"},{"id":"3908","label":"Combined authorities - designation of key route network roads","desc":"A combined authority may designate a highway or proposed highway in its area as a key route network road, or remove its designation as a key route network road, with the consent of\u2014(a) each constituent council in whose area the highway or proposed highway is, and(b) in the case of a mayoral combined authority, the mayor.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/3908"},{"id":"3018","label":"Combined authorities - functions","desc":"A combined local authority must comply with an order of the Secretary of State regarding the local authority functions that it must carry out.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3018"},{"id":"3017","label":"Combined authorities - functions of a Mayor","desc":"The Mayor of a combined local authority must carry out the functions set out in the Secretary of States Order.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3017"},{"id":"3012","label":"Combined authorities - Mayor","desc":"A combined local authority must comply with an Order of the Secretary of State regarding combined authorities having a mayor for the combined area.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3012"},{"id":"3909","label":"Combined authorities - non-constituent members","desc":"A combined authority may designate a body other than a constituent council as a nominating body for the purposes of this Part. A body may be designated only if the body consents to the designation.A nominating body of a combined authority may nominate a representative of the body for appointment by the authority as a member (a \"non-constituent member\").","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/3909"},{"id":"3907","label":"Combined authorities - proposed boundary changes","desc":"A combined authority must undertake statutory consultation in certain circumstances when boundary changes are proposed by the Secretary of State.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3907"},{"id":"3906","label":"Combined authorities - review of constitutional arrangements","desc":"In accordance with the requirements of this section an appropriate person may carry out a review of the combined authority's constitutional provision if\u2014(a) an appropriate person proposes a review, and(b) the combined authority consents to the review.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/3906"},{"id":"3917","label":"Combined authority - changes to existing authority","desc":"One or more authorities may, in accordance with the requirements of the legislation and Regulations published by the Secretary of State(a) prepare a proposal for the making of an order under sections 104 to 107F in relation to an existing combined authority, and(b) submit the proposal to the Secretary of State.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/3917"},{"id":"3916","label":"Combined authority - proposal for new authority","desc":"Any one or more authorities may, in accordance with the requirements of the legislation and Regulations published by the Secretary of State(a) prepare a proposal for the establishment of a combined authority for an area, and(b) submit the proposal to the Secretary of State.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/3916"},{"id":"3888","label":"Combined County Authorities - additional financial matters relating to the Mayor","desc":"A Combined County Authority may exercise powers set down in Regulations relating to financial matters concerning the Mayor.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/3888"},{"id":"3883","label":"Combined County Authorities - additional functions of Mayor","desc":"A Combined County Authority may exercise powers in relation to the functions of the Mayor and Deputy Mayor as set out in Regulations or in section 30 to 32 of the Act.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/3883"},{"id":"3879","label":"Combined County Authorities - changes to area","desc":"A local authority must comply with Regulations when changing the area of a CCA, or when dissolving or abolishing the Combined County Authority.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3879"},{"id":"3889","label":"Combined County Authorities - choosing mayoral title","desc":"A Combined County Authority who has elected a Mayor must by resolution at the first meeting of the mayoral CCA select a mayoral title either of 'Mayor' or from the options specified in legislation.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3889"},{"id":"3871","label":"Combined County Authorities - constitutional arrangements","desc":"A local authority must comply with Regulations making provision about the constitutional arrangements of a Combined County Authority.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3871"},{"id":"3885","label":"Combined County Authorities - exercise of or delegation of Fire and Rescue functions","desc":"The Secretary of State may by Regulations require the mayor for the area of a Combined County Authority to exercise fire and rescue functions in relation to that area and/or to delegate them to the Chief Constable or Police for that area.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3885"},{"id":"3887","label":"Combined County Authorities - financial matters relating to the Mayor","desc":"A Combined County Authority must comply with duties set down in the Act or determined by the Secretary of State in regulations relating to financial matters concerning the Mayor.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3887"},{"id":"3874","label":"Combined County Authorities - functions","desc":"A Combined County Authority must comply with Regulations regarding its functions. This may include sharing functions with other local authorities or public bodies.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3874"},{"id":"3882","label":"Combined County Authorities - functions of Mayor and Deputy Mayor","desc":"A Combined County Authority must comply with Regulations in relation to the functions of the Mayor and Deputy Mayor as set out in Regulations or in section 30 of the Act.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3882"},{"id":"3872","label":"Combined County Authorities - funding","desc":"A local authority must comply with Regulations making provision about the funding of a Combined County Authority.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3872"},{"id":"3893","label":"Combined County Authorities - general powers","desc":"A Combined County Authority may (subject to the restrictions in section 50 and any Regulations made pursuant to section 51) do\u2014(a) anything it considers appropriate for the purposes of the carrying-out of any of its functions (its \"functional purposes\"),(b) anything it considers appropriate for purposes incidental to its functional purposes,(c) anything it considers appropriate for purposes indirectly incidental to its functional purposes through any number of removes,(d) anything it considers to be connected with\u2014(i) any of its functions, or(ii) anything it may do under paragraph (a), (b) or (c), and(e) for a commercial purpose anything which it may do under any of paragraphs (a) to (d) otherwise than for a commercial purpose.Where subsection the above confers power on a CCA to do something, it confers power (subject to section 50) to do it anywhere in the United Kingdom or elsewhere.Power conferred on a CCA by the above is in addition to, and is not limited by, its other powers.This section does not apply in relation to a CCA in respect of which regulations under section 52(1) have effect.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/3893"},{"id":"3876","label":"Combined County Authorities - highways and traffic functions","desc":"A Combined County Authority may give directions to highway authorities if authorised to do so by Regulations","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/3876"},{"id":"3878","label":"Combined County Authorities - key route network roads","desc":"A Combined County Authority may designate or change the designation of key route networks, subject to obtaining the necessary consents or may request the Secretary of State to do so.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/3878"},{"id":"3875","label":"Combined County Authorities - management of passenger transport","desc":"A Combined County Authority must comply with Regulations regarding the functions of an Integrated Transport Authority and Passenger Transport Executive.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3875"},{"id":"3884","label":"Combined County Authorities - Mayor to be Police and Crime Commissioner","desc":"Where required by regulations, the mayor for the area of a Combined County Authority must exercise functions of a police and crime commissioner in relation to that area.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3884"},{"id":"3891","label":"Combined County authorities - proposals for new authorities","desc":"A local authority may prepare a proposal (which must comply with any Regulations) for the establishment of a Combined County Authority for an area, and submit the proposal to the Secretary of State.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/3891"},{"id":"3886","label":"Combined County Authorities - request to Secretary of State regarding Fire and Rescue functions","desc":"Where authorised by regulations under Section 30 to make that request the Mayor may request the Secretary of State to require the mayor for the area of a Combined County Authority to exercise fire and rescue functions in relation to that area and/or to delegate them to the Chief Constable or Police for that area.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/3886"},{"id":"3895","label":"Combined County Authorities - Secretary of State\u2019s guidance","desc":"A local authority must comply with Guidance published by the Secretary of State when considering matters relating to Combined County Authorities.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3895"},{"id":"3894","label":"Combined County Authorities - transfer of property, rights and liabilities","desc":"A local authority must comply with Regulations relating to the transfer of property, rights and liabilities (including employment rights) relating to the formation, alteration or abolition of a Combined County Authority.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3894"},{"id":"3877","label":"Combined County Authorities \u2013 carrying out highways and traffic functions","desc":"A Combined County Authority may directly carry out directions to highway authorities given under section 21 if the highway authority fails to follow those directions and may recover its reasonable expenses in doing so.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/3877"},{"id":"3873","label":"Combined County Authorities \u2013 change of name","desc":"A Combined County Authority may change its name in accordance with the requirements of section 17.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/3873"},{"id":"3881","label":"Combined County Authorities \u2013 election of Deputy Mayor","desc":"A Combined County Authority who has elected a Mayor must elect a Deputy Mayor and comply with the provisions of section 29 regarding that position.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3881"},{"id":"3880","label":"Combined County Authorities \u2013 election of Mayor","desc":"A Combined County Authority may elect a Mayor if given the power to do so by Regulations.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/3880"},{"id":"3890","label":"Combined County Authorities \u2013 further changes to mayoral title","desc":"A Combined County Authority who has elected a Mayor and assigned a mayoral title may change that title by resolution in accordance with the requirements of section 43.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/3890"},{"id":"3892","label":"Combined County Authority - changes to existing arrangements","desc":"A local authority may prepare a proposal (which must comply with any Regulations and section 47) for changes to existing arrangements of a Combined County Authority, and submit the proposal to the Secretary of State.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/3892"},{"id":"1216","label":"Commercial waste - receptacles for collection","desc":"A local authority may, in certain circumstances, provide and charge for the provision of receptacles for commercial or industrial waste make provision by notice as to the type of receptacles to be used for the collection of that waste.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/1216"},{"id":"236","label":"Common land - amendments to register","desc":"A commons registration authority may amend the register of common land in certain circumstances.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/236"},{"id":"238","label":"Common land - charge for inspection of register","desc":"A commons registration authority may charge for supplying a copy of the document forming part of the commons register.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/238"},{"id":"237","label":"Common land - deregistration and exchange","desc":"A commons registration authority must amend the register of common land when ordered to do so by the national authority or by the High Court.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/237"},{"id":"239","label":"Common land - inspection and copies of register","desc":"A Commons Registration Authority must make the commons register available for inspection and to allow copies of documents to be taken","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/239"},{"id":"1570","label":"Common land - public access","desc":"A local authority may act in the interests of those wishing to access common land for open air recreation including the erection of buildings and the acquisition of land.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/1570"},{"id":"235","label":"Common land - register","desc":"A commons registration authority must keep a register of common land and a register of town or village greens in accordance with the regulations.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/235"},{"id":"240","label":"Common land - unclaimed land","desc":"A local authority may take any steps to protect the land against unlawful interference that could be taken by an owner in possession of the land; and institute proceedings against any person for any offence committed in respect of the land.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/240"},{"id":"1855","label":"Commons - acquisition of property","desc":"A local authority may acquire property in a regulated common.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/1855"},{"id":"1856","label":"Commons - amendment or revocation of scheme","desc":"A local authority may amend or revoke a scheme for the regulation and management of a common.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/1856"},{"id":"1857","label":"Commons - byelaws relating to management scheme","desc":"A local authority may make byelaws relating to a scheme for the regulation and management of a common.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/1857"},{"id":"1858","label":"Commons - contributions to expense of management scheme","desc":"A local authority may contribute towards the expenses of another local authority in relation to the making of a scheme.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/1858"},{"id":"1861","label":"Commons - general powers","desc":"A local authority being a London Borough Council shall have the same powers with respect to commons as a district council under the Commons Act 1876.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/1861"},{"id":"1854","label":"Commons - provision for compensation","desc":"A local authority must pay compensation in connection with a scheme of regulation in certain circumstances.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1854"},{"id":"1859","label":"Commons - rights of common and rights of way","desc":"A local authority being a district council may with the consent of the county council for the county within which any common land is situate aid persons in maintaining rights of common where, in the opinion of the council, the extinction of such rights would be prejudicial to the inhabitants of the district and may, for the purpose of carrying into effect this section, institute or defend any legal proceedings, and generally take such steps as they deem expedient","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/1859"},{"id":"1853","label":"Commons - scheme of regulation","desc":"A local authority may make a scheme of regulation for the commons within their area in accordance with the prescribed procedure.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/1853"},{"id":"1568","label":"Commons registration - town and village greens","desc":"A local authority shall maintain a register of town and village greens and the ownership of rights over them.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1568"},{"id":"1774","label":"Communications/TV equipment - byelaws","desc":"A local authority may make byelaws about communications or TV equipment for the prevention of danger or obstruction to persons using any street or public place.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/1774"},{"id":"2501","label":"Communities - proposal for sustainable communities","desc":"A local authority may respond to an invitation from the Secretary of State to produce a proposal for sustainable local communities.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2501"},{"id":"3186","label":"Community assets - list of assets","desc":"The local authority must publish and allow inspections of lists of assets of community value also assets unsuccessfully nominated for inclusion on such lists.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3186"},{"id":"3187","label":"Community assets - sale or transfer","desc":"The local authority must edit list of assets of community value to show notification of intended sale and publicise that intended sale and to notify owner of community interest group bidder and to pay compensation in certain circumstances.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3187"},{"id":"1299","label":"Community care - assessment and provision","desc":"A local authority must, in the manner prescribed, carry out an assessment of needs, provide information and where necessary make provision for community care services.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1299"},{"id":"2586","label":"Community care - direct payments","desc":"A local authority must, in prescribed circumstances, or may, make direct payments to persons who have, or lack, the capacity to consent to the making of a direct payment where their needs are met by such a payment and what amount (if any) it is reasonably practicable to pay towards securing the provision of the relevant service (either reimbursement or by contribution). A local authority must or may impose conditions in respect of direct payments to persons with the capacity to consent and to persons lacking capacity respectively. An authority may require a direct payment to be repaid if it has not been used to secure the provision of service to which it relates. A local authority must review and must or may stop the making of direct payments in certain prescribed circumstances.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2586"},{"id":"461","label":"Community care - liability to make delayed discharge payments","desc":"A local authority must make prescribed payments to the NHS for a delayed discharge because arrangements are not in place for agreed community care services.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/461"},{"id":"460","label":"Community care - needs assessment","desc":"A local authority may carry out the determination of a patients need for community care services in certain circumstance.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/460"},{"id":"1298","label":"Community care - plans for community care services","desc":"A local authority must prepare, publish and keep under review plans for community care services.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1298"},{"id":"1300","label":"Community care - transfer of staff from health services","desc":"A local authority must comply with regulations regarding the transfer of staff from NHS employment to employment by the local authority.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1300"},{"id":"3591","label":"Community centres - temporary restrictions","desc":"A person who is responsible for a community centre must ensure that, during the emergency period, the community centre is closed except where it is used to provide: (a) essential voluntary activities or urgent public support services (including the provision of food banks or other support for the homeless or vulnerable people, blood donation sessions or support in an emergency) orfor early years childcare provided by a person registered on the Early Years Register under Part 3 of the Childcare Act 2006.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3591"},{"id":"3652","label":"Community Infrastructure Levy - charging","desc":"The local planning authority can charge the Community Infrastructure Levy on developments which create new or additional internal area and meet the criteria specified in Regulations.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/3652"},{"id":"3653","label":"Community Infrastructure Levy - consultation","desc":"A local authority must consult on plans to implement a Community Infrastructure Levy, and a charging schedule which sets out its levy rates. The schedule once approved must be published on its website.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3653"},{"id":"3654","label":"Community Infrastructure Levy - deferral of payments","desc":"Where a Community Infrastruture Levy payment is due to be paid by a person with an annual turnover not exceeding \u00a345,000,000 and who is experiencing financial difficulties due to the effects of Coronavirus the authority has a duty to consider a deferral of the payment and may issue a revised demand notice.Where a deferral request is being considered no surcharge or interest on the payment may be imposed.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3654"},{"id":"2422","label":"Community protection notices - fixed penalty notice","desc":"A person authorised by a local authority may issue a fixed penalty notice to anyone who that person has reason to believe has committed an offence under section 48 of the Act","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2422"},{"id":"2423","label":"Community protection notices - guidance","desc":"A local authority must have regard to any guidance issued by the Secretary of State with regard to the exercise of its functions under the Act.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2423"},{"id":"2418","label":"Community protection notices - issuing","desc":"A person duly authorised by a local authority may (subject to the requirements of section 43) issue a community protection notice to an individual aged 16 or over, or a body, if satisfied on reasonable grounds that\u2014 the conduct of the individual or body is having a detrimental effect, of a persistent or continuing nature, on the quality of life of those in the locality, andthe conduct is unreasonable","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2418"},{"id":"2419","label":"Community protection notices - powers of entry","desc":"Where the identity of the owner or occupier of a premises is unobtainable a person duly authorised by a local authority may The authorised person may\u2014 post the community protection notice on the premises;and enter the premises, or other premises, to the extent reasonably necessary for that purpose.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2419"},{"id":"2421","label":"Community protection notices - powers of seizure","desc":"Where authorised to do so by a warrant from a JP the person authorised by the relevant local authority may enter the premises within 14 days from the date of issue of the warrant to seize the item in question.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2421"},{"id":"2420","label":"Community protection notices - powers on default","desc":"Where a person issued with a community protection notice (\u201cthe defaulter\u201d) fails to comply with a requirement of the notice, the relevant local authority may have work carried out to ensure that the failure is remedied, but only on land that is open to the air and/or) as regards premises other than land open to the air, if the relevant local authority issues the defaulter with a notice\u2014specifying work it intends to have carried out to ensure that the failure is remedied,specifying the estimated cost of the work (for which the defaulter becomes liable), andinviting the defaulter to consent to the work being carried out,the local authority may have the work carried out if the necessary consent is given.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2420"},{"id":"1485","label":"Compulsory acquisition of rights over land","desc":"A local authority may be authorised by the Crown to compulsorily purchase rights over land by means of a compulsory purchase order.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/1485"},{"id":"2072","label":"Compulsory purchase - acquisition by agreement","desc":"A local authority may enter into an agreement for the compulsory purchase of land.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2072"},{"id":"3239","label":"Compulsory purchase - acquisition of land","desc":"The acquiring authority must comply with the confirmation procedure.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3239"},{"id":"3899","label":"Compulsory purchase - common standards for data","desc":"A local authority must comply with regulations, making provision requiring an acquiring authority, in preparing, holding or providing such of its relevant compulsory purchase data as is specified or described in the regulations, to comply with any approved data standards which are applicable.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3899"},{"id":"3902","label":"Compulsory purchase - compensation","desc":"The acquiring authority may include in the order a direction that compensation is to be assessed in accordance with section 14A of the Land Compensation Act 1961.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/3902"},{"id":"2077","label":"Compulsory purchase - compensation for injurious affection","desc":"A local authority must comply with an order to pay compensation for injurious affection in certain circumstances.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2077"},{"id":"2081","label":"Compulsory purchase - cost of conveyances","desc":"A local authority must pay for the cost of all conveyances of the land subject to compulsory purchase.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2081"},{"id":"2082","label":"Compulsory purchase - deed poll","desc":"Any deed poll made by a local authority under the Act must comply with the provisions of section 28.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2082"},{"id":"2076","label":"Compulsory purchase - deposit of compensation and deed poll on refusal to convey","desc":"A local authority may in the case of a refusal to sell land pay a deposit of compensation into court and execute a deed poll.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2076"},{"id":"2075","label":"Compulsory purchase - divided land","desc":"A local authority may be required to purchase divided land in certain circumstances.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2075"},{"id":"2078","label":"Compulsory purchase - entry of land","desc":"A local authority may, having served notice, enter land for certain purposes connected with the Act.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2078"},{"id":"3901","label":"Compulsory purchase - extended time for completion","desc":"A local authority may extend time limits for implementation of compulsory purchase orders in certain circumstances.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/3901"},{"id":"1486","label":"Compulsory purchase - injurious affection","desc":"A local authority must take certain steps after passing a resolution relating to land to which this section applies.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1486"},{"id":"2080","label":"Compulsory purchase - interests omitted from purchase","desc":"A local authority must pay compensation for interests omitted from purchase in certain circumstances.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2080"},{"id":"2079","label":"Compulsory purchase - mortgages","desc":"A local authority may purchase or redeem the interest of the mortgagee or acquire land subject to a mortgage or rent charges in certain circumstances.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2079"},{"id":"2074","label":"Compulsory purchase - notice to treat","desc":"A local authority proposing to compulsorily acquire land must issue and serve a notice to treat.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2074"},{"id":"1488","label":"Compulsory purchase - particulars of person with an interest in land","desc":"A local authority may obtain the particulars of a person with an interest in land in connection with compulsory purchase. Note - a person who\u2014(a) fails to comply with the requirements of a notice served on him in pursuance of the preceding subsection; or(b) in furnishing any information in compliance with such a notice makes a statement which he knows to be false in a material particular or recklessly makes a statement which is false in a material particular, shall be guilty of an offence and liable on summary conviction to a fine not exceeding level 5 on the standard scale.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/1488"},{"id":"3905","label":"Compulsory purchase - postponement of vesting date","desc":"A local authority, in relation to compulsory purchase, may in certain circumstances agree with the owner of an interest to postpone the vesting date.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/3905"},{"id":"2083","label":"Compulsory purchase - refusal to agree rent charge compensation","desc":"A local authority may in the case of a refusal to agree rent charge compensation pay a deposit of compensation into court and execute a deed poll.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2083"},{"id":"1494","label":"Compulsory purchase - repayment of unclaimed compensation","desc":"A local authority may recover unclaimed compensation paid into court in respect of land clauses and compulsory purchase in certain circumstances.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/1494"},{"id":"1487","label":"Compulsory purchase - survey of land","desc":"A person authorised in writing in that behalf by a local authority may at any reasonable time survey any land in connection with a proposal by the authority to acquire compulsorily an interest in the land or a right over the land which is not such an interest; and for the purpose of surveying any land in pursuance of the preceding paragraph, enter on the land and other land.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/1487"},{"id":"2073","label":"Compulsory purchase - time limit","desc":"A notice to treat may not be served by the acquiring local authority after the end of the period of 3 years beginning with the day on which the compulsory purchase order becomes operative.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2073"},{"id":"2539","label":"Conservation - habitats and species","desc":"Local authorities must exercise their nature conservation functions so as to comply with the Habitats Directive and consider the effect on a European site before the granting consents or authorisations including the grant of planning permission and subject to specified exceptions (considerations of overriding public interest), may not authorise a plan or project that may adversely affect the integrity of a European site.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2539"},{"id":"2656","label":"Construction products - enforcement","desc":"Local authorities (local weights and measures authorities) must carry out market surveillance duties under the 2008 Regulation as it applies to construction products; enforce the 2011 Regulations and enforce using prescribed powers the provisions of Part 2 in their areas and may investigate and prosecute in relation to offences anywhere in England and Wales. They must give notice of any suspension notices and forfeiture applications to the Secretary of State.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2656"},{"id":"694","label":"Consultation - local polls","desc":"A local authority may conduct a local poll in relation to its services and its expenditure on the same.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/694"},{"id":"3277","label":"Consumer contracts - regulation and enforcement","desc":"The local authority has a duty to ensure compliance with and to enforce regulations regarding the provision of information, cancellation and additional charges in relation to consumer contracts.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3277"},{"id":"2086","label":"Consumer credit - compensation for loss","desc":"Where, in exercising his powers an officer of an enforcement authority seizes and detains goods and their owner suffers loss by reason of that seizure, or the loss, damage or deterioration of the goods during detention,then, unless the owner is convicted of an offence under this Act committed in relation to the goods, the authority shall compensate him for the loss so suffered.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2086"},{"id":"2084","label":"Consumer credit - enforcement","desc":"A local authority must enforce the Consumer Credit Act 1974.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2084"},{"id":"2085","label":"Consumer credit - entry and inspection","desc":"A duly authorised officer of a local authority may enter and inspect premises and seize and detain goods for the purposes of enforcing the Act.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2085"},{"id":"2087","label":"Consumer credit - test purchases","desc":"A local authority may make test purchases for the purposes of enforcing the Act.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2087"},{"id":"3258","label":"Consumer protection - aerosol manufacture and sale","desc":"The local authority has the power to initiate criminal proceedings where an aerosol dispenser is found not to comply with these regulations","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/3258"},{"id":"3415","label":"Consumer protection - bus and coach transport","desc":"The local authority has a duty to ensure compliance with and to enforce regulations relating to the rights of passengers in bus and coach transport.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3415"},{"id":"2927","label":"Consumer protection - compensation for seizure and detention","desc":"A local authority must pay compensation where it has exercised its powers of seizure and detention in certain circumstances.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2927"},{"id":"3328","label":"Consumer protection - consumer credit enforcement","desc":"The local authority has a duty to ensure compliance and enforce the Order relating to consumer credit.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3328"},{"id":"3329","label":"Consumer protection - consumer credit proceedings","desc":"The local authority may institute proceedings in England and Wales for a relevant offence under the Financial Services Act 2012 (Consumer Credit) Order 2013","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/3329"},{"id":"3327","label":"Consumer protection - distance marketing of financial services","desc":"The local authority has a duty to ensure compliance and enforce the Regulations relating to distance marketing of financial services.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3327"},{"id":"3280","label":"Consumer protection - distance selling advice","desc":"The local authority has the power to give advice concerning the operation of the distance selling regulations.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/3280"},{"id":"3278","label":"Consumer protection - distance selling enforcement","desc":"The local weights and measures authority has a duty to enforce regulations regarding the distance selling of goods and services.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3278"},{"id":"1959","label":"Consumer protection - enforcement of safety provisions","desc":"It shall be the duty of every weights and measures authority in Great Britain to enforce within their area the safety provisions.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1959"},{"id":"3369","label":"Consumer protection - motor fuel composition and content","desc":"The local authority has a duty to ensure compliance with and to enforce regulations relating to motor fuel composition and content.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3369"},{"id":"3385","label":"Consumer protection - package travel and linked travel arrangements","desc":"The local authority has a duty to ensure compliance with and to enforce regulations relating to package travel and linked travel arrangements","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3385"},{"id":"3386","label":"Consumer protection - passenger car fuel consumption and CO2 emissions","desc":"The local authority has a duty to ensure compliance with and to enforce regulations relating to information provided about fuel consumption and CO2 emissions for passenger cars.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3386"},{"id":"3388","label":"Consumer protection - personal protective equipment","desc":"The local authority has a duty to ensure compliance with and to enforce regulations relating to the sale and marketing of personal protective equipment (PPE).","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3388"},{"id":"3397","label":"Consumer protection - price indications (bureaux de change)","desc":"A local authority may institute proceedings where anyone who operates a bureau de change fails to comply with regulations relating to exchange rate information and price indications.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/3397"},{"id":"3398","label":"Consumer protection - pricing of products and services","desc":"The local authority has a duty to ensure compliance with and to enforce regulations relating to the pricing of products and services.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3398"},{"id":"3410","label":"Consumer protection - radio equipment","desc":"The local authority has a duty to ensure compliance with and to enforce regulations relating to the design and manufacture of radio equipment.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3410"},{"id":"2926","label":"Consumer protection -
