recalculation, withholding or repayment","desc":"A local authority must recalculate, withhold or demand repayment of the grant in certain circumstances as detailed in the legislation.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/991"},{"id":"994","label":"Housing grants - recovery of Secretary of State's contributions","desc":"A local authority must repay funds to the Secretary of State in certain circumstances.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/994"},{"id":"989","label":"Housing grants - repayment of grant","desc":"A local authority may demand that an applicant must repay a grant or part of a grant plus interest in certain circumstances.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/989"},{"id":"980","label":"Housing grants - restrictions where work already begun","desc":"A local authority may approve a grant where work has already begun in certain circumstances.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/980"},{"id":"1379","label":"Housing or council tax benefit - sharing of information","desc":"A local authority must comply with regulations relating to the sharing of information relating to housing or council tax benefit.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1379"},{"id":"2034","label":"Housing renewal areas - declaration of renewal area","desc":"Where a local housing authority are satisfied that the living conditions in an area within their district consisting primarily of housing accommodation are unsatisfactory, and that those conditions can most effectively be dealt with by declaring the area to be a renewal area, then, subject to provisions, they may cause the area to be defined on a map and by resolution declare it to be a renewal area","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2034"},{"id":"2036","label":"Housing renewal areas - duty to publish information","desc":"Where a local housing authority have declared an area to be a renewal area, they shall from time to time publish, in such manner as appears to them best designed to secure that the information is brought to the attention of persons residing or owning property in the area, information with respect to the action they propose to take in relation to the area, the action they have taken in relation to the area, and the assistance available for the carrying out of works in the area","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2036"},{"id":"2039","label":"Housing renewal areas - exclusion of land from, or termination of, renewal area","desc":"A local housing authority may by resolution exclude land from a renewal area; or declare that an area shall cease to be a renewal area","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2039"},{"id":"2037","label":"Housing renewal areas - general powers of local housing authority","desc":"Where a local housing authority have declared an area to be a renewal area, the authority may acquire by agreement, or be authorised by the Secretary of State to acquire compulsorily, any land in the area on which there are premises consisting of or including housing accommodation or which forms part of the curtilage of any such premises; and the authority may provide housing accommodation on land acquired under this provision.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2037"},{"id":"2038","label":"Housing renewal areas - orders extinguishing right to use vehicles on highway","desc":"A local housing authority who have declared a renewal area may exercise the powers of a local planning authority (extinguishment of right to use vehicles on certain highways) with respect to a highway in that area notwithstanding that they are not the local planning authority subject to certain provisions.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2038"},{"id":"2040","label":"Housing renewal areas - powers of entry and penalty for obstruction","desc":"A person authorised by the local housing authority may at any reasonable time, on giving not less than seven days' notice of his intention to the occupier, and to the owner if the owner is known, enter premises for certain types of survey and examination/valuation.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2040"},{"id":"2035","label":"Housing renewal areas - steps to be taken after declaration or extension","desc":"As soon as may be after declaring an area to be a renewal area; or extending (or further extending) the period for which an area is to be a renewal area, a local housing authority shall take steps to bring the matter to the attention of persons residing or owning property in the area; and that those persons are informed of the name and address of the person to whom should be addressed inquiries and representations concerning action to be taken with respect to the renewal area.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2035"},{"id":"3989","label":"Housing \u2013 censure during or following an inquiry","desc":"A local authority must comply with censure notice issued by the Regulator during or following an inquiry and must respond to the same.NOTE this is applicable to any local authority which is a registered provider of social housing.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3989"},{"id":"3987","label":"Housing \u2013 compulsory outsourcing of management functions by tender","desc":"A local authority must comply with a notice requiring it to tender for the outsource of its housing management functions.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3987"},{"id":"3982","label":"Housing \u2013 emergency remedial action","desc":"A local authority must allow a person authorized by the Regulator to take emergency remedial action.NOTE this is applicable to any local authority which is a registered provider of social housing.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3982"},{"id":"3984","label":"Housing \u2013 emergency remedial action and resulting expenses - appeal","desc":"A local authority may appeal against proposals for emergency remedial action and/or associated expenses.NOTE this is applicable to any local authority, which is a registered provider of social housing.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/3984"},{"id":"3983","label":"Housing \u2013 emergency remedial action \u2013 Regulator\u2019s expenses","desc":"A local authority must pay the expenses of the Regulator incurred when carrying out emergency remedial action. NOTE this is applicable to any local authority which is a registered provider of social housing.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3983"},{"id":"3980","label":"Housing \u2013 enforcement notice","desc":"A local authority must comply with the requirements of an Enforcement Notice.NOTE this is applicable any local authority, which is a registered provider of social housing.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3980"},{"id":"4091","label":"Housing \u2013 Enforcement of landlord legislation by county council in England which is not a local housing authorities: duty to notify","desc":"Where a county council in England which is not a local housing authority proposes to take enforcement action in respect of a breach of, or an offence under, the landlord legislation the authority must notify the local housing authority for that area that it proposes to do so and must also notify if it chooses not to act.Where a such a county council acts in the area of a housing authority that authority is relieved of its duty to act in respect of that matter.In such circumstances the county council must notify the housing authority regarding proceedings, appeals, penalties and convictions.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/4091"},{"id":"4090","label":"Housing \u2013 Enforcement of landlord legislation by local housing authorities: duty to notify","desc":"Where a local housing authority proposes to take enforcement action in respect of a breach of, or an offence under, the landlord legislation which occurs (or which also occurs) in the area of another local housing authority the authority must notify the authority of the other area that it proposes to do so and must also notify if it chooses not to act.Where a local authority acts in the area of another the second local authority is relieved of its duty to act in respect of that matter.In such circumstances the first authority must notify the second authority regarding proceedings, appeals, penalties and convictions.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/4090"},{"id":"4089","label":"Housing \u2013 Enforcement of landlord legislation by local housing authorities: general duty","desc":"(1) It is the duty of every local housing authority to enforce the landlord legislation in its area.(2) But the duty in (1) does not prevent a local housing authority from taking enforcement action in respect of a breach of, or an offence under, the landlord legislation which occurs outside of its area.(3) The duty is also subject to sections 108(3) (enforcement by another local housing authority), 109(3) (enforcement by county council in England which is not a local housing authority) and 113(4) (enforcement by the lead enforcement authority).(4) A county council in England which is not a local housing authority may\u2014(a) enforce the landlord legislation;(b) for that purpose, exercise any powers that a local housing authority may exercise for the purposes of enforcing that legislation.Landlord legislation means\u2014(a) Chapters 3 and 6 of Part 1 of this Act,(b) Part 2 of this Act,(c) sections 1 and 1A of the Protection from Eviction Act 1977, and(d) Chapter 1 of Part 1 of the Housing Act 1988.For the purposes of this Part, a reference to taking enforcement action is a reference to\u2014(a) imposing a financial penalty, or(b) instituting proceedings against a person for an offence, under the landlord legislation.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/4089"},{"id":"4100","label":"Housing \u2013 Enforcement of landlord legislation: Business premises: Duty to allow access to seized documents","desc":"This section applies where any document seized by an officer of a local housing authority under this Chapter is detained by the officer or authority.If a request for permission to be granted access to that document is made to the local housing authority by a person who had custody or control of it immediately before it was seized, the local housing authority must allow that person access to it under the supervision of an officer.If a request for a photograph or copy of that document is made to the local housing authority by a person who had custody or control of it immediately before it was seized, the local housing authority must\u2014(a) allow that person access to it under the supervision of an officer for the purpose of photographing or copying it, or(b) photograph or copy it, or cause it to be photographed or copied.Where any document is photographed or copied, the photograph or copy must be supplied to the person who made the request within a reasonable time from the making of the request.This section does not require access to be granted to, or a photograph or copy to be supplied of, any document if the local housing authority has reasonable grounds for believing that to do so would prejudice the doing of anything for the purposes of which it was seized.A local housing authority may recover the reasonable costs of complying with a request under this section from the person by whom or on whose behalf it was made. References in this section to a person who had custody or control of a document immediately before it was seized include a representative of such a person.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/4100"},{"id":"4097","label":"Housing \u2013 Enforcement of landlord legislation: Business premises: entry with warrant","desc":"A local housing authority may apply to a justice of the peace to enter a business premises with a warrant if the required conditions for making the application are met and if it is granted an authorised officer has the powers given by section 121.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/4097"},{"id":"4095","label":"Housing \u2013 Enforcement of landlord legislation: Business premises: entry without warrant","desc":"An officer of a local housing authority may, at any reasonable time, enter any premises in England (and take photographs and make recordings there) if(a) the officer reasonably believes the premises to be occupied by a relevant person for the purposes of a rental sector business, and(b) the officer considers it necessary to enter the premises in order to exercise the powers under section 122 or 123 purposes connected with any function of the authority under or by virtue of the rented accommodation legislation.This power does not authorise entry into premises used wholly or mainly as residential accommodation.Routine inspections require service of a notice in the prescribed form upon the occupier.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/4095"},{"id":"4098","label":"Housing \u2013 Enforcement of landlord legislation: Business premises: Power to require production of documents following entry","desc":"An officer of a local housing authority who has entered premises under section 118 or under a warrant under section 120 may, for the purposes mentioned below, at any reasonable time\u2014(a) require a relevant person occupying the premises, or anyone on the premises acting on behalf of such a person, to produce any documents relating to the relevant business to which the person on the premises has access, and(b) take copies of, or of any entry in, any such document.The purposes are\u2014(a) to ascertain whether there has been compliance with the rented accommodation legislation where an officer of the local housing authority reasonably suspects a breach of, or an offence under, that legislation;(b) to ascertain whether the documents may be required as evidence in proceedings for such a breach or offence.The power above is available regardless of whether\u2014(a) the purpose for which the documents are required relates to the relevant person or some other person, or(b) proceedings could be taken against the relevant person or some other person.That power includes power to require the person to give an explanation of the documents.Where a document required to be produced contains information recorded electronically, the power in that subsection includes power to require the production of a copy of the document in a form in which it can easily be taken away and in which it is visible and legible.There is no requirement for a person to create a document or to produce a document which is subject to legal professional privilege.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/4098"},{"id":"4099","label":"Housing \u2013 Enforcement of landlord legislation: Business premises: Power to seize documents following entry","desc":"An officer of a local housing authority who has entered premises under section 118(1) or under a warrant under section 120 may seize and detain documents which the officer reasonably suspects may be required as evidence in proceedings relating to a breach of, or an offence under, the rented accommodation legislation.If one or more occupiers are on the premises, an officer seizing documents under this section must provide to that occupier or (if there is more than one) to at least one of them evidence of the officer's identity and authority, before seizing the documents.The officer need not comply with the above if it is not reasonably practicable to do so.An officer seizing documents under this section must take reasonable steps to\u2014(a) inform the person from whom they are seized that they have been seized, and(b) provide that person with a written record of what has been seized.In determining the steps to be taken, an officer exercising a power under this section must have regard to any relevant provision about the seizure of property made by a code of practice under section 66 of the Police and Criminal Evidence Act 1984.The above section does not confer any power on an officer to seize from a person any document which the person would be entitled to refuse to produce in proceedings in the High Court on the grounds of legal professional privilege.For the purpose of exercising the power under this section, the officer may, to the extent that is reasonably necessary for that purpose\u2014(a) require a person with authority to do so to access any electronic device in which information may be stored or from which it may be accessed, and(b) if such a requirement has not been complied with, access the electronic device.Documents seized under this section may not be detained\u2014(a) for a period of more than 3 months beginning with the day on which they were seized, or(b) where the documents are reasonably required to be detained for a longer period by the local housing authority for the purposes of the proceedings for which they were seized, for longer than they are required for those purposes.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/4099"},{"id":"4096","label":"Housing \u2013 Enforcement of landlord legislation: Duties where business premises is entered without warrant","desc":"If an officer of a local housing authority enters premises under section 118(1) and finds one or more occupiers on the premises, the officer must\u2014(a) produce evidence of the officer's identity and authority to that occupier or (if there is more than one) to at least one of them, and(b) if the entry takes place otherwise than in the course of a routine inspection, provide to that occupier or (if there is more than one) to at least one of them a document that\u2014(i) sets out why the entry is necessary, and(ii) indicates the nature of the offences under section 131(1) and (2).An officer need not comply with the above if it is not reasonably practicable to do so.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/4096"},{"id":"4102","label":"Housing \u2013 Enforcement of landlord legislation: Duties where occupiers are on residential premises entered without warrant","desc":"If an officer of a local housing authority enters premises under section 126(1) and finds one or more occupiers on the premises, the officer must produce evidence of the officer's identity and special authorisation to that occupier or (if there is more than one) to at least one of them.An officer need not comply with the above if it is not reasonably practicable to do so.Proceedings resulting from the exercise of the power under section 126(1) are not invalid merely because of a failure to comply with the above.NOTE: \"special authorisation\" has the same meaning as in section 126(10).","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/4102"},{"id":"4092","label":"Housing \u2013 Enforcement of landlord legislation: duty to report","desc":"A local housing authority, or a county council which is not a local housing authority, must report to the Secretary of State on the exercise of its functions under the landlord legislation.A report under must\u2014(a) be provided at such time and in such form as the Secretary of State requires, and(b) contain such information as the Secretary of State requires.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/4092"},{"id":"4094","label":"Housing \u2013 Enforcement of landlord legislation: power to apply for court order","desc":"If a person fails to comply with a notice under section 115, the local housing authority or an officer of the authority may make an application to the court.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/4094"},{"id":"4093","label":"Housing \u2013 Enforcement of landlord legislation: power to require information form relevant person or any person","desc":"A local housing authority, may, in prescribed circumstances, when enforcing landlord legislation issue a notice in the specified form requiring information from a relevant person or from any person.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/4093"},{"id":"4104","label":"Housing \u2013 Enforcement of landlord legislation: Powers of accompanying person","desc":"A person who accompanies an officer of a local housing authority entering premises under, or under a warrant under, sections 114 to 129 of the Renters Rights Act 2025\u2014(a) has the same powers as the officer in relation to the premises, but(b) must exercise those powers only in the company, and under the supervision, of the officer.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/4104"},{"id":"4103","label":"Housing \u2013 Enforcement of landlord legislation: Suspected residential tenancy: entry with warrant","desc":"A local housing authority may apply to a justice of the peace to enter a business premises with a warrant if the required conditions for making the application are met and if it is granted an authorised officer has the powers given by section 129.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/4103"},{"id":"4101","label":"Housing \u2013 Enforcement of landlord legislation: Suspected residential tenancy: entry without warrant","desc":"A specially authorised officer of a local housing authority may enter premises in England at any reasonable time, if\u2014(a) the officer reasonably suspects that the premises, or part of the premises, are subject to a residential tenancy within the meaning of Part 2 of the Act, and(b) the officer considers it necessary to inspect the premises for the purpose of investigating whether there has been, in relation to the premises\u2014(i) a breach of section 82(3),(ii) an offence under subsection 92(1)(iii) an offence under subsection 92(2) where the continuing conduct referred to in paragraph (b) of that subsection is a breach of section 82(3),(iv) an offence under subsection 92(3) where the different breach to in paragraph (b) of that subsection is a breach of section 82(3),(v) an offence under subsection 92(4) where the different breach to in paragraph (b) of that subsection is a breach of section 82(3), or(vi) an offence under section 1 of the Protection from Eviction Act 1977, and(c) notice has been given in accordance with the requirements of the above to\u2014(i) an occupier of the premises, and(ii) any person who has an estate or interest in the premises, other than a mortgagee not in possession and has supplied the local housing authority with an address for the purposes of this paragraph, unless notice is not required.The requirements referred to in (c) are that\u2014(a) the notice is in writing and is given by an officer of the local housing authority,(b) the notice sets out why the entry is necessary and indicates the nature of the offences under section 131(1) and (2) (obstruction), and(c) there are at least 24 hours between the giving of the notice and the entry.A notice need not be given to a person who has waived the requirement to give notice.A notice need not be given in accordance with (1)(c)(ii) to a person who is a residential landlord.If\u2014(a) premises are entered in exercise of the power conferred by (1), and(b) notice is not given to any person because of (4), an officer of the local housing authority must give that person notice in writing of the exercise of that power within a reasonable period after its exercise.The notice must\u2014(a) identify the premises that were entered,(b) state when the premises were entered, and(c) state the purpose for which the premises were entered.A specially authorised officer entering premises may be accompanied by such persons, and may take onto the premises such equipment, as the officer thinks necessary.A specially authorised officer entering premises may take photographs or make recordings.A specially authorised officer must, if requested to do so, produce the officer's special authorisation for inspection by a person to whom notice is required to be given under this section or anyone acting on behalf of such a person.For the purposes of this section an officer of a local housing authority is \"specially authorised\" where the officer's authorisation by the local housing authority for the purposes of this power; and(a) states the particular purpose for which the officer is authorised to exercise the power, and(b) is given by the local housing authority acting through\u2014(i) a deputy chief officer of the authority whose duties include duties relating to a purpose within subsection (1)(b), or(ii) an officer of the authority to whom such a deputy chief officer reports directly, or is directly accountable, as respects duties so relating.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/4101"},{"id":"3913","label":"Housing \u2013 HMO license revocation in banning order cases","desc":"A local authority must revoke a licence for a house in multiple occupation banning order cases.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3913"},{"id":"3988","label":"Housing \u2013 housing related advisers","desc":"A local authority must comply with a direction from the Regulator to appoint or co-operate with housing related advisers on the terms advised by the Regulator.NOTE this is applicable to any local authority which is a registered provider of social housing.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3988"},{"id":"4088","label":"Housing \u2013 Imposition of financial penalty for breach of requirement to state rent and requirement to avoid rental bidding","desc":"(1) A local housing authority may impose a financial penalty under this subsection on a person if satisfied on the balance of probabilities that the person has breached the prohibition imposed by section 56(2) or (3)If\u2014(a) the local housing authority imposes a financial penalty under (1) on a person, and(b) within the period of five years ending with the date on which that penalty was imposed, a previous financial penalty under (1) was imposed on that person in relation to a breach of the same subsection of section 56, then the local housing authority may impose an additional financial penalty under this subsection on that person.(3) The amount of a financial penalty imposed under this section is to be determined by the authority imposing it, but must not be more than \u00a37,000.(4) Subsection (2) does not enable a penalty to be imposed after the final notice in respect of the previous penalty has been withdrawn or quashed on appeal.(5) Where\u2014(a) a local housing authority is satisfied as mentioned in subsection (1) in relation to two or more persons, and(b) the breaches in relation to which the local housing authority is so satisfied arise from the same conduct by one or more of the persons acting on behalf of the others, the local housing authority may impose a financial penalty under that subsection on the persons (or some of them) jointly, and if the local housing authority does so, the persons on whom the penalty is imposed are jointly and severally liable to pay it.(6) The Secretary of State may give guidance to local housing authorities about the exercise of their functions under this section.(7) Local housing authorities must have regard to any guidance issued.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/4088"},{"id":"4087","label":"Housing \u2013 Imposition of financial penalty for further certain acts of discrimination","desc":"(1) A local housing authority may impose a financial penalty under this subsection on a person if satisfied on the balance of probabilities that the person has breached a requirement imposed by\u2014(a) section 33 or 34(b) provision in regulations made under section 39.(2) More than one financial penalty may be imposed under subsection (1) on the same person in respect of the same conduct only if\u2014(a) the conduct continues after the end of 28 days beginning with the day after that on which the previous penalty in respect of the conduct was imposed on the person, unless the person appeals against the decision to impose the penalty within that period, or(b) if the person appeals against the decision to impose the penalty within that period, the conduct continues after the end of 28 days beginning with the day after that on which the appeal is finally determined, withdrawn or abandoned.(3) Where a person applies a single provision, criterion or practice on more than one occasion in relation to the same dwelling, each application of that provision, criterion or practice is to be treated as the same conduct for the purposes of subsection (2).(4) If\u2014(a) the local housing authority imposes a financial penalty under subsection (1) on a person, and(b) within the period of five years ending with the date on which that penalty was imposed, a previous financial penalty under subsection (1) was imposed on that person in relation to a breach of the same section or provision in regulations made under section 39 then the local housing authority may impose an additional financial penalty under this subsection on that person.(5) The amount of a financial penalty imposed under this section is to be determined by the authority imposing it, but must not be more than \u00a37,000.(6) Neither subsection (2) nor subsection (4) enables a penalty to be imposed after the final notice in respect of the previous penalty has been withdrawn or quashed on appeal.(7) Where\u2014(a) a local housing authority is satisfied as mentioned in subsection (1) in relation to two or more persons, and(b) the breaches in relation to which the local housing authority is so satisfied arise from the same conduct by one or more of the persons acting on behalf of the others, the local housing authority may impose a financial penalty under that subsection on the persons (or some of them) jointly, and if the local housing authority does so, the persons on whom the penalty is imposed are jointly and severally liable to pay it.(8) The Secretary of State may give guidance to local housing authorities about the exercise of their functions under this section.(9) Local housing authorities must have regard to any guidance issued under (8).","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/4087"},{"id":"4105","label":"Housing \u2013 Imposition of financial penalty for unlawful eviction and harassment of occupier","desc":"A local housing authority may impose a financial penalty on a person if satisfied beyond reasonable doubt that the person has committed an offence under section 1 in relation to premises in England.No financial penalty may be imposed in respect of any conduct amounting to an offence under section 1 if\u2014(a) the person has been convicted of an offence under that section in respect of the conduct,(b) criminal proceedings for an offence under that section in respect of the conduct have been instituted against the person and the proceedings have not been concluded, or(c) criminal proceedings for an offence under that section in respect of the conduct have been concluded and the person has not been convicted of the offence.The amount of a financial penalty imposed under this section is to be determined by the authority imposing it, but must not be more than \u00a340,000.The Secretary of State may give guidance to local housing authorities about the exercise of their functions under this section.Local housing authorities must have regard to any guidance issued and to schedule 1A.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/4105"},{"id":"3985","label":"Housing \u2013 penalties and fines","desc":"A local authority must pay a penalty or fine imposed by the Regulator.NOTE this is applicable to any local authority which is a registered provider of social housing.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3985"},{"id":"3986","label":"Housing \u2013 Penalties and Fines - Appeal","desc":"A local authority may appeal against a penalty or fine imposed by The Regulator.NOTE this is applicable to any local authority which is a registered provider of social housing.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/3986"},{"id":"3978","label":"Housing \u2013 performance improvement plan","desc":"A local authority must comply with the requirements of a performance improvement plan. NOTE this is applicable to any local authority which is a registered provider of social housing.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3978"},{"id":"3915","label":"Housing \u2013 revoke licence in banning order cases","desc":"A local authority must revoke a licence for residential accommodation in Banning Order cases.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3915"},{"id":"996","label":"Human rights - acts of public authorities","desc":"A local authority must comply with the Human Rights Act 1998.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/996"},{"id":"1671","label":"Hypnotism - licence fee","desc":"A local authority may charge a fee for a licence for demonstrations of hypnotism.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/1671"},{"id":"1670","label":"Hypnotism - licensing","desc":"A local authority may issue a licence, with conditions, for the exhibition, demonstration or performance of hypnotism.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/1670"},{"id":"3896","label":"Illegal migration - provision of information","desc":"A local authority in England must comply with a direction form the Secretary of State directing the local authority to provide information to the Secretary of State for the purposes of helping the Secretary of State to make a decision under section 17(1) or (4) (decision to transfer unaccompanied migrant child from Secretary of State to local authority or vice versa) of the Act.The information that the Secretary of State may direct a local authority to provide is\u2014(a) information about the accommodation and support provided to children by the local authority;(b) such other information as may be specified in regulations made by the Secretary of State.A local authority which is directed to provide information under this section must provide it\u2014(a) in such form and manner as the Secretary of State may direct, and(b) before such time or before the end of such period as the Secretary of State may direct.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3896"},{"id":"998","label":"Immigration and asylum - accommodation","desc":"A local authority must assist the Secretary of State with regard to the provision of accommodation for asylum seekers.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/998"},{"id":"700","label":"Immigration and asylum - accommodation centres","desc":"A local authority may assist in the provision of an accommodation centre including the provision of services and reasonable expenditure.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/700"},{"id":"1001","label":"Immigration and asylum - child welfare","desc":"A local authority must not provide child welfare services to anyone to whom the Secretary of State is providing support pursuant to section 122.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1001"},{"id":"701","label":"Immigration and asylum - disclosure of information","desc":"A local authority must supply the Secretary of State with information for the purpose of establishing where a person is when requested to do so.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/701"},{"id":"1000","label":"Immigration and asylum - housing","desc":"A local authority must not supply housing to anyone subject to immigration control other than in accordance with the Act.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1000"},{"id":"999","label":"Immigration and asylum - reception zones","desc":"A local authority must comply with the Secretary of State's directions regarding accommodation for asylum seekers, if its area is designated as a reception zone.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/999"},{"id":"997","label":"Immigration and asylum - support","desc":"A local authority may provide support to asylum seekers in prescribed circumstances.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/997"},{"id":"3854","label":"Immigration control - assistance with age assessment","desc":"Where a local authority refers an age-disputed person to a designated person for an age assessment under subsection 50(1) or (3)(a) of the Act, the local authority must provide any assistance that the designated person reasonably requires from the authority for the purposes of conducting that assessment.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3854"},{"id":"3853","label":"Immigration control - evidence of age assessment","desc":"Where a local authority - (a) conducts an age assessment itself, or(b) informs the Secretary of State that it is satisfied that an age-disputed person is the age they claim (or are claimed) to be,it must, on request from the Secretary of State, provide the Secretary of State with such evidence as the Secretary of State reasonably requires for the Secretary of State to consider the local authority's decision.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3853"},{"id":"3852","label":"Immigration control - mandatory age assessment","desc":"Where a local authority -(a) needs to know the age of an age-disputed person for the purposes of deciding whether or how to exercise any of its functions under relevant children's legislation in relation to the person, or(b) the Secretary of State notifies a local authority in writing that the Secretary of State doubts that an age-disputed person in relation to whom the local authority has exercised or may exercise functions under relevant children's legislation is the age that they claim (or are claimed) to be.The local authority must -(a) refer the age-disputed person to a designated person for an age assessment under this section,(b) conduct an age assessment on the age-disputed person itself and inform the Secretary of State in writing of the result of its assessment, or(c) inform the Secretary of State in writing that it is satisfied that the person is the age they claim (or are claimed) to be, without the need for an age assessment","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3852"},{"id":"3851","label":"Immigration control - referral for age assessment","desc":"Local authorities may refer an age-disputed person to a designated person for an age assessment where -(a) a local authority needs to know the age of an age-disputed person for the purposes of deciding whether or how to exercise any of its functions under relevant children's legislation in relation to the person, or(b) the Secretary of State notifies a local authority in writing that the Secretary of State doubts that an age-disputed person in relation to whom the local authority has exercised or may exercise functions under relevant children's legislation is the age that they claim (or are claimed) to be.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/3851"},{"id":"1731","label":"Injurious weeds - exercise of Minister's powers","desc":"A local authority must exercise the Minister's powers under the Act if authorised to do so.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1731"},{"id":"2063","label":"Inspection of breeding establishments for dogs","desc":"A local authority may authorise in writing any of its officers or any veterinary practitioner to inspect any premises in their area as respects which a licence granted is in force. Any person authorised under this section may, on producing his authority if so required, enter any such premises at all reasonable times and inspect them and any animals found, for the purpose of ascertaining whether an offence has been or is being committed against this Act.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2063"},{"id":"2157","label":"Insurance - members/voluntary assistants","desc":"A local authority may enter into a contract of accident insurance against the risk of any member or voluntary assistant of the authority meeting with a personal accident, whether fatal or not, while engaged on the business of the authority.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2157"},{"id":"1196","label":"Integrated pollution control and air pollution - discharge of functions","desc":"A local authority must have regard to directions from the Secretary of State and to the Act when exercising its functions.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1196"},{"id":"2328","label":"Land acquisition - compulsory purchase for road improvement","desc":"Where the appropriate Minister is satisfied that the construction or improvement of a road is needed, a local highway authority may, on being authorised to do so by the appropriate Minister acquire compulsorily any land as to which he is satisfied that its acquisition by the authority is requisite for the construction or improvement of the road, or for carrying out the improvement, or controlling the development, of frontages to the road or of land abutting on or adjacent to the road.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2328"},{"id":"2330","label":"Land acquisition - compulsory purchase notices in newspapers","desc":"The acquiring authority shall in two successive weeks publish a notice in the prescribed form in one or more local newspapers circulating in the locality in which the land comprised in the order is situated.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2330"},{"id":"2331","label":"Land acquisition - compulsory purchase notices to owners, lessees and occupiers","desc":"The acquiring authority shall serve on every qualifying person a notice in the prescribed form stating the effect of the order, stating that it is about to be submitted for confirmation, and specifying the time (not being less than twenty-one days from service of the notice) within which, and the manner in which, objections to the order can be made.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2331"},{"id":"2147","label":"Land acquisition - payment of purchase or compensation money to another authority","desc":"A local authority may pay purchase or compensation money to another authority, in certain circumstances, with the consent of the Secretary of State.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2147"},{"id":"2329","label":"Land acquisition - request for inofrmation","desc":"This applies to information about land in relation to which an acquiring authority is entitled to exercise a power of compulsory purchase. The acquiring authority may serve a notice requiring information","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2329"},{"id":"2333","label":"Land and property - compulsory purchase - preliminary notices","desc":"Before making a declaration with respect to any land which is subject to a compulsory purchase order the acquiring authority shall produce a notice as required by the Act","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2333"},{"id":"2334","label":"Land and property - compulsory purchase - recovery of overpaid compensation","desc":"Where after the execution of a general vesting declaration a person (the claimant) claims compensation in respect of the acquisition by the acquiring authority of an interest in land by virtue of the declaration, and the authority pay compensation in respect of that interest. in certain circumstances the acquiring authority may recover from the claimant the amount of the excess.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2334"},{"id":"38","label":"Land of community value - co-operation between authorities","desc":"Where land on the register of community assets spans local authority areas all of those local authorities must co-operate in ensuring compliance with the Act.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/38"},{"id":"37","label":"Land of community value - disposal moratorium","desc":"The local authority must comply with regulations governing the moratorium on the disposal by the owner of land included in a local authority's list of assets of community value.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/37"},{"id":"3183","label":"Land of community value - maintenance of list","desc":"The local authority must maintain a list of land in its area that is land of community value.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3183"},{"id":"3184","label":"Land of community value - nominations for register of land","desc":"The local authority must consider a nomination to list land in its list of assets of community value and to give reasons if the nomination is unsuccessful. The local authority must also give notice of inclusion or removal from the list and must review land included if requested.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3184"},{"id":"36","label":"Land of community value - publication of intended sale","desc":"The local authority must edit its list of assets of community value to show notification of intended sale and publicise that intended sale and notify the owner of the asset of any community interest group that requests to be treated as a potential bidder and to pay compensation in certain circumstances.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/36"},{"id":"3185","label":"Land of community value - unsuccessful nominations for register of land","desc":"The local authority must maintain a list of land that has been unsuccessfully nominated for inclusion in its list.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3185"},{"id":"1931","label":"Landlord and tenant - power of local housing authority to prosecute","desc":"Proceedings for an offence under any provision of the Landlord and Tenant Act may be brought by a local housing authority.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/1931"},{"id":"2947","label":"Lcensing - zoo licence - local authority zoos","desc":"A local authority must send certain information to the Secretary of State regarding the licencing of local authority zoos and must comply with the Secretary of State\u2019s directions.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2947"},{"id":"1767","label":"Leading and driving of animals - streets and routes","desc":"A local authority may prescribe routes over which the leading and driving of animals is permitted in certain circumstances.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/1767"},{"id":"2169","label":"Legal proceedings - appearance of local authorities","desc":"Any member or officer of a local authority who is authorised by that authority to prosecute or defend on their behalf, or to appear on their behalf in, proceedings before a magistrates' court shall be entitled to prosecute or defend or to appear in any such proceedings, and to conduct any such proceedings.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2169"},{"id":"2168","label":"Legal proceedings - prosecution or defence and representations at inquiries","desc":"A local authority where it considers it expedient for the promotion or protection of the interests of the inhabitants of their area may prosecute or defend or appear in any legal proceedings and, in the case of civil proceedings, may institute them in their own name, and may, in their own name, make representations in the interests of the inhabitants at any public inquiry held by or on behalf of any Minister or public body under any enactment.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2168"},{"id":"3361","label":"Legal services - reserved legal activities","desc":"The local weights and measures authority institute proceedings for an offence under section 14 or under section 16 of the Act if the activity which it is alleged that the accused was not entitled to carry on constitutes reserved instrument activities. The authority has the power to enter premises, search and obtain copies or seize documents which may be relevant to any investigation.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/3361"},{"id":"3138","label":"Libraries - charging","desc":"A local authority may not charge for library services save as allowed for by section 8 or by Regulations","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3138"},{"id":"1622","label":"Libraries - co-operation with the Secretary of State","desc":"A local authority shall furnish such information, and provide such facilities for the inspection of library premises, stocks and records, as the Secretary of State may require for carrying out his duty.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1622"},{"id":"1627","label":"Libraries - contributions towards expenses","desc":"A local authority may make contributions towards the expenses of another library authority.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/1627"},{"id":"1628","label":"Libraries - default powers of Secretary of State","desc":"A local authority must comply with the directions of the Secretary of State when he is exercising his default powers where a library authority has failed to carry out duties relating to the public library service.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1628"},{"id":"1623","label":"Libraries - formation of joint boards","desc":"Two or more local authorities may form joint boards with the consent of the Secretary of State.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/1623"},{"id":"1625","label":"Libraries - library service","desc":"A local authority must provide a comprehensive and efficient library service for all persons desiring to make use thereof.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1625"},{"id":"1626","label":"Libraries - restriction on charges for library facilities","desc":"A local authority may not charge for library services save as allowed for by section 8 or by regulations.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1626"},{"id":"1629","label":"Libraries - transfer of staff, assets and liabilities","desc":"A local authority must take certain steps where staff, assets and liabilities transfer under the Act.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1629"},{"id":"2785","label":"Licences - child performances","desc":"Local authorities may grant and must follow the prescribed procedure and requirements in respect of licences granted under section 25 of the Children and Young Persons Act 1933 for children performing or taking part in activities abroad for profit. LAs must impose any conditions which they consider necessary in order to ensure that the child is fit to take part in the performance or activity; proper provision is made to secure the child's health and wellbeing; and proper provision is made to ensure that the child's education will not suffer.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2785"},{"id":"3092","label":"Licences - child performances- requirements and conditions","desc":"Local authorities must follow the prescribed procedure and requirements in respect of licences granted under section 25 of the Children and Young Persons Act 1933 for children performing or taking part in activities abroad for profit. LAs must impose any conditions which they consider necessary in order to ensure that the child is fit to take part in the performance or activity; proper provision is made to secure the child's health and wellbeing; and proper provision is made to ensure that the child's education will not suffer.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3092"},{"id":"2945","label":"Licences - granting of zoo licence","desc":"A local authority may grant a licence for a zoo, after consider inspectors' reports. Such a licence may be granted subject to conditions, may be transferred, renewed or altered.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2945"},{"id":"3777","label":"Licensing - conditions for determination of pavement licence application","desc":"When considering an application for a pavement licence the local authority must take into account any representations made to it during the public consultation period, consult the highway authority for the relevant highway to which the application relates, where the local authority is not that authority, and consult such other persons as the local authority considers appropriate.undertake certain consultations and must have regard to A local authority may grant a pavement licence only if the authority considers that, taking into account any conditions subject to which it proposes to grant the licence nothing done by the licence-holder pursuant to the licence would have an effect on other pavement users as specified in Regulations.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3777"},{"id":"3778","label":"Licensing - enforcement of pavement licences","desc":"A local authority may revoke a pavement licence or enforce conditions under which the licence was issued where it considers it necessary to do so. Circumstances under which revocation or enforcement may be imposed are as detailed in legislation.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/3778"},{"id":"529","label":"Licensing - fireworks suppliers","desc":"A local authority must comply with regulations regarding the licensing of fireworks.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/529"},{"id":"3779","label":"Licensing - grant of pavement licence","desc":"A local authority may grant a pavement licence, subject to conditions as prescribed, but only if the authority considers that, taking into account any conditions subject to which it proposes to grant the licence, nothing done by the licence-holder pursuant to the licence would have a negative effect on certain matters relating to traffic and statutory undertakings.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/3779"},{"id":"3780","label":"Licensing - guidance on pavement licences","desc":"A local authority must have regard to guidance issued by the Secretary of State when considering pavement licences.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3780"},{"id":"3776","label":"Licensing - information and notices for pavement licence","desc":"The local authority may require information to be provided as part of an application and for notices to be published in a certain manner.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/3776"},{"id":"2946","label":"Licensing - inspection of zoos","desc":"A local authority must inspect zoos and closed zoos in its area in certain circumstances.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2946"},{"id":"2800","label":"Licensing - late night refreshment","desc":"The local authority (Licensing Authority) may designate the premises described in these Regulations under paragraph 2A of Schedule 2 to the Licensing Act 2003 as exempt from the licensing requirements that apply to the provision of late night refreshment, that is to say the supply to the public of hot food or hot drinks between 11pm and 5am.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2800"},{"id":"2735","label":"Licensing - mobile home site rules (England)","desc":"Local authorities must establish and keep up a register of site rules for protected sites in its area, publish it online and open it for inspection during office hours at the LA\u2019s offices.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2735"},{"id":"2736","label":"Licensing - mobile home site rules (Wales)","desc":"local authorities must establish and keep up a register of site rules for protected sites in its area, publish it online and open it for inspection during office hours at the LA\u2019s offices","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2736"},{"id":"2734","label":"Licensing - mobile home sites transfer of licence","desc":"Local authorities must have regard to prescribed matters when issuing or giving consent to transfer of a site licence; may require transfer applications to be accompanied by specified information and must provide prescribed information on refusal","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2734"},{"id":"3775","label":"Licensing - pavement licences","desc":"The local authority to which an application for a pavement licence is made must, in such manner as it considers appropriate\u2014(a)publish the application and any information or material required by the local authority, and(b)publicise the fact that representations relating to the application may be made to the authority during the public consultation period (and indicate when that period comes to an end).","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3775"},{"id":"3215","label":"Licensing - Petroleum storage certificates","desc":"A petroleum enforcement authority must grant a certificate in respect of dispensing premises (a \u201cstorage certificate\u201d) where\u2014(a)an application has been made in accordance with this regulation; and(b)it is satisfied that the containment system for petrol at the dispensing premises, including storage tanks, pipework and dispensers, may reasonably be used to store petrol and would not create an unacceptable risk to the health or safety of any person.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3215"},{"id":"3216","label":"Licensing - petroleum storage licence","desc":"A petroleum enforcement authority may grant a person a licence authorising the keeping of petrol in excess of 275 litres in domestic or other relevant premises.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/3216"},{"id":"3142","label":"Licensing - taxi and private hire vehicles","desc":"A local authority responsible for the licencing of taxis and private hire vehicles must have regard to the Secretary of State's Guidance.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3142"},{"id":"2948","label":"Licensing - zoo licence - exemptions","desc":"A local authority may apply to the Secretary of State for a dispensation that certain zoos are to be exempt from the provisions of the Act.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2948"},{"id":"2949","label":"Licensing - zoo licencing - fees","desc":"A local authority may charge reasonable fees in relation to dealing with licences and inspections","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2949"},{"id":"2950","label":"Licensing - zoo licensing - enforcement and closure","desc":"A local authority may give directions to enforce licencing conditions or the requirement to be licenced after following the prescribed procedure and may direct the closure of a zoo in certain circumstances.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2950"},{"id":"2952","label":"Licensing - zoo licensing - powers of entry","desc":"A person duly authorised by a local authority may enter a zoo in certain circumstances.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2952"},{"id":"2951","label":"Licensing - zoo licensing - welfare of animals","desc":"A local authority may give directions or make arrangements for the welfare or disposal of animals in certain circumstances.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2951"},{"id":"735","label":"Licensing and registration - private security industry licence","desc":"A local authority must comply with any Regulations issued regarding private security industry licensing.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/735"},{"id":"2062","label":"Licensing of breeding establishments for dogs","desc":"A local authority may grant a licence for the breeding in dogs in certain circumstances.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2062"},{"id":"2340","label":"Licensing/registration - acupuncture, tattooing, ear-piercing and electrolysis","desc":"A local authority may resolve to control acupuncture, tattooing, ear-piercing and electrolysis establishments in their area.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2340"},{"id":"696","label":"Licensing/registration - cancellation of motor salvage operator registration","desc":"A local authority may cancel a person's registration in the register for their area if they are satisfied that he is not a fit and proper person to carry on business as a motor salvage operator.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/696"},{"id":"698","label":"Licensing/registration - entry to property of registration plate supplier","desc":"An authorised officer of a local authority may enter a and inspect the premises of a registered registration plate supplier for the purposes of enforcing the Act.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/698"},{"id":"2335","label":"Licensing/registration - objections to application for PSV operator's licence","desc":"Where an application is made for the grant of a PSV operator's licence under this Act, any chief officer of police or local authority may object to the grant of the licence","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2335"},{"id":"697","label":"Licensing/registration - proceedings for offences related to motor salvage operators","desc":"A local authority may institute proceedings for an offence under Part I of the Act.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/697"},{"id":"699","label":"Licensing/registration - proceedings for offences related to registration plate suppliers","desc":"A local authority may institute proceedings under Part II of the Act.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/699"},{"id":"695","label":"Licensing/registration - register of motor salvage operators","desc":"A local authority must establish and maintain a register of motor salvage operators.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/695"},{"id":"2339","label":"Licensing/registration - sex establishments","desc":"A local authority may resolve to control sex establishments in their area.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2339"},{"id":"2337","label":"Licensing/registration - zoos","desc":"Before granting or refusing to grant a licence for a zoo, the local authority shall consider inspectors' reports made in pursuance of inspections of the zoo under this Act and shall also consult the applicant about the conditions they propose would be attached to the licence, if one were granted, and make arrangements for an inspection to be carried out.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2337"},{"id":"3251","label":"Lieutenants - appointment","desc":"Her majesty may appoint a Lieutenants other than Lord Lieutenants for every County in England and Wales.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/3251"},{"id":"2344","label":"Litter - consultations and proposals for abatement","desc":"In England and Wales, it shall be the duty of the council of each non-metropolitan county and the other litter authorities whose areas are included in the county to consult from time to time together, and with such voluntary bodies as they consider appropriate about the steps which the county council and each of the other litter authorities are to take for the purpose of abating litter in the county.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2344"},{"id":"1252","label":"Litter - direction regarding collected litter","desc":"A local authority must comply with directions in respect of certain collected litter.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1252"},{"id":"1244","label":"Litter - fixed penalty notice","desc":"A person authorised by a local authority may issue a fixed penalty notice for the offence of littering.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/1244"},{"id":"1249","label":"Litter - fixed penalty notices for street litter","desc":"An authorised officer of a local authority may issue a fixed penalty notice in the prescribed manner in relation to certain street litter offences.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/1249"},{"id":"1250","label":"Litter - free distribution of printed matter","desc":"A local authority may make certain orders and grant licences about the distribution of printed matter.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/1250"},{"id":"1245","label":"Litter - keeping land and highway litter free","desc":"A local authority must ensure that the land in their area is, so far as is practicable, kept clear of litter and refuse.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1245"},{"id":"1246","label":"Litter - land of the Crown, educational establishments and statutory undertakers","desc":"A local authority must where land of the Crown, educational establishments or statutory undertakers is defaced by litter or refuse or that defacement of it by litter or refuse is likely to recur, serve a litter abatement notice imposing either a prescribed requirement or prohibition.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1246"},{"id":"1247","label":"Litter - litter clearing notices","desc":"A local authority may serve a litter clearing notice in respect of any land in the open air.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/1247"},{"id":"2091","label":"Litter - litter statement","desc":"A county council must consult with district councils in its area draw up (and from time to time revise) a litter statement and keep it available for inspection at its offices.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2091"},{"id":"1251","label":"Litter - public register","desc":"A local authority must maintain a public register of litter control notices and orders and make the same a available for inspection and supply copy documents for a fee.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1251"},{"id":"1243","label":"Litter - publicity of offence of leaving litter","desc":"A local authority may publicise the fact that leaving litter is an offence and the consequences of committing that offence.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/1243"},{"id":"1248","label":"Litter - street litter control notices","desc":"A local authority may issue a street litter clearing notice in certain circumstances.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/1248"},{"id":"3093","label":"Litter bins - cleaning and emptying","desc":"It shall be the duty of a litter authority in England and Wales to make arrangements for the regular emptying and cleansing of any litter bins provided.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3093"},{"id":"2346","label":"Litter bins - contribution to expenditure","desc":"A county council and a metropolitan district council may if they think fit make a contribution to any expenditure incurred by a parish council or a community council in providing/emptying bins.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2346"},{"id":"2345","label":"Litter bins - provision and maintenance","desc":"A litter authority in England and Wales may provide and maintain in any street or public place receptacles for refuse or litter. It shall be the duty of a litter authority in England and Wales to make arrangements for the regular emptying and cleansing of any litter bins provided.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2345"},{"id":"233","label":"Litter, graffiti and fly-posting - providing information about receipts","desc":"A local authority must provide information about their use of fixed penalty receipts to the appropriate person.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/233"},{"id":"232","label":"Litter, graffiti and fly-posting - use of receipts","desc":"A local authority may use specified fixed penalty receipts for certain purposes of qualifying functions of the authority.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/232"},{"id":"2651","label":"Livestock - animal by-products (England)","desc":"A local authority is the enforcement authority (other than as prescribed) with regards to the staining of animal by-products and derived products not intended for human consumption","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2651"},{"id":"2700","label":"Livestock - animal by-products (Wales)","desc":"A LA is the enforcement authority (other than as prescribed) with regards to Regulations regarding the staining of animal by-products and derived products not intended for human consumption","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2700"},{"id":"3261","label":"Livestock - animal gatherings enforcement","desc":"The local authority has a duty to enforce the regulations relating to animal gatherings. For the purposes of this legislation \u201canimals\u201d means cattle (excluding bison and yak), deer, goats, sheep and pigs.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3261"},{"id":"3262","label":"Livestock - post-import control","desc":"The local authority has a duty to enforce regulations relating to the post-import control of livestock.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3262"},{"id":"2729","label":"Local audit - auditor panel","desc":"The local authority which appoints the panel member must determine the term of that office. It must take steps on the disqualification of a member or chair as prescribed and may pay the members of its auditor panel such allowances as the authority may determine.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2729"},{"id":"2728","label":"Local audit - auditor resignation and removal","desc":"A local authority must take prescribed steps upon an auditor\u2019s resignation from office or when removing a local auditor from office and when appointing a new local auditor (within three months).","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2728"},{"id":"2968","label":"Local auditor \u2013 costs for court application for unlawful item of expenditure","desc":"A local authority must pay the auditor\u2019s reasonable costs in connection with an application to court that an item of expenditure was unlawful.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2968"},{"id":"2967","label":"Local auditor \u2013 costs for dealing with objections to accounts","desc":"A local authority must pay the auditor\u2019s reasonable costs in dealing with objections to accounts.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2967"},{"id":"2969","label":"Local auditor \u2013 costs for judicial review","desc":"A local authority must pay the auditor\u2019s reasonable costs in relation to the Auditor applying for judicial review.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2969"},{"id":"2966","label":"Local auditor \u2013 Inspection of Statement of Accounts and other information","desc":"A local authority must allow its Statement of Accounts and certain other information to be inspected by a local government elector and must supply copies where necessary.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2966"},{"id":"2143","label":"Local authorities - acquisition of land by agreement","desc":"A local authority may acquire land by agreement whether within or outside their area, for the purposes of any of their functions under this or any other enactment, or for the benefit, improvement or development of their area.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2143"},{"id":"2144","label":"Local authorities - acquisition of land by compulsory purchase","desc":"A local authority may acquire land by compulsory purchase for certain purposes.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2144"},{"id":"2139","label":"Local authorities - appointment of staff","desc":"A local authority must appoint such officers as they think necessary for the proper discharge by the authority of their or another authority's functions as fall to be discharged by them pursuant to an agreement made under section 113. An officer appointed shall hold office on such reasonable terms and conditions as the authority think fit.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2139"},{"id":"2145","label":"Local authorities - appropriation of land","desc":"A local authority may appropriate land for certain purposes.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2145"},{"id":"2146","label":"Local authorities - disposal of land","desc":"A local authority may dispose of land in certain circumstances.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2146"},{"id":"3014","label":"Local authorities - governance arrangements","desc":"A local authority must comply with the governance arrangements laid down in an Order of the Secretary of State.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3014"},{"id":"2138","label":"Local authorities - incidental powers","desc":"A local authority may do anything (whether or not involving the expenditure, borrowing or lending of money or the acquisition or disposal of any property or rights) which is calculated to facilitate, or is conducive or incidental to, the discharge of any of their functions.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2138"},{"id":"2142","label":"Local authorities - payments due to deceased officers","desc":"A local authority may make certain payments to the family of deceased officers in certain circumstances without seeing a grant of probate or letters of administration.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2142"},{"id":"2140","label":"Local authorities - placing staff at the disposal of other authorities","desc":"A local authority may enter into an agreement with another local authority or other defined public bodies for the placing at the disposal of the latter for the purposes of their functions, on such terms as may be provided by the agreement, of the services of officers employed by the former, but shall not enter into any such agreement with respect to any officer without consulting him.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2140"},{"id":"2141","label":"Local authorities - security to be taken in relation to officers","desc":"A local authority must take securities in relation to certain officers to be entrusted with money and may takes securities in respect of other officers.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2141"},{"id":"2924","label":"Local authority - code of practice for publicity","desc":"A local authority must take account of Codes of Practice regarding publicity published by the Secretary of State and comply with any compliance orders made","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2924"},{"id":"2879","label":"Local authority - commercial trading","desc":"A local authority as a best value authority is authorised to do for a commercial purpose anything which it is authorised to do for the purpose of carrying on any of its ordinary functions.(2) Before exercising the power conferred by paragraph (1), the authority shall\u2014(a) prepare a business case in support of the proposed exercise of that power; and(b) approve that business case.(3) A best value authority shall recover the costs of any accommodation, goods, services, staff or any other thing that it supplies to a company in pursuance of any agreement or arrangement to facilitate the exercise of the power conferred by paragraph (1).","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2879"},{"id":"3031","label":"Local authority - complaints procedure regarding language (England)","desc":"A local authority must have a complaints procedure for dealing with complaints regarding an alleged breach of the Section 77 duty and must have regard to the code of practice under section 80 applicable to that Authority when so doing.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3031"},{"id":"3033","label":"Local authority - complaints procedure regarding language (Wales)","desc":"A local authority must have a complaints procedure for dealing with complaints regarding an alleged breach of the Section 77 duty and must have regard to the code of practice under section 80 applicable to that Authority when so doing.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3033"},{"id":"3053","label":"Local authority - contracting out of functions","desc":"A local authority may contract out its functions to the extent allowed for by ministerial order.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/3053"},{"id":"2614","label":"Local authority - discharge of functions","desc":"An LA may make arrangements for the discharge of functions, by another LA or an executive of another LA.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2614"},{"id":"3058","label":"Local authority - employee pension scheme","desc":"A local authority must comply with terms of the appropriate public sector pension scheme regulations for its employees.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3058"},{"id":"3059","label":"Local authority - management of pension scheme","desc":"If and where relevant under the terms of the various local authority employee related schemes a local authority must manage the scheme and set up a Pensions Board.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3059"},{"id":"2925","label":"Local authority - mortgagors consent to dispose of interest as mortgagee","desc":"A local authority shall not dispose of their interest as mortgagee of land without the prior written consent of the mortgagor (or, if there is more than one mortgagor, of all of them) specifying the name of the person to whom the interest is to be transferred.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2925"},{"id":"2923","label":"Local authority - prohibition of political publicity","desc":"A local authority shall not publish or arrange for the publication of any material which, in whole or in part, appears to be designed to affect public support for a political party.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2923"},{"id":"2486","label":"Local authority - publicity","desc":"A local authority must comply with a Direction form the Secretary of State to comply with Code of Practice on local authority publicity.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2486"},{"id":"3030","label":"Local authority - spoken English in customer facing roles (England)","desc":"A local authority must ensure that each person who works for the public authority in a customer-facing role speaks fluent English and must have regard to the code of practice under section 80 applicable to that Authority when so doing.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3030"},{"id":"3032","label":"Local authority - spoken English/Welsh in customer facing roles (Wales)","desc":"A local authority must ensure that each person who works for the public authority in a customer-facing role speaks fluent English or Welsh and must have regard to the code of practice under section 80 applicable to that Authority when so doing.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3032"},{"id":"3015","label":"Local authority - transfer of functions","desc":"A local authority must carry out the functions transferred to it by an Order of the Secretary of State.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3015"},{"id":"3590","label":"Local authority library services and businesses - temporary suspension","desc":"A local authority where it is responsible for carrying on a business, not listed in Part 3 of Schedule 2 of the Regulations, of offering goods for sale or for hire in a shop, or providing library services must, during the emergency period:(a) cease to carry on that business or provide that service except by making deliveries or otherwise providing services in response to orders received through a website, or otherwise by on-line communication, by telephone, including orders by text message, or by post(b) close any premises which are not required to carry out its business or provide its services as permitted by sub-paragraph (a)(c) cease to admit any person to its premises who is not required to carry on its business or provide its service as permitted by sub-paragraph (a).","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3590"},{"id":"3656","label":"Local authority meetings - attendance","desc":"A local authority may conduct a meeting which is not limited to all attendees being present in the same place but may allow attendance by electronic, digital or virtual means. Attendance is dependent upon conditions specified in Regulations being met.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/3656"},{"id":"3657","label":"Local authority meetings - notification of meetings","desc":"Where a meeting is scheduled the authority may give notice of the date/time and place of the meeting by publishing such information on its website.
