The place of the meeting may be remote.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/3657"},{"id":"3658","label":"Local authority meetings - public and press access","desc":"A meeting being \u201copen to the public\u201d include access to the meeting through remote means including (but not limited to) video conferencing, live webcast, and live interactive streaming and where a meeting is accessible to the public through such remote means the meeting is open to the public whether or not members of the public are able to attend the meeting in person.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/3658"},{"id":"2934","label":"Local authority meetings - religious/belief observance","desc":"A local authority meeting may make time for religion or belief observance and may support or facilitate a religion or belief event","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2934"},{"id":"3655","label":"Local authority meetings - scheduling","desc":"In respect of a reference in any enactment to a meeting of a local authority, that authority may, as they may determine\u2014(a) hold such meetings and at such hour and on such days; and(b) alter the frequency, move or cancel such meetings, without requirement for further notice.Where an appointment would otherwise be made or require to be made at an annual meeting of a local authority, such appointment continues until the next annual meeting of the authority or until such time as that authority may determine.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/3655"},{"id":"1957","label":"Local authority publicity - separate account of expenditure on publicity","desc":"A local authority shall keep a separate account of their expenditure on publicity, which must be made available for inspections free of charge. Publicity refers to any communication, in whatever form, addressed to the public at large or to a section of the public","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1957"},{"id":"405","label":"Local community - proposals for sustainability","desc":"A local authority may respond to an invitation from the Secretary of State to produce a proposal for sustainable local communities.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/405"},{"id":"3815","label":"Local council tax reduction - amount of reduction","desc":"The amount of council tax which a person is liable to pay in respect of any chargeable dwelling (as determined in accordance with sections 10 to 13) is to be reduced to the extent, if any, required by the authority's council tax reduction scheme.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3815"},{"id":"3818","label":"Local council tax reduction - application of scheme in Wales","desc":"The amount of council tax which a person is liable to pay in respect of any chargeable dwelling (as determined in accordance with sections 10 to 13) is to be reduced to the extent, if any, required by any council tax reduction scheme (made under regulations) that apply to that dwelling.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3818"},{"id":"3816","label":"Local council tax reduction - decision on amount","desc":"The amount of council tax which a person is liable to pay may in any case, be reduced to such extent as the billing authority for the area in which the dwelling is situated thinks fit.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/3816"},{"id":"3819","label":"Local council tax reduction - determination of amount in Wales","desc":"The amount of council tax which a person is liable to pay in respect of any chargeable dwelling may be reduced to such extent as the billing authority for the area in which the dwelling is situated thinks fit.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/3819"},{"id":"3817","label":"Local council tax reduction - duty to make scheme","desc":"Each billing authority in England must make a scheme specifying the reductions which are to apply to amounts of council tax payable, in respect of dwellings situated in its area, by\u2014(a) persons whom the authority considers to be in financial need, or(b) persons in classes consisting of persons whom the authority considers to be, in general, in financial need.in accordance with the requirements Schedule 1A (which contains provisions about council tax reduction schemes).","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3817"},{"id":"63","label":"Local economy - assessment of economic conditions","desc":"A local authority must prepare an assessment of the economic conditions in its area, consult/co-operate with consultation as required by section 69 and have regard to guidance issued by the Secretary of State.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/63"},{"id":"64","label":"Local economy - funding for Economic Prosperity Board","desc":"A local authority must comply with secretary of state's funding order with regard to an Economic Prosperity Board operating within its area where the authority is a constituent council of the Board.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/64"},{"id":"66","label":"Local economy - new Economic Prosperity Board","desc":"Any two or more authorities may prepare and publish a scheme for a new economic prosperity board for their area.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/66"},{"id":"68","label":"Local economy - preparation and publication of scheme","desc":"An authority who has undertaken in review in accordance with section 100 may prepare and publish a scheme to exercise powers to improve economic prosperity for its area.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/68"},{"id":"65","label":"Local economy - review of arrangements","desc":"Any two or more authorities may undertake a review of the effectiveness and efficiency of arrangements to promote economic development and regeneration in their area.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/65"},{"id":"67","label":"Local economy - review of Economic Prosperity Board matters","desc":"In accordance with the framework laid down by section 100 an authority may undertake a review of economic prosperity board matters for their area.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/67"},{"id":"1593","label":"Local government - acquisition and deposit of records","desc":"A local authority may acquire and deposit records.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/1593"},{"id":"2135","label":"Local government - admission to meetings and access to associated documents","desc":"A local authority must allow the general public admission to its meetings, agenda, reports, records, minutes and background papers in certain circumstances.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2135"},{"id":"3903","label":"Local government - alternative mayoral titles","desc":"A local authority may by resolution adopt an alternative title for the mayor in accordance with the requirements of the section.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/3903"},{"id":"2026","label":"Local government - appointment and management etc. of staff","desc":"Every appointment of a person to a paid office or employment under a local authority or parish or community council in England and Wales shall be made on merit.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2026"},{"id":"2127","label":"Local government - appointment of deputy presiding member","desc":"A local authority must appoint a deputy presiding member in circumstances where they have appointed a presiding member","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2127"},{"id":"2126","label":"Local government - appointment of presiding member","desc":"A local authority may appoint a presiding member.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2126"},{"id":"2118","label":"Local government - appointment of vice-chairman in England","desc":"A local authority may appoint a vice chairman and may pay an allowance.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2118"},{"id":"2125","label":"Local government - appointment of vice-chairman in Wales","desc":"A local authority may appoint a vice chairman.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2125"},{"id":"1024","label":"Local government - area committees (Wales)","desc":"A local authority in Wales must comply with regulations relating to the discharge of their functions by area committees.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1024"},{"id":"2137","label":"Local government - arrangements for discharge of functions by committees or by another local authority","desc":"A local authority may make arrangements for the discharge of its functions by committees or by another local authority.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2137"},{"id":"2801","label":"Local government - audit of smaller authorities","desc":"Smaller local authorities may opt in to arrangements made by the Secretary of State to audit their accounts. They may also certify themselves as \u201cexempt authorities\u201d if they meet the prescribed provisions.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2801"},{"id":"2136","label":"Local government - availability of documents to members","desc":"A local authority must allow members access to its documents in certain circumstances.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2136"},{"id":"2173","label":"Local government - byelaws","desc":"A local authority may make or may revoke byelaws for its area in certain circumstances which may include powers of seizure and fixed penalty notices.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2173"},{"id":"1084","label":"Local government - case tribunals","desc":"A local authority must consider recommendations made by case tribunals and take other steps.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1084"},{"id":"2133","label":"Local government - casual vacancies","desc":"An authority must follow designated procedures regarding filling casual vacancies for chairman or councillors and the term of office of persons filling casual vacancies.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2133"},{"id":"1049","label":"Local government - change of governance arrangements","desc":"A local authority may change from one form of governance to another or make other variations.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/1049"},{"id":"2131","label":"Local government - change of name by resolution","desc":"A local authority may change the name of its area by resolution.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2131"},{"id":"1081","label":"Local government - code of conduct for members","desc":"A local authority must adopt a code of conduct for members and comply with the same.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1081"},{"id":"3870","label":"Local government - Combined County Authorities","desc":"A local authority must comply with Regulations designed to combine it with one or more other local authorities into a Combined County Authority.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3870"},{"id":"1047","label":"Local government - committee system","desc":"A local authority must comply with regulations regarding the operation of the committee system.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1047"},{"id":"2616","label":"Local government - committee system rules","desc":"Local authorities operating the committee system under Part 1A of the Local Government Act 2000 must follow prescribed rules which include the functions that cannot be delegated by a committee system local authority and therefore must be carried out by the full council of the local authority and which cannot be delegated to any officer, committee or sub-committee of the authority. The rules also deal with overview and scrutiny committees within committee system local authorities","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2616"},{"id":"2027","label":"Local government - conflict of interest in staff negotiations","desc":"It shall be the duty of a local authority to secure that, so far as practicable, the interests of that authority in any negotiations with respect to the terms and conditions on which persons in local authority employment hold office or are employed are never represented, whether directly or indirectly by, or by persons who include a person who is both a member of the authority and in such employment; or a person who is both a member of the authority and an official or employee of a trade union whose members include persons in local authority employment.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2027"},{"id":"2130","label":"Local government - consideration of result of community poll","desc":"A local authority must provide a response and explanation for its response to a community poll in certain circumstances.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2130"},{"id":"2121","label":"Local government - constitution and membership of London borough councils","desc":"The constitution and membership of the council of a London borough must comply with regulations.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2121"},{"id":"2116","label":"Local government - constitution of councils in England","desc":"A local authority shall consist of a chairman and councillors and will carry out the functions vested in them.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2116"},{"id":"2123","label":"Local government - constitution of councils in Wales","desc":"A local authority shall consist of a chairman and councillors and will carry out the functions vested in them.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2123"},{"id":"2617","label":"local government - council tax increase referendum","desc":"A local authority must follow rules prescribed regarding referendums relating to the question of whether a council tax increase set by an authority \u2013 a billing authority, a major precepting authority, or a local precepting authority \u2013 for a financial year is approved of.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2617"},{"id":"2767","label":"Local government - credit arrangements and capital receipts","desc":"A local authority must comply with Regulations relating to credit arrangements and capital receipts.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2767"},{"id":"2170","label":"Local government - custody of documents","desc":"A local authority shall make proper arrangements for the custody of documents in their possession and must comply with provisions relating to inspection and copying.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2170"},{"id":"2132","label":"Local government - declaration of vacancy in office","desc":"A local authority must declare a vacancy in office in certain circumstances.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2132"},{"id":"1087","label":"Local government - delegation of monitoring officer functions","desc":"A monitoring officer of a local authority must delegate certain functions in certain circumstances.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1087"},{"id":"2023","label":"Local government - designation and reports of head of paid service","desc":"It shall be the duty of every relevant authority to designate one of their officers as the head of their paid service and to provide that officer with such staff, accommodation and other resources as are, in his opinion, sufficient to allow his duties to be performed. It shall be the duty of a relevant authority to consider any report by the head of their paid service at a meeting held not more than three months after copies of the report are first sent to members of the authority.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2023"},{"id":"2024","label":"Local government - designation and reports of monitoring officer","desc":"It shall be the duty of every relevant authority to designate one of their officers as the monitoring officer and provide that officer with such staff, accommodation and other resources as are, in his opinion, sufficient to allow those duties to be performed. It shall be the duty of a relevant authority to consider any report by a monitoring officer or his deputy at a meeting held not more than twenty-one days after copies of the report are first sent to members of the authority.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2024"},{"id":"1063","label":"Local government - discharge of function of and by another local authority","desc":"A local authority in Wales must comply with regulations relating to the discharge of their functions by another local authority.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1063"},{"id":"1033","label":"Local government - discharge of functions by others","desc":"A local authority when adopting executive arrangements may allow others to discharge its functions in accordance with regulations.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/1033"},{"id":"2618","label":"Local government - elected mayor","desc":"A local authority must hold an election for a mayor according to the prescribed rules and for the term prescribed. It must also appoint casual vacancies according to prescribed rules.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2618"},{"id":"2117","label":"Local government - election of chairman in England","desc":"A local authority shall elect a Chairman following a certain procedure and may pay an allowance.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2117"},{"id":"2124","label":"Local government - election of chairman in Wales","desc":"A local authority shall elect a chairman following a certain procedure.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2124"},{"id":"1086","label":"Local government - employee code of conduct","desc":"A local authority must comply with prescribed requirements for a code of conduct for employees.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1086"},{"id":"2953","label":"Local Government - Enforcement of covenant relating to land","desc":"A local Authority may enforce certain covenants relating to land in certain circumstances.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2953"},{"id":"1068","label":"Local government - exclusion of confidential and exempt information from reports","desc":"A local authority in Wales must, when its overview and scrutiny committee publish certain reports, exclude confidential information and may exclude exempt information.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1068"},{"id":"1041","label":"Local government - exclusion of exempt and confidential information from published reports","desc":"A local authority must, when its overview and scrutiny committee publish certain reports, exclude confidential information and may exclude exempt information.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1041"},{"id":"2633","label":"Local government - executive arrangements","desc":"Where LAs are operating executive arrangements under Part 1A of the Local Government Act 2000 their executive and committee meetings must be held in public and the public must be excluded from meetings in prescribed circumstances and in accordance with the prescribed formalities. LAs must follow the specific requirements and publicity requirements relating to executive decisions which are key decisions.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2633"},{"id":"1676","label":"Local government - financial assistance to district and parish councils","desc":"A county council may provide financial assistance towards expenditure to a district or parish council in its area.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/1676"},{"id":"1042","label":"Local government - flood risk management by overview and scrutiny committee","desc":"A local authority which is a lead flood authority must refer such matters to its overview and scrutiny committee in certain circumstances.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1042"},{"id":"1053","label":"Local government - general provisions for change of governance arrangements","desc":"A local authority wishing to change its governance arrangements must comply with certain general provisions.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1053"},{"id":"2022","label":"Local government - grant and supervision of exemptions from political restriction in England","desc":"Every local authority must give the head of paid service all such information as he reasonably requires for the purpose of carrying out its functions in relation to political restriction and to comply with any direction in respect of the maintained list of politically restricted posts.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2022"},{"id":"2021","label":"Local government - grant and supervision of exemptions from political restriction in Wales","desc":"Wales It shall be the duty of a local authority to give a person appointed to carry out the functions in relation to political restriction all such information as he reasonably requires for the purpose of carrying out his functions and to comply with any direction in respect of the maintained list of politically restricted posts.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2021"},{"id":"2129","label":"Local government - grouping or dissolution of community councils","desc":"A local authority may in certain circumstances establish, group, separate or dissolve community councils.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2129"},{"id":"2122","label":"Local government - grouping or dissolving of parish councils","desc":"A local authority may in certain circumstances group parish councils or dissolve a parish council into smaller parishes.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2122"},{"id":"1055","label":"Local government - guidance for change of governance arrangements","desc":"A local authority must in formulating or changing its governance arrangements comply with guidance from the Secretary of State.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1055"},{"id":"1051","label":"Local government - implementation of change of governance arrangements","desc":"A local authority wishing to change its governance arrangements must implement the same in the prescribed manner.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1051"},{"id":"1071","label":"Local government - implementation of proposals for executive arrangements","desc":"A local authority in Wales must implement proposals where no referendum is required in accordance with the published timetable.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1071"},{"id":"1028","label":"Local government - indemnification of members and officers of relevant authorities","desc":"A local authority must comply with regulations regarding member and officer indemnities.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1028"},{"id":"2632","label":"Local government - information for overview and scrutiny","desc":"LA overview and scrutiny committees may obtain information from their relevant partner authorities, and ensure that executives of LA exclude confidential information when publishing their responses to reports and recommendations of overview and scrutiny committees.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2632"},{"id":"1034","label":"Local government - joint discharge of functions","desc":"A local authority when adopting executive arrangements may jointly discharge its functions in accordance with regulations.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/1034"},{"id":"1064","label":"Local government - joint exercise of functions","desc":"A local authority in Wales must comply with Regulations relating to the joint exercise of their functions.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1064"},{"id":"2670","label":"Local government - joint overview and scrutiny","desc":"Two or more local authorities may appoint a joint overview and scrutiny committee to make reports or recommendations to any of the authorities or their executives about matters affecting their areas and if so must comply with the administrative requirements contained in the Regulations.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2670"},{"id":"1056","label":"Local government - local authority executives","desc":"A local authority in Wales must adopt one of the permitted forms of government.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1056"},{"id":"1059","label":"Local government - mayor and cabinet executive","desc":"A local authority in Wales adopting executive arrangements consisting of a mayor and cabinet executive must accord with section 14.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1059"},{"id":"1061","label":"Local government - mayor and council manager executive","desc":"A local authority in Wales adopting executive arrangements consisting of a mayor and council manager must accord with section 16.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1061"},{"id":"2134","label":"Local government - meetings and proceedings","desc":"The meetings and proceedings of a local authority must comply with Schedule 12 of the Local Government Act 1972.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2134"},{"id":"1083","label":"Local government - monitoring officer","desc":"A local authority must refer certain matters to its monitoring officer for investigation.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1083"},{"id":"2025","label":"Local government - officer responsible for financial administration of certain authorities","desc":"On and after the commencement day the Common Council shall make arrangements for the proper administration of such of its financial affairs as relate to it in its capacity as a local authority, police authority or port health authority, and secure that one of its officers has responsibility for the administration of those affairs.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2025"},{"id":"1073","label":"Local government - outline fall back proposals for executive arrangements","desc":"A local authority in Wales may apply to Welsh ministers for the approval of outline fall back proposals.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/1073"},{"id":"2629","label":"Local Government - overview and scrutiny","desc":"A local authority cannot refer to an overview and scrutiny committee the excluded matters specified in article 3, but can refer a matter which consists of an allegation of systemic failure of a LA to discharge a function for which the LA is responsible, notwithstanding the fact that the allegation specifies matters which would otherwise be excluded by virtue of article 3.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2629"},{"id":"1035","label":"Local government - overview and scrutiny committee","desc":"A local authority when adopting executive arrangements must include provision for an overview and scrutiny committee.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1035"},{"id":"1065","label":"Local government - overview and scrutiny committees","desc":"A local authority in Wales must ensure that executive arrangements provide for one or more overview and scrutiny committees.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1065"},{"id":"1036","label":"Local government - overview and scrutiny sub-committees","desc":"The overview and scrutiny committee of a local authority may appoint sub-committees.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/1036"},{"id":"1591","label":"Local government - payment of officer expenses","desc":"A local authority may pay its officers' expenses.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/1591"},{"id":"1748","label":"Local government - payments to dependants under superannuation schemes","desc":"A local authority may make payments from its superannuation fund to the dependants of employees killed in or as a result of military service.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/1748"},{"id":"2028","label":"Local government - political balance on committees, duty to allocate seats to political groups","desc":"It shall be the duty of a relevant authority having power from time to time to make appointments to a body to which this section applies to review the representation of different political groups on that body","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2028"},{"id":"2020","label":"Local government - political restriction of officers and staff","desc":"It shall be the duty of every local authority to prepare and maintain a list of politically restricted posts and deposit that list prepared with their proper officer and to revise that list as and when necessary","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2020"},{"id":"2634","label":"Local government - post election surveys","desc":"A local authority must conduct a survey after each ordinary election to the council of the county or county borough and to each community in the local authority's area by asking prescribed questions of councillors and unsuccessful candidates who have stood for election as councillors in the local authority's area. The questions relate to gender, sexual orientation, language, race, age, disability, religion or belief, health, education and qualifications, employment, work as a councillor, party affiliation, involvement with the third sector and length of political activity. Survey information must be collated in an electronic spreadsheet. Details relating to the spreadsheet will be included in guidance.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2634"},{"id":"1080","label":"Local government - principles governing conduct of members","desc":"A local authority in Wales must comply with principals governing the conduct of members.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1080"},{"id":"2599","label":"Local government - procurement","desc":"Certain bodies may submit an expression of interest in providing services on behalf of specified authorities in the exercise of any of those relevant authorities\u2019 functions under powers contained in Chapter 2 of Part 5 of the Localism Act 2011. Fire authorities are added to the list of relevant authorities and may specify prescribed grounds on which an expression of interest may be rejected.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2599"},{"id":"1592","label":"Local government - promotion of adequate use of records","desc":"A local authority may take steps to make adequate use of its records by promoting the same in various ways.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/1592"},{"id":"1070","label":"Local government - proposals for executive arrangements","desc":"A local authority in Wales must draw up and publicise its proposals for executive arrangements in the prescribed manner.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1070"},{"id":"1043","label":"Local government - provision of information to another authority with executive arrangements","desc":"A local authority must provide certain information to another authority with executive arrangements in certain circumstances.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1043"},{"id":"2809","label":"Local government - public contracts","desc":"Local authorities (as contracting authorities) must have regard to the regulations in relation to how they award public contracts for the execution of works, the supply of products or the provision of services.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2809"},{"id":"2681","label":"Local government - public health functions","desc":"Local authorities must exercise prescribed public health functions in their area including arranging the weighing and measuring of certain children, health checks for eligible persons, access to sexual health services, a public health advice service to any clinical commissioning groups in their area, health protection arrangements against any threat to the health of the local population, including infectious disease, environmental hazards and extreme weather events. A local authority may make and recover charges in respect of certain steps taken in the exercise of its duty as to health improvement, but not in respect of anything which the local authority is required to do in exercise of its prescribed public health functions.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2681"},{"id":"2739","label":"Local government - records","desc":"A local authoriy decision-making officer must produce a written record of any category of prescribed decision as soon as reasonably practicable after the decision making officer has made the decision and must contain prescribed information. The local authority must publicise the decision (unless it contains confidential or exempt information) as prescribed.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2739"},{"id":"2685","label":"Local government - recoupment of education costs","desc":"A local authority must pay and claim recoupment of money as prescribed where a person belonging to the area of one authority (\u201cthe home authority\u201d) in England is educated by another authority (\u201cthe providing authority\u201d) in England or Wales.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2685"},{"id":"1075","label":"Local government - referendum following petition, direction or order","desc":"A local authority in Wales must comply with regulations requiring a referendum.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1075"},{"id":"2565","label":"Local government - referendum on governance","desc":"An LA must hold a referendum on whether a local authority should change to a different form of governance if a valid petition is received with the support of at least 5% of the local government electors in the authority's area.The LA must follow the prescribed procedure including giving public notice of notices received and any referendum to be held.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2565"},{"id":"1072","label":"Local government - referendum on proposals for executive arrangements","desc":"A local authority in Wales whose proposals include an elected mayor must hold a referendum and take other steps in accordance with section 27.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1072"},{"id":"1052","label":"Local government - referendum regarding change of governance arrangements","desc":"A local authority wishing to change its governance arrangements must in certain circumstances hold a referendum.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1052"},{"id":"1038","label":"Local government - referral arrangements for overview and scrutiny committee","desc":"A local authority when adopting executive arrangements must adopt certain referral arrangements regarding its overview and scrutiny committee.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1038"},{"id":"1077","label":"Local government - regard to guidance (Wales)","desc":"A local authority in Wales must have regard to guidance issued by the Welsh Ministers.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1077"},{"id":"1085","label":"Local government - register of members interests","desc":"A local authority must maintain and disclose a register of members' interests.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1085"},{"id":"2171","label":"Local government - reports and returns","desc":"A local authority must comply with requests from the Secretary of State for reports and returns.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2171"},{"id":"2029","label":"Local government - requirements for companies/Trusts under control or subject to influence of local authorities","desc":"It shall be the duty of every local authority to ensure, so far as practicable, that any company/Trust under its control complies with any provisions made by the Secretary of State","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2029"},{"id":"1074","label":"Local government - resolution and publicity for executive arrangements","desc":"A local authority in Wales must pass an appropriate resolution and comply with publicity requirements before executive arrangements can operate.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1074"},{"id":"1050","label":"Local government - resolution for change of governance arrangements","desc":"A local authority wishing to change its governance arrangements must comply with the prescribed procedure for passing resolution.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1050"},{"id":"1039","label":"Local government - responding to overview and scrutiny committee","desc":"A local authority or its executive must respond to its overview and scrutiny committee in certain circumstances.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1039"},{"id":"1040","label":"Local government - response by partner authority to overview and scrutiny committee","desc":"A local authority must respond to the overview and scrutiny committee of a partner authority in certain circumstances.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1040"},{"id":"1067","label":"Local government - response to overview and scrutiny committee","desc":"A local authority in Wales or its executive must respond to certain matters reviewed by its overview and scrutiny committees.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1067"},{"id":"1048","label":"Local government - review of flood risk function in committee system","desc":"A local authority with a committee system which is a lead local flood authority must review and scrutinise flood risk functions and may take certain steps.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1048"},{"id":"3911","label":"Local Government - risk management directions","desc":"A local authority must comply with risk management directions given by the Secretary of State.The following are \u201crisk-mitigation directions\u201d\u2014(a)a direction that sets limits in relation to the borrowing of money by the local authority;(b)a direction that requires the local authority to take action specified in the direction.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3911"},{"id":"1037","label":"Local government - scrutiny officers","desc":"A local authority when adopting executive arrangements must designate an officer to promote, support and guide the overview and scrutiny committee and other members of the authority.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1037"},{"id":"2172","label":"Local government - service of public notices","desc":"A local authority must serve public notices in the manner prescribed.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2172"},{"id":"1082","label":"Local government - standards committee","desc":"A local authority must establish a standards committee.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1082"},{"id":"2115","label":"Local government - supply of and use of goods and services","desc":"Subject to certain limitations a local authority may enter into an agreement for all or any of the following purposes (a) the supply by the authority to the body of any goods or materials; (b) the provision by the authority for the body of any administrative, professional or technical services; (c) the use by the body of any vehicle, plant or apparatus belonging to the authority, the placing at the disposal of the body of the services of any person employed in connection with the vehicle or other property in question; and (d) the carrying out by the authority of works of maintenance in connection with land or buildings for the maintenance of which the body is responsible.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2115"},{"id":"2120","label":"Local government - terms of office and retirement of councillors in England","desc":"A local authority must comply with the requirements of section 6 and 7 of of the Local Government Act 1972 with regard to election of, terms of office and retirement of councillors.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2120"},{"id":"2128","label":"Local government - terms of office and retirement of councillors in Wales","desc":"A local authority must comply with the requirements of section 25 of the Local Government Act 1972 with regard to election of, terms of office and retirement of councillors.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2128"},{"id":"1079","label":"Local government - timing of elections","desc":"A local authority in Wales must comply with regulations regarding the timing of elections.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1079"},{"id":"2803","label":"Local government - transparency","desc":"Local authorities in England must comply with Part 2 of the Local Government Transparency Code 2015 .","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2803"},{"id":"2161","label":"Local Government associations - subscriptions","desc":"A local authority may pay reasonable subscriptions, whether annually or otherwise, to the funds of any association of local authorities formed (whether inside or outside the United Kingdom) for the purpose of consultation as to the common interests of those authorities and the discussion of matters relating to local government, or of any association of officers or members of local authorities which was so formed.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2161"},{"id":"1031","label":"Local government England - permitted forms of government","desc":"A local authority must adopt one of the permitted forms of government.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1031"},{"id":"2757","label":"Local government finance - accounts","desc":"Local authorities must follow detailed rules for the preparation, approval and publication of their statement of accounts.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2757"},{"id":"1978","label":"Local government finance - revenue support grant England","desc":"Where the sum shown by the relevant calculation (in an amending report) as falling to be paid to a receiving authority for the financial year concerned is less than that shown as falling to be paid to it by the relevant previous calculation, a sum equal to the difference shall be paid by the authority to the Secretary of State.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1978"},{"id":"1979","label":"Local government finance - revenue support grant Wales","desc":"The Welsh Ministers shall calculate what sum, if any, falls to be paid to each receiving authority by way of revenue support grant for the year in accordance with the basis of distribution agreed. Where the Welsh Ministers make a calculation that shows a decrease in the sum that falls to be paid to a receiving authority, the authority shall pay to the Welsh Ministers a sum equal to the difference.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1979"},{"id":"1044","label":"Local government in England - access to information and record keeping","desc":"A local authority must comply with certain steps regarding access to information and record keeping.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1044"},{"id":"1045","label":"Local government in England - elected mayors","desc":"A local authority wishing to have an elected mayor must comply with regulations regarding elected mayors.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1045"},{"id":"1032","label":"Local government in England - executive arrangements","desc":"A local authority when adopting executive arrangements must ensure that they are as prescribed.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1032"},{"id":"1046","label":"Local government in England - leader and cabinet executive","desc":"A local authority operating executive arrangements that provide for a leader and cabinet executive must include certain provisions regarding the executive leader and may include other provisions.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1046"},{"id":"1054","label":"Local government in England - preparation and maintenance of constitution","desc":"A local authority must prepare and keep up to date a constitution.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1054"},{"id":"1069","label":"Local government in Wales - access to information and record keeping","desc":"A local authority in Wales must comply with certain steps regarding access to information and record keeping.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1069"},{"id":"1078","label":"Local government in Wales - elected mayors","desc":"A local authority in Wales must comply with certain prescribed steps with regard to elected mayors and comply with regulations if made.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1078"},{"id":"1057","label":"Local government in Wales - executive arrangements","desc":"A local authority in Wales adopting executive arrangements must ensure that they are as prescribed.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1057"},{"id":"1060","label":"Local government in Wales - leader and cabinet executive","desc":"A local authority in Wales adopting executive arrangements consisting of a leader and cabinet executive must accord with section 15.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1060"},{"id":"1076","label":"Local government in Wales - preparation and maintenance of constitution","desc":"A local authority in Wales must prepare, keep up to date and make available a document regarding their constitution.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1076"},{"id":"3671","label":"Local government re-organisation - Plans, reviews, schemes etc.","desc":"Each preparing council which is a county council and each shadow council shall prepare for the whole of its area, and if required by the enactment concerned publish plans, reviews, schemes, statements and strategies as detailed in Regulations.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3671"},{"id":"1066","label":"Local government reference of matter to overview and scrutiny committee","desc":"A local authority in Wales must refer certain matters to its overview and scrutiny committees.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1066"},{"id":"2158","label":"Local information - research and collection","desc":"A local authority may conduct, or assist in the conducting of, investigations into, and the collection of information relating to, any matters concerning the county or any part of the county.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2158"},{"id":"2159","label":"Local information - submission to Minister on request","desc":"A local authority must comply with a request from the Secretary of State to provide him with any information collected.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2159"},{"id":"1523","label":"Local land charges - compensation","desc":"A local authority must pay compensation in certain cases of non-registration or defective official search","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1523"},{"id":"1520","label":"Local land charges - general charge","desc":"A local authority may register a general charge with the Chief Land Registrar against land in certain circumstances.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/1520"},{"id":"1522","label":"Local land charges - official search of register","desc":"A local authority must allow an official search of the register following payment of the prescribed fee.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1522"},{"id":"1521","label":"Local land charges - personal search of register","desc":"A local authority must allow a personal search of the register following payment of the prescribed fee.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1521"},{"id":"1518","label":"Local land charges - register and index","desc":"A local authority must keep a local land charges register and a local land charges register, which may be in electronic form.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1518"},{"id":"1519","label":"Local land charges - registration","desc":"A local authority must as respects a local land charge apply to the Chief Land Registrar for its registration in the local land charges register.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1519"},{"id":"1525","label":"Local land charges - rules","desc":"A local authority must comply with rules prescribed by the Lord Chancellor when carrying out its functions under the Local Land Charges Act 1975.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1525"},{"id":"1524","label":"Local land charges - specification of fees","desc":"A local authority must specify and publish its fees relating to land charges and have regard to guidance when so doing.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1524"},{"id":"1163","label":"Local transport plans","desc":"A local authority must develop and carry out policies for the promotion and encouragement of safe, integrated, efficient and economic transport to, from and within their area.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1163"},{"id":"1165","label":"Local transport plans - approval of plans","desc":"A local authority in Wales must submit their transport plan to the National Assembly for approval and amend the same if required.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1165"},{"id":"1167","label":"Local transport plans - modification order and directions","desc":"A local authority in Wales must comply with a modification order or Directions made by the National assembly with regard to its transport plans.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1167"},{"id":"1164","label":"Local transport plans - review and alteration in England","desc":"A local authority must keep their transport plan under review and alter the same where required and consult where required.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1164"},{"id":"1166","label":"Local transport plans - review and alteration in Wales","desc":"A local authority in Wales must keep its transport plan under review and alter the same as required. It must also take such other steps as are required.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1166"},{"id":"3843","label":"London Mayor or Assembly member - disqualification due to sexual offences etc.","desc":"A person is disqualified from being elected or being the Mayor or an Assembly member in the Greater London Authority if the person is subject to:(a) any relevant notification requirements, or(b) a relevant order.Where that notification or order is in relation to sexual offences etc. and is given or made on or after 28 June 2022.The terms for disqualification are defined by section 21A.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3843"},{"id":"1694","label":"Long distance routes - provision of facilities","desc":"A local authority whose area includes a long distance route may provide facilities for accommodation, meals and refreshments.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/1694"},{"id":"1693","label":"Long-distance routes - ferry services","desc":"A local authority may establish a ferry service to connect a long distance route where it crosses water.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/1693"},{"id":"1996","label":"Looked after children - additional functions of the responsible authority","desc":"It is the duty of each local authority to take reasonable steps to keep in touch with a relevant child for whom they are the responsible authority, whether he is within their area or not; to appoint a personal adviser for each relevant child; and to carry out an assessment of his needs (where there is not already a pathway plan) with a view to determining what advice, assistance and support it would be appropriate for them to provide","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1996"},{"id":"2529","label":"Looked after children - admission to school","desc":"A school governing body as admissions authority and a local authority where it is the admissions authority must comply with the Regulations with regard to the admissions of looked after children to school.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2529"},{"id":"2005","label":"Looked after children - appointment of independent reviewing officer","desc":"If a local authority are looking after a child, they must appoint an individual as the independent reviewing officer for that child's case.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2005"},{"id":"1992","label":"Looked after children - children's homes provided by appropriate national authority","desc":"Where a local authority place a child they are looking after in a children's home provided, equipped and maintained by an appropriate national authority, they must do so on such terms as that national authority may from time to time determine.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1992"},{"id":"3226","label":"Looked after children - designated person for former looked after pupils (academy)","desc":"An academy must designate a member of the staff at the school (the \u201cdesignated person\u201d) as having responsibility for promoting the educational achievement of registered pupils formerly within state care and ensure that the designated person undertakes appropriate training and has regard to any guidance issued by the Secretary of State.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3226"},{"id":"3228","label":"Looked after children - designated person for former looked after pupils (maintained school)","desc":"A Governing Body of a maintained school must designate a member of the staff at the school (the \u201cdesignated person\u201d) as having responsibility for promoting the educational achievement of registered pupils formerly within state care and ensure that the designated person undertakes appropriate training and has regard to any guidance issued by the Secretary of State.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3228"},{"id":"2528","label":"Looked after children - designated teacher","desc":"A school governing body must ensure that the designated teacher for looked after pupils meets with the requirements of Regulation 3.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2528"},{"id":"1997","label":"Looked after children - functions in respect of former relevant children","desc":"Each local authority shall have the duties towards a person who has been a relevant child and a person who was being looked after by them when he attained the age of eighteen, and a former relevant child. This includes children who have been detained or who are in hospital who were previously looked after.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1997"},{"id":"1988","label":"Looked after children - general duty of local authority","desc":"It shall be the duty of a local authority looking after any child to safeguard and promote his welfare; and to make such use of services available for children cared for by their own parents as appears to the authority reasonable in his case.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1988"},{"id":"2000","label":"Looked after children - independent visitors","desc":"A local authority looking after a child must appoint an independent person to be the child's visitor in prescribed circumstances","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2000"},{"id":"3105","label":"Looked after children - independent visitors (Wales)","desc":"In Wales where it appears to a local authority in relation to any child that they are looking after that communication between the child and a parent of his, or any person who is not a parent of his but who has parental responsibility for him, has been infrequent; or he has not visited or been visited by (or lived with) any such person during the preceding twelve months,and that it would be in the child's best interests for an independent person to be appointed to be his visitor for the purposes of this paragraph, they shall appoint such a visitor.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3105"},{"id":"3769","label":"Looked after children - information regarding child trust funds","desc":"When required to do so by regulations or by authorised officers of the Inland Revenue an authority must make documents available for inspection on behalf of the Inland Revenue or by a person appointed under regulations, ormust provide to the Inland Revenue or to such a person any information which the Inland Revenue or (as the case may be) the person may require for the discharge of any function relating to child trust funds.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3769"},{"id":"3106","label":"Looked after children - living outside England and Wales","desc":"A local authority may, with the approval of every person who has parental responsibility for the child arrange for, or assist in arranging for, any other child looked after by them to live outside England and Wales.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/3106"},{"id":"1990","label":"Looked after children - maintenance","desc":"It is the duty of a local authority to maintain a child they are looking after in other respects apart from the provision of accommodation.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1990"},{"id":"1998","label":"Looked after children - needs assessment and pathway plan","desc":"It is the duty of the responsible local authority to appoint a personal adviser for a former relevant child and to assess their needs and prepare a pathway plan.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1998"},{"id":"3109","label":"Looked after children - notification of death","desc":"If a child who is being looked after by a local authority dies, the authority shall notify the appropriate national authority and shall, so far as is reasonably practicable, notify the child's parents and every person who is not a parent of his but who has parental responsibility for him.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3109"},{"id":"3760","label":"Looked after children - other children living outside England and Wales","desc":"A local authority may, with the approval of every person who has parental responsibility for the child arrange for, or assist in arranging for, any other child looked after by them to live outside England and Wales.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/3760"},{"id":"3104","label":"Looked after children - payments","desc":"Where a child is being looked after by a local authority the authority may make payments to a parent of the child; any person who is not a parent of his but who has parental responsibility for him; or any relative, friend or other person connected with him, in respect of travelling, subsistence or other expenses incurred by that person in visiting the child.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/3104"},{"id":"3108","label":"Looked after children - personal adviser","desc":"A local authority shall arrange for each child whom they are looking after who is a eligible to have a personal adviser.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3108"},{"id":"3759","label":"Looked after children - placement outside England and Wales","desc":"A local authority may only arrange for, or assist in arranging for, any child in their care to live outside England and Wales with the approval of the court.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3759"},{"id":"1993","label":"Looked after children - promoting contact","desc":"Where a child is being looked after by a local authority Part 2 of Schedule 2 states: the authority shall, where appropriate, endeavour to promote contact between the child and his parents; any person who is not a parent of his but who has parental responsibility for him; and any relative, friend or other person connected with him and keep them informed of where he is being accommodated.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1993"},{"id":"3725","label":"Looked after children - prospective adopters","desc":"The local authority has a duty to consider fostering for adoption as part of the care planning process to achieve permanence for a looked after child","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3725"},{"id":"1989","label":"Looked after children - provision of accommodation","desc":"When a child is in the care of a local authority, it is their duty to provide the child with accommodation.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1989"},{"id":"1995","label":"Looked after children - provision of accommodation and maintenance by local authority","desc":"It shall be the duty of any local authority looking after a child when he is in their care, to provide accommodation for him; and to maintain him in other respects apart from providing accommodation for him.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1995"},{"id":"1994","label":"Looked after children - securing of sufficient accommodation","desc":"It is the general duty of a local authority to take steps that secure, so far as reasonably practicable, to provide the children with accommodation that is within the authority's area; and meets the needs of those children","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1994"},{"id":"2579","label":"Looked after children - visits","desc":"The LA\u2019s representative must visit an unassessed accommodated child (in private) within 7 days of a notification under S.85(1) of the 1989 Act and at 6 monthly intervals (maximum) thereafter. Where a child\u2019s needs have been assessed within the 12 months up to the notification, the LA\u2019s representative must visit the child within 3 months and at 6 monthly intervals (maximum) afterwards. A LA\u2019s representative must visit whenever reasonably requested by the child or if necessary to safeguard the child\u2019 welfare and write a report of the visit containing prescribed information.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2579"},{"id":"2561","label":"Looked after children - visits in detention","desc":"LAs must visit children who have ceased to be looked after by them as a result of prescribed circumstances (under section 23ZA of the 1989 Act) in the frequency and manner prescribed and provide a report on such visits.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2561"},{"id":"2571","label":"Looked after children - visits in detention (Wales)","desc":"A LA must ensure that children who have ceased to be looked after by it and that are detained are visited by a representative of the LA in private within ten working days of the child first being detained and thereafter whenever reasonably requested to do so by specified persons, for example, the child and that they have access to advice, support and assistance. The representative must provide a report of each visit including prescribed details and provide a copy to the child","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2571"},{"id":"1999","label":"Looked after children - visits to, and contact with, looked after children and others","desc":"It is the duty of the local authority to ensure that a looked after child is visited by a representative of the authority; to arrange for appropriate advice, support and assistance to be available","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1999"},{"id":"1991","label":"Looked after children - ways to be accommodated and maintained","desc":"Where it is appropriate, the local authority must make arrangements for a looked after child to live with: a parent; a person with parental responsibility; or where a child is in the care of the local authority and there was a residence order in force immediately before the care order was made, a person in whose favour the residence order was made.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1991"},{"id":"3107","label":"Looked after children - welfare after leaving care","desc":"It is the duty of the local authority looking after a child to advise, assist and befriend him with a view to promoting his welfare when they have ceased to look after him.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3107"},{"id":"2014","label":"Looked after children and child welfare - provision of community homes","desc":"Every local authority shall make such arrangements as they consider appropriate for securing that community homes are available for the care and accommodation of children looked after by them; and for purposes connected with the welfare of children (whether or not looked after by them), and may do so jointly with one or more other local authorities.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2014"},{"id":"3250","label":"Lord Lieutenant - appointment","desc":"Her majesty must appoint a Lord Lieutenant (or acting Lord Lieutenant) for every County in England and Wales.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3250"},{"id":"3254","label":"Lord Lieutenant - appointment of clerk","desc":"A Lord Lieutenant shall appoint and may revoke the appointment of a clerk","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3254"},{"id":"3252","label":"Lord Lieutenant - appointment of deputy","desc":"A Lord Lieutenant must appoint one or more Deputy Lieutenants","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3252"},{"id":"3253","label":"Lord Lieutenant - appointment of Vice Lord Lieutenant","desc":"A Lord Lieutenant may with Her Majesty\u2019s approval appoint a Vice Lord Lieutenant","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/3253"},{"id":"3054","label":"Maintained school - intervention where school causing concern","desc":"The Governing Body of a maintained school must enter into arrangements if directed to do so by the Secretary of State.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3054"},{"id":"112","label":"Marine Conservation Zones - applications which may hinder MCZ objectives","desc":"Where the authority receives an application for authorisation of the doing of an act where there is or may be a significant risk of the act hindering the achievement of the conservation objectives stated for the MCZ, the authority must notify the appropriate statutory conservation body of that fact.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/112"},{"id":"113","label":"Marine Conservation Zones - failure to comply","desc":"A local authority must provide the appropriate statutory conservation body with an explanation for alleged failure to comply with duties.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/113"},{"id":"111","label":"Marine Conservation Zones - furthering conservation objectives","desc":"A local authority must exercise its functions in a way which the authority considers best furthers the conservation objectives stated for the Marine Conservation Zone or where it is not possible to exercise its functions in a manner which furthers those objectives, exercise them in the manner which the authority considers least hinders the achievement of those objectives. If an authority considers that any of its functions is such that the exercise of the function would or might significantly hinder the achievement of the conservation objectives for an MCZ, it must inform the appropriate statutory conservation body of that fact.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/111"},{"id":"110","label":"Marine licensing - delegation of functions","desc":"A local authority must comply with any delegation of functions order in respect of marine licensing.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/110"},{"id":"108","label":"Marine planning - delegation of functions relating to marine plans","desc":"A local authority must comply with directions from a Marine Planning Authority.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/108"},{"id":"109","label":"Marine policy - decisions in accordance with marine policy documents","desc":"A public authority must take any authorisation or enforcement decision in accordance with the appropriate marine policy documents, unless relevant considerations indicate otherwise.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/109"},{"id":"2552","label":"Marine strategy","desc":"Each LA must, in exercising any functions so far as affecting the marine strategy area, have regard to any marine strategy developed under regulation 5.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2552"},{"id":"1500","label":"Markets - appointment of times and charges","desc":"A local authority may, in certain circumstances appoint times and charges for markets.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/1500"},{"id":"3088","label":"Markets - cold stores","desc":"A local authority may provide cold stores at markets","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/3088"},{"id":"2357","label":"Markets - establishment or acquisition","desc":"A local authority may establish a market within [their area] or acquire by agreement (but not otherwise), either by purchase or on lease, the whole or any part of an existing market undertaking within [their area], and any rights enjoyed by any person within [their area] in respect of a market and of tolls, and, in either case, may provide a market place with convenient approaches to it; a market house and other buildings convenient for the holding of a market.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2357"},{"id":"3089","label":"Markets - information from drivers of livestock vehicles","desc":"A local authority officer may obtain certain information from drivers of certain livestock vehicles.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/3089"},{"id":"2358","label":"Markets - market byelaws","desc":"A local authority who maintain a market, whether or not they are a market authority within the meaning of this Act, may make byelaws for regulating the use of the market place, and the buildings, stalls, pens and standings in that market place; for preventing nuisances or obstructions in the market place, or in the immediate approaches to it; for regulating porters and carriers resorting to the market, and fixing the charges to be made for carrying articles from the market within the district.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2358"},{"id":"3086","label":"Markets - market days, hours and charging","desc":"A local authority may determine market days, hours; charge for certain items/services and recover unpaid charges.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/3086"},{"id":"3087","label":"Markets - weighing machines and scales","desc":"A local authority must provide weighing machines and scales in certain circumstances","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3087"},{"id":"2733","label":"Marriage - cancellation of registration of shared buildings","desc":"Local authorities (the Registrar General) must follow prescribed procedures for the cancellation of the registration of buildings which are shared by more than one religious organisation for the solemnization of marriages of same sex couples.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2733"},{"id":"2731","label":"Marriage - conversion of civil partnership","desc":"Local authorities may provide secular services or ceremonies following conversions.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2731"},{"id":"2732","label":"Marriage - registration and appointment for same sex marriage","desc":"Local authorities (the Registrar General and superintendent registrar) must follow the prescribed procedures on registration and cancellation of a building","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2732"},{"id":"3842","label":"Mayor of combined authority - disqualification due to sexual offences etc.","desc":"A person is disqualified from being elected or holding office as a Mayor in a combined authority in England if the person is subject to:(a) any relevant notification requirements, or(b) a relevant order.Where that notification or order is in relation to sexual offences etc. and is given or made on or after 28 June 2022.The terms applying to any disqualification are defined by Schedule 5B.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3842"},{"id":"2483","label":"Meetings - providing live or later access to meetings","desc":"A local authority must comply with Regulations made by the Secretary of State in making provision for and in connection with allowing persons\u2014(a) to film, photograph or make sound recordings of proceedings at a meeting of a body to which this section applies, or of a committee or sub-committee of such a body;(b) to use other means for enabling persons not present at such a meeting to see or hear proceedings at the meeting, as it takes place or later;(c) to report or provide commentary on the proceedings at such a meeting, orally or in writing, so that the report or commentary is available, as the meeting takes place or later, to persons not present at the meeting.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2483"},{"id":"3002","label":"Meetings - religious observance","desc":"The business at a meeting of an English local authority or committee or subcommittee of that Authority may include time for\u2014(a) prayers or other religious observance, or(b) observance connected with a religious or philosophical belief.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/3002"},{"id":"2165","label":"Members - allowances and expenses","desc":"A local authority may pay certain allowances and expenses to Members.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2165"},{"id":"2631","label":"Members - declaration of office","desc":"Local authority members and elected mayors must complete the prescribed declaration of office within two months of election for county, district and London borough.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2631"},{"id":"116","label":"Members - dispensation where pecuniary interest","desc":"An authority may in certain circumstances issue a dispensation allowing a member to take part in a debate or to vote where he or she has a pecuniary interest as per section 31(4) of the Localism Act 2011.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/116"},{"id":"3841","label":"Members - disqualification due to sexual offences etc.","desc":"A person is disqualified for being elected or being a member of a local authority in England if the person is subject to:(a) any relevant notification requirements, or(b) a relevant order.Where that notification or order is given or made on or after 28 June 2022 in relation to sexual offences etc. as defined in section 81A.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3841"},{"id":"365","label":"Members - exercise of any function of a local authority","desc":"A local authority may authorise a councillor for a ward or division to discharge its functions (to the extent allowed) in respect of that ward or division.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/365"},{"id":"114","label":"Members - promote and maintain high standards of conduct","desc":"A relevant authority must promote and maintain high standards of conduct by members and co-opted members of the authority. In discharging its duty as above a relevant authority must, in particular, adopt a code dealing with the conduct that is expected of members and co-opted members of the authority when they are acting in that capacity.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/114"},{"id":"1027","label":"Members - provision about allowances","desc":"A local authority must comply with regulations regarding member's allowances.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1027"},{"id":"115","label":"Members - register of interests","desc":"The monitoring officer of a relevant authority must establish and maintain a register of interests of members and co-opted members of the authority.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/115"},{"id":"2883","label":"Members - written record of decisions and actions","desc":"Where a member of a local authority discharges any function of the authority by virtue of arrangements made under section 236 of the Local Government and Public Involvement in Health Act 2007 (exercise of functions by local councillors in England), that member must\u2014(a) ensure that a record is made in writing of any decision made or action taken in connection with the discharge of that function; and(b) within one month of the date on which the decision is made, or action taken, provide the record to the authority.The authority may also withdraw that exemption by notice.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2883"},{"id":"2350","label":"Mental health - after-care services","desc":"It shall be the duty of the local social services authority to provide, in co-operation with relevant voluntary agencies, after-care services for any person to whom this section applies until such time as they are satisfied that the person concerned is no longer in need of such services","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2350"},{"id":"2347","label":"Mental health - application for guardianship","desc":"The person named as guardian in a guardianship application may be either a local social services authority or any other person but a guardianship application in which a person other than a local social services authority is named as guardian shall be of no effect unless it is accepted on behalf of that person by the local social services authority for the area in which he resides, and shall be accompanied by a statement in writing by that person that he is willing to act as guardian.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2347"},{"id":"2348","label":"Mental health - applications for admission or guardianship by approved mental health professionals","desc":"If a local social services authority have reason to think that an application for admission to hospital or a guardianship application may need to be made in respect of a patient within their area, they shall make arrangements for an approved mental health professional to consider the patient's case on their behalf.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2348"},{"id":"2349","label":"Mental health - approval by local social services authority","desc":"A local social services authority may approve a person to act as an approved mental health professional","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2349"},{"id":"2342","label":"Mental health - approved social workers","desc":"A local social services authority shall appoint a sufficient number of approved social workers for the purpose of discharging the functions referred to in the Act.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2342"},{"id":"2957","label":"Mental health - arrangement of interview","desc":"A local social services authority must arrange for a person to be interviewed by a mental health professional in certain circumstances","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2957"},{"id":"2567","label":"Mental health - assessment of residency","desc":"A LA is responsible for determining within which local area an adult (who is a former user of secondary mental health services) resides, where there is a question about whether an adult's usual or most residence is situated within a particular LA area.However, where the local mental health partners for another LA area agree to act as the local mental health partners for an adult, then that adult is deemed to be usually resident within that other LA area","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2567"},{"id":"2352","label":"Mental health - availability of independent mental health advocates","desc":"A local social services authority shall make such arrangements as it considers reasonable to enable persons (independent mental health advocates) to be available to help qualifying patients.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2352"},{"id":"2566","label":"Mental health - care co-ordination","desc":"Where a Local Health Board is responsible for providing a secondary mental health service to a relevant patient and a LA is also responsible for providing such a service, then the Local Health Board is the relevant mental health service provider for a relevant patient unless the patient is the subject of\u2014 a guardianship application or order, or, is under the age of eighteen years and\u2014is looked after by a LA or is a relevant child or qualifies for advice and assistance or is admitted to a school in accordance with a statement of SEN that names the school in which case the LA is to act as the mental health service provider","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2566"},{"id":"2353","label":"Mental health -
