register of notices of contraventions of tree preservation orders","desc":"It shall be the duty of a local planning authority to compile and keep available for public inspection free of charge at all reasonable hours and at a convenient place a register containing such particulars as the Secretary of State may determine of notices of intended acts affecting protected trees in their area.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1440"},{"id":"1447","label":"Planning - removal of placards and posters","desc":"A local authority may remove or obliterate placards and posters and remove structures used for unauthorised display (England only) in certain circumstances.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/1447"},{"id":"1406","label":"Planning - review of simplified planning zone schemes","desc":"A local authority must keep the question of simplified planning zone schemes for their area under review.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1406"},{"id":"2878","label":"Planning - reviews of old minerals permissions","desc":"A local authority must, where acting as planning authority, comply with the requirements therein.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2878"},{"id":"1348","label":"Planning - revocation and modification of listed buildings consent","desc":"A local authority may revoke or modify listed buildings consent.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/1348"},{"id":"1329","label":"Planning - revocation or modification of hazardous substances consents","desc":"A local authority may by order (which must be confirmed) revoke or modify hazardous substance consents in certain circumstances.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/1329"},{"id":"1411","label":"Planning - revocation or modification of planning permission","desc":"A local authority may revoke or modify planning permissions.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/1411"},{"id":"1340","label":"Planning - right of entry on land with hazardous substances","desc":"A person authorised in writing by a local authority may with or without a warrant enter land in certain circumstances for the purpose of surveying in connection with any application for hazardous substances consent or any proposal to issue a hazardous substances contravention notice.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/1340"},{"id":"1341","label":"Planning - right of entry to Crown land for hazardous substances surveying","desc":"A person authorised in writing by a local authority may enter Crown land in certain circumstances for the purpose of surveying the same, but only after having first obtained the appropriate authority.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/1341"},{"id":"1469","label":"Planning - rights of entry to land","desc":"A person authorised in writing by a local authority may enter land for certain purposes connected with the Town and Country Planning Act 1990.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/1469"},{"id":"1405","label":"Planning - simplified planning zones","desc":"A local authority may make or alter a simplified planning zone scheme.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/1405"},{"id":"3670","label":"Planning - spatial development availability of documents","desc":"The combined authority must make the spatial development strategy documents available for public inspection.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3670"},{"id":"1426","label":"Planning - stop notice","desc":"A local authority may issue and serve a stop notice prohibiting the carrying out a relevant activity on the land to which the enforcement notice relates, or any part of that land specified in the stop notice in certain circumstances.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/1426"},{"id":"3904","label":"Planning - street vote development orders","desc":"A local authority must comply with the procedure and outcome relating to Street Vote Developments Orders and associated referenda.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3904"},{"id":"1420","label":"Planning - temporary stop notice","desc":"A local authority may issue a temporary stop notice in certain circumstances.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/1420"},{"id":"1462","label":"Planning - temporary stopping up of highway for mineral workings","desc":"A local authority may temporarily stop up a highway for mineral working purposes.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/1462"},{"id":"2877","label":"Planning - time period for appeals","desc":"A local authority must, where acting as planning authority, comply with the time period set out in the Town and Country Planning (Determination of Appeal Procedure) (Prescribed Period) (England) Regulations 2009/454.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2877"},{"id":"1374","label":"Planning - town scheme agreements","desc":"A local authority may enter into a town scheme agreement in certain circumstances.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/1374"},{"id":"1437","label":"Planning - tree preservation orders","desc":"A local authority may, in certain circumstances, make tree preservation orders and provisional orders in the case of Welsh authorities.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/1437"},{"id":"1455","label":"Planning - use of appropriated or acquired land","desc":"A local authority may use land appropriated or acquired for planning purposes for certain other purposes.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/1455"},{"id":"1346","label":"Planning - variation or discharge of conditions attached to listed buildings consent","desc":"A local authority may vary or discharge conditions attached to a listed Buildings Consent to the extent permitted.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/1346"},{"id":"1352","label":"Planning - variation or revocation of local listed building consent orders","desc":"A local authority may vary or revoke a local listed building consent order.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/1352"},{"id":"1423","label":"Planning - variation or withdrawal of enforcement notice","desc":"A local authority may vary or withdraw an enforcement notice.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/1423"},{"id":"2876","label":"Planning - written representations for appeals","desc":"A local authority must, where acting as planning authority, comply with the procedure for dealing with written representations.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2876"},{"id":"709","label":"Planning and development - adoption of local development documents","desc":"The local planning authority may adopt a local development document (other than a development plan document) either as originally prepared or as modified to take account of any representations made in relation to the document or any other matter they think is relevant.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/709"},{"id":"716","label":"Planning and development - co-operation in relation to sustainable development","desc":"Local authorities must co-operate in relation to the planning of sustainable development.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/716"},{"id":"714","label":"Planning and development - discretionary joint committees","desc":"One or more local authorities may agree with one or more county councils in relation to any area of such a council for which there is also a district council to establish a joint committee to be the local planning authority","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/714"},{"id":"710","label":"Planning and development - discretionary revision of local development documents","desc":"The local planning authority may at any time prepare a revision of a local development document.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/710"},{"id":"732","label":"Planning and development - expenditure of Assembly","desc":"A local authority must pay the expenditure of the Assembly if the Assembly prepares, revises or approves a local development plan in circumstances where the Assembly does so because it thinks the local authority is failing to do anything necessary in connection with the preparation, revision or adoption of the plan.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/732"},{"id":"713","label":"Planning and development - joint local development documents","desc":"Two or more local authorities may agree to prepare joint local development documents and may request the Secretary of State's involvement to enable continued examination of a document if a local authority withdraws from such an agreement.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/713"},{"id":"718","label":"Planning and development - local development monitoring reports","desc":"Local authorities must prepare and make available monitoring reports on local development as directed.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/718"},{"id":"704","label":"Planning and development - local development schemes","desc":"A local authority must prepare, maintain and revise a scheme to be known as their local development scheme, and revise it if directed by the Secretary of State or the Mayor of London (if the authority is a London Borough), and must make the up-to-date text of the scheme available to the public (together with a copy of amendments).","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/704"},{"id":"715","label":"Planning and development - mandatory joint committees","desc":"Local authorities must comply with the Secretary of State's direction to establish or to revoke a joint committee.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/715"},{"id":"711","label":"Planning and development - mandatory revision of local development documents","desc":"The authority must prepare a revision of a local development document if the Secretary of State directs them to do so, and in accordance with such timetable as he directs.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/711"},{"id":"705","label":"Planning and development - minerals and waste development scheme","desc":"A county council in respect of so much of their area for which there is a district council must prepare and maintain a scheme to be known as their minerals and waste development scheme","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/705"},{"id":"719","label":"Planning and development - neighbourhood development plans","desc":"Local authorities must prepare a neighbourhood development plan in certain circumstances","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/719"},{"id":"707","label":"Planning and development - preparation of local development documents","desc":"A local authority must prepare and submit development plan documents in accordance with the local development scheme.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/707"},{"id":"717","label":"Planning and development - regard to Secretary of State's guidance","desc":"Local authorities must have regard to the Secretary of State's guidance when exercising their functions with relation to local development.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/717"},{"id":"712","label":"Planning and development - reimbursement of costs to Secretary of State","desc":"A local authority must pay the costs of the Secretary of State where he utilises his default power if he thinks that a local planning authority are failing or omitting to do anything it is necessary for them to do in connection with the preparation, revision or adoption of a development plan document.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/712"},{"id":"706","label":"Planning and development - statement of community involvement","desc":"A local authority must prepare a statement of community involvement.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/706"},{"id":"702","label":"Planning and development - survey of area in England","desc":"A local authority must keep under review the matters which may be expected to affect the development of their area or the planning of its development.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/702"},{"id":"703","label":"Planning and development - survey of area related to county matters","desc":"A county council in respect of so much of their area for which there is a district council must keep under review the matters which may be expected to affect development of that area or the planning of its development in so far as the development relates to a county matter.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/703"},{"id":"720","label":"Planning and development - sustainable development","desc":"A local authority must exercise various functions under the Act with a view to achieving sustainable development.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/720"},{"id":"708","label":"Planning and development - withdrawal of local development documents","desc":"A local authority may withdraw local development documents at any time before adoption.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/708"},{"id":"727","label":"Planning and development Wales - adoption of local development plan","desc":"A local authority may adopt a local development plan in certain circumstances.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/727"},{"id":"734","label":"Planning and development Wales - annual monitoring report","desc":"A local authority must prepare an annual monitoring report to the Assembly in the manner directed.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/734"},{"id":"2511","label":"Planning and development Wales - direction from Assembly","desc":"Two or more bodies must prepare a joint development plan when directed to do so by the Assembly","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2511"},{"id":"725","label":"Planning and development Wales - intervention by Assembly","desc":"A local authority must comply with directions from the Assembly.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/725"},{"id":"723","label":"Planning and development Wales - local development plan","desc":"A local authority must prepare and appraise a local development plan as directed.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/723"},{"id":"733","label":"Planning and development Wales - regard to guidance from Assembly","desc":"A local authority must in exercising any function under Part 6 of the Act have regard to Guidance from the Assembly.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/733"},{"id":"729","label":"Planning and development Wales - review of local development plan","desc":"A local authority must review a local development plan if they think the plan should be reviewed and at such others times as prescribed by Welsh Ministers, and must report to the Assembly on the findings of their review.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/729"},{"id":"730","label":"Planning and development Wales - revision of local development plan","desc":"A local authority must revise a local development plan in certain circumstances.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/730"},{"id":"728","label":"Planning and development Wales - revocation of local development plan","desc":"A local authority may request the Assembly to revoke a local development plan.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/728"},{"id":"722","label":"Planning and development Wales - survey of area in Wales","desc":"A local authority must keep under review the matters which may be expected to affect the development of their area or the planning of its development.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/722"},{"id":"726","label":"Planning and development Wales - withdrawal of local development plan","desc":"A local authority may withdraw a local development plan at any time before it is adopted.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/726"},{"id":"2327","label":"Planning and land - assessment of development land","desc":"If the Secretary of State directs an authority to do so, it shall make an assessment of land which is in its area and which is in its opinion available and suitable for development for residential purposes.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2327"},{"id":"2326","label":"Planning and land - public access to register of land held by public bodies","desc":"Registers sent to the local authority by the Secretary of State shall be available at the council's principal office for inspection by any member of the public at all reasonable hours.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2326"},{"id":"2521","label":"Planning and land - publication of information","desc":"A local authority must as prescribed publish information about the discharge of its functions and other related matters in accordance with a code of practice that may be issued by the Secretary of State.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2521"},{"id":"3920","label":"Planning Data \u2013 Compliance with Regulations","desc":"A local authority must comply with regulations regarding the management of its planning data and approved data standards where applicable.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3920"},{"id":"3922","label":"Planning Data \u2013 Duty to make certain planning data publicly available","desc":"A local authority must make planning data publicly available where required to do so by Regulations.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3922"},{"id":"3921","label":"Planning Data \u2013 Provision of Planning Data from third parties","desc":"A local authority may by publishing a notice require a person, or persons of a particular description, to provide to the authority such planning data as is specified or described in planning data regulations.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/3921"},{"id":"3923","label":"Planning Data \u2013 Use of planning data software","desc":"A local authority must use planning data software where required to do so by Regulations.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3923"},{"id":"1605","label":"Plant health - publication of orders","desc":"A local authority must publish certain orders when required to do so.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1605"},{"id":"1604","label":"Plant health - removal or destruction of crop, seed or plant","desc":"A local authority must comply with certain directions and pay compensation in certain circumstances in respect of any crop, or any seed, plant or part thereof, which is removed or destroyed in pursuance of any order.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1604"},{"id":"1862","label":"Platforms - safety for use on public occasions","desc":"A local authority must check the safety of every roof of a building, and every platform, balcony, or other structure or part thereof let or used or intended to be let or used for the purpose of affording sitting or standing accommodation for a number of persons used on the occasion of any show, entertainment, public procession, open-air meeting, or other like occasion.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1862"},{"id":"1769","label":"Pleasure boats - licensing","desc":"A local authority may grant, amend or revoke licences for pleasure boats.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/1769"},{"id":"692","label":"Policy - charging for discretionary services","desc":"A local authority may charge the service recipient for certain discretionary services.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/692"},{"id":"32","label":"Policy - Chief Officer remuneration","desc":"The authority must comply with its pay policy statement for the financial year in making the determination of the remuneration of or other terms and conditions applying to a chief officer of the authority","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/32"},{"id":"75","label":"Policy - direction to prepare and submit draft multi-area agreement","desc":"Local Authorities must prepare a multi-area agreement when directed to do so by the Secretary of State and must consult before so doing.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/75"},{"id":"691","label":"Policy - housing finance strategies and statements Wales","desc":"A local authority must prepare such housing strategies and statements as may be required.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/691"},{"id":"360","label":"Policy - local area agreement","desc":"A local authority when directed to do so by the Secretary of State must prepare a draft local area agreement and should consult with partner authorities and such other persons as appear to it to be appropriate in so doing.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/360"},{"id":"31","label":"Policy - pay policy statement","desc":"Local authority must prepare a pay policy statement, annually and have regard to Guidance when doing so.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/31"},{"id":"102","label":"Policy - power of general competence","desc":"A local authority may do anything that an individual can do providing it is not otherwise prevented from doing so by statute.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/102"},{"id":"74","label":"Policy - proposal for multi-area agreement","desc":"The local authorities for an area proposed to be covered by a multi-area agreement (the proposed area) may request the Secretary of State to give a direction under section 125 for the preparation and submission of a draft multi-area agreement for the proposed area.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/74"},{"id":"140","label":"Policy - proposals for single tier of local government","desc":"A local authority may respond to an invitation from the Secretary of State to bring forward a proposal regarding the establishment of a single tier of local government for the area","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/140"},{"id":"141","label":"Policy - provision of information to Boundary Committee","desc":"A local authority must if requested by the Boundary Committee to do so provide the Boundary Committee, by such date as the Boundary Committee may specify, with any information that the Boundary Committee may reasonably require in connection with any of their functions.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/141"},{"id":"80","label":"Policy - publication of information about multi-area agreement","desc":"A Local Authority must publish information about multi-area agreements or revised multi-area agreements.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/80"},{"id":"73","label":"Policy - regard to guidance by Secretary of State for combined authority","desc":"A local authority must have regard to guidance prepared by the Secretary of State with regard to anything done under Part VI of the Act.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/73"},{"id":"361","label":"Policy - regard to local improvement targets in local area agreement","desc":"A local authority must have regard to local improvement targets in its local area agreement when exercising its functions.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/361"},{"id":"155","label":"Policy - review by Boundary Committee of local government areas","desc":"A local authority may request the Boundary Committee to conduct a review of local government areas.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/155"},{"id":"362","label":"Policy - revision and amendment of targets in local area agreement","desc":"Any local improvement target other than a designated target for the time being specified in a local area agreement may be amended, or removed from the local area agreement,by the responsible local authority with the agreement of any partner authority to which the target relates and after consulting each other person to whom it relates. The responsible local authority may, with the consent of each person to whom the target in question is to relate, specify a new local improvement target in a local area agreement. Designated targets may only be amended following consultation with the Secretary of State.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/362"},{"id":"79","label":"Policy - revision proposals for multi-area agreement","desc":"A Local Authority may or must if directed to do so by the Secretary of State prepare a proposal for a revised multi-area agreement and consult as required.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/79"},{"id":"154","label":"Policy - structural and boundary changes","desc":"A local authority may make agreements about incidental matters regarding the subject matter of orders issued under sections 7 and 10 of the Local Government and Public Involvement in Health Act 2007.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/154"},{"id":"76","label":"Policy - submission of existing multi-area agreement","desc":"Local Authorities must when preparing a multi-area agreement other than in accordance with section 125 comply with the requirements of section 128 and consult when so doing.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/76"},{"id":"693","label":"Policy - trading in function-related activities through a company","desc":"A local authority may as authorised by regulations trade in function related activities through a company.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/693"},{"id":"78","label":"Policy - transfer of responsibility in multi-area agreement","desc":"The local authorities to which the targets specified in a multi-area agreement relate may request the Secretary of State to agree to another one of those authorities becoming the responsible authority in relation to the agreement.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/78"},{"id":"2107","label":"Pollution control - default powers where authority failed to perform functions","desc":"A local authority must comply with the directions of the Secretary of State when utilising his default powers under the Act.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2107"},{"id":"2541","label":"Pollution control - detergents in water","desc":"LAs in England and Wales are enforcement authorities with powers to appoint authorised officers who must enforce contraventions of the Regulations in their area by serving notices, imposing requirements, using powers of entry and seizure and disposing of controlled product","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2541"},{"id":"2718","label":"Pollution control - emissions register","desc":"Each local authority must maintain a register containing information concerning emissions from premises which has been obtained by the authority under section 35 of the Clean Air Act and information concerning certain appeals against section 36 notices.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2718"},{"id":"2548","label":"Pollution control - environment permits","desc":"Where a specified regulated facility is or will be operated in a LA\u2019s area, a LA may carry out various functions in relation to that facility including granting, varying, transferring and requiring surrender of permits and take actions relating to the enforcement and prevention of pollution","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2548"},{"id":"2106","label":"Pollution control - power to obtain information","desc":"A local authority may, in certain circumstances, serve a notice requiring the provision of information.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2106"},{"id":"2105","label":"Pollution control - powers of entry","desc":"An officer duly authorised by a local authority may enter any land or vessel for the purposes of inspections, measurements or tests required by the Act.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2105"},{"id":"2641","label":"Pollution control - volatile organic compounds","desc":"A LA must enforce the regulations which implement Directive 2004/42/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council on the limitation of emissions of volatile organic compounds due to the use of organic solvents in certain paints, varnishes and vehicle refinishing products (the VOCs in Paints Directive).","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2641"},{"id":"2562","label":"Pollution control - water quality","desc":"LAs must make such arrangements with the specified relevant supplier as will secure that the authority is notified as required by the regulations and may take and analyse, by a person designated by them in writing, such samples of the water supplied to premises in their area as they may reasonably require","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2562"},{"id":"3697","label":"Postponed elections - duties of registration officer","desc":"Where notice of an election or referendum was required to be published before 6th April 2020 and the poll was not held on the date specified the relevant registration officer must:(a)retain the documents forwarded to the officer in accordance with regulation 4(4) for the period of one year, and(b)after that period, cause those documents to be destroyed, unless otherwise directed by an order of a county court, a Crown Court or a magistrates\u2019 court.A person must not be allowed to inspect any of the documents in the possession of the relevant registration officer, except in accordance with an order made by a court for the inspection or production of any document for the purpose of instituting or maintaining a prosecution for an offence in relation to ballot papers.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3697"},{"id":"3698","label":"Postponed elections - London Mayor or assembly and councillor by-elections","desc":"The authority must comply with these regulations in relation to any candidates for the postponed election for the Mayor of London and London Assembly due to be held on 7th May 2020 and any postponed by-election to fill a vacancy in the office of councillor for any principal area in England.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3698"},{"id":"3699","label":"Postponed elections - parish council by-elections","desc":"A local authority must observe the following. A person (\u201cP\u201d) who became a candidate at a relevant by-election to fill a casual vacancy in the office of parish councillor on or before 6th April 2020 is no longer a candidate, and is treated as not having been a candidate before the coming into force of this regulation. Nothing in paragraph 1 above affects whether or not P is a candidate at the postponed poll for such an election.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3699"},{"id":"3700","label":"Postponed elections - police and crime commissioner elections","desc":"A returning officer for a relevant PCC election may recover charges in respect of expenses incurred for or in connection with that election, notwithstanding that the election was not held, if the expenses were necessarily incurred for the efficient and effective conduct of the election. The amount of any charges recoverable is to be paid by the Minister on an account being submitted to the Minister.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/3700"},{"id":"3695","label":"Postponed elections and referendums - postal ballots","desc":"Where a local authority makes arrangements for the election of a councillor for any local government area in England to fill a casual vacancy; or a referendum, the poll for which is conducted in accordance with Schedule 3 or 5 to the 2012 Regulations (neighbourhood planning referendums).In circumstances where notice of election or (as the case may be) notice of the referendum was required to be published on or before 6th April 2020, and the poll for that election or referendum was not held on the date required to be stated in that notice as a result of the Local Government and Police and Crime Commissioner (Coronavirus) (Postponement of Elections and Referendums) (England and Wales) Regulations 2020(1).A postal ballot paper which was returned by a postal voter has no effect for the purpose of the postponed poll.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3695"},{"id":"3696","label":"Postponed elections and referendums - treatment of postal ballot documents","desc":"Where notice of an election or referendum was required to be published on or before 6th April 2020 and the poll for that election or referendum was not held on the date required the returning officer must comply with regulations concerning the opening of and disposal of postal ballots.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3696"},{"id":"1876","label":"Powers of entry for surveying, measuring etc.","desc":"A local authority may enter land for certain purposes connected with the Act.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/1876"},{"id":"437","label":"Premises associated with persistent disorder or nuisance - closure notice","desc":"A local authority may apply for a closure notice with regard to premises associated with persistent disorder or nuisance and enforce that notice or apply for its extension or discharge (with rights to appeal).","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/437"},{"id":"438","label":"Premises associated with persistent disorder or nuisance - reimbursement of costs","desc":"A local authority may apply to have the cost of cleaning, securing or maintaining premises associated with persistent disorder or nuisance.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/438"},{"id":"2432","label":"Premises closure notice - closure order","desc":"A local authority may apply to a magistrate\u2019s court for a closure order or an extension of a closure order where a closure notice has been made and served.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2432"},{"id":"2434","label":"Premises closure notice - closure order appeal","desc":"A local authority may appeal to the Crown Court against various types of decision by the magistrate\u2019s court relating to a closure order.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2434"},{"id":"2435","label":"Premises closure notice - closure order enforcement","desc":"A person authorised by a local authority person may enter premises in respect of which a closure order is in force, do anything necessary to secure the premises against entry.A person acting under subsection (1) may use reasonable force. A person seeking to enter premises under subsection (1) must, if required to do so by or on behalf of the owner, occupier or other person in charge of the premises, produce evidence of his or her identity and authority before entering the premises.An authorised person may also enter premises in respect of which a closure order is in force to carry out essential maintenance or repairs to the premises.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2435"},{"id":"2437","label":"Premises closure notice - closure order guidance","desc":"A local authority must have regard to any guidance issued by the Secretary of State when considering taking action in relation to a closure notice or closure order.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2437"},{"id":"2436","label":"Premises closure notice - closure order reimbursement of costs","desc":"A local authority that incurs expenditure for the purpose of clearing, securing or maintaining premises in respect of which a closure order is in force may apply to the court that made the order for an order for those costs.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2436"},{"id":"2433","label":"Premises closure notice - discharge of closure order","desc":"A local authority may apply to a magistrate\u2019s court for the discharge of a closure order.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2433"},{"id":"2430","label":"Premises closure notice - issue and duration","desc":"A local authority may issue a closure notice if satisfied on reasonable grounds\u2014that the use of particular premises has resulted, or (if the notice is not issued) is likely soon to result, in nuisance to members of the public, orthat there has been, or (if the notice is not issued) is likely soon to be, disorder near those premises associated with the use of those premises,and that the notice is necessary to prevent the nuisance or disorder from continuing, recurring or occurring.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2430"},{"id":"2431","label":"Premises closure notice - variation and discharge","desc":"A local authority may vary and cancel a premises closure notice","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2431"},{"id":"3550","label":"Private fostering - actions on notification of child privately fostered","desc":"Where a local authority have received a notification about a child being fostered privately they must arrange for an officer of the authority within seven working days or as soon as is reasonably practicable visit the premises where the child is being cared for, visit and speak to the private foster carer and family, visit and speak to the child and ensure that all matters relating to the welfare of the child have been considered.Having made the visits the officer should make a written report to the authority.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3550"},{"id":"3549","label":"Private fostering - actions on notification of proposal to foster","desc":"Where a local authority have received notification of a proposal to foster a child privately they must arrange for an officer of the authority within seven working days or as soon as is reasonably practicable, to visit the proposed foster home, proposed foster carer and family, the child and every parent or person with parental responsibility for the child.Having completed the visits the officer should prepare a written report to the authority.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3549"},{"id":"3552","label":"Private fostering - monitoring the discharge of functions","desc":"Each local authority must monitor the way in which they discharge their functions under Part 9 of the Act and must appoint an officer of the authority for that purpose.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3552"},{"id":"3551","label":"Private fostering - subsequent visits to children","desc":"Each local authority must arrange for an officer of the authority to visit every child who is being fostered privately in their area:(a)in the first year of the private fostering arrangement, where reasonably practicable, at intervals of not more than six weeks(b)in any second or subsequent year, where reasonably practicable, at intervals of not more than 12 weeks.The authority must also arrange for every child who is fostered privately in their area to be visited by an officer when reasonably requested to do so by the child, the private foster carer, a parent of the child or any other person with parental responsibility for the child.Visits and matters considered during visits must be in accordance with regulations and the officer should make a written report of the visit.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3551"},{"id":"1504","label":"Private hire vehicles - licensing","desc":"Subject to the provisions of this legislation, a council may on the receipt of an application from the proprietor of any vehicle for the grant in respect of such vehicle of a licence to use the vehicle as a private hire vehicle, grant in respect thereof a vehicle licence and may attach conditions to the grant of any such licence.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/1504"},{"id":"1968","label":"Procurement - exclusion of non-commercial considerations from contracts","desc":"It is the duty of every public authority in relation to its public supply or works contracts, to exclude non-commercial considerations.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1968"},{"id":"1969","label":"Procurement - explanation of procurement decisions","desc":"Public authorities have a duty to give reasons for certain contract decisions to the person concerned. This includes decisions regarding approved suppliers, contract awards and existing contracts.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1969"},{"id":"1019","label":"Procurement - implied power to enter into contracts","desc":"Any statutory provision imposing a function upon a local authority confers a power for that authority to enter into a contract for the purpose of carrying out that function.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/1019"},{"id":"1970","label":"Procurement - review of approved supplier list","desc":"It is the duty of a public authority which maintains an approved list to consider whether persons have been included in or excluded from the list by reference to non-commercial matters, and if it appears to the authority that that is the case to compile the list afresh.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1970"},{"id":"3990","label":"Procurement - valuation of contracts","desc":"The \"estimated value\" of a contract is its value for the time being estimated by a contracting authority.A contracting authority that estimates the value of a contract must do so in accordance with Schedule 3 of the Procurement Act 2023.A contracting authority must not exercise a discretion in connection with estimating the value of a contract with a view to securing that any requirement of this Act does not apply in relation to the contract.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3990"},{"id":"4065","label":"Procurement investigations","desc":"A contracting authority must comply with an investigation by an appropriate authority relating to the relevant contracting authority's compliance with requirements of this Act.The relevant contracting authority must comply with a notice from the appropriate authority before the end of\u2014(a) the period specified in the notice (which must be at least 30 days beginning with the day on which the notice is given), or(b) such longer period as the appropriate authority may agree to.In this section\u2014\"procurement investigation\" means an investigation under section 108(1);\"relevant contracting authority\" means a contracting authority other than\u2014(a) a Minister of the Crown or a government department;(b) the Welsh Ministers;(c) a Northern Ireland department;(d) the Corporate Officer of the House of Commons;(e) the Corporate Officer of the House of Lords;(f) the Senedd Commission;(g) the Northern Ireland Assembly Commission;(h) a private utility;\"relevant documents\" means documents or other information that\u2014(a) are specified or described in a notice, and(b) are in the possession or control of the relevant contracting authority to which the notice is given.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/4065"},{"id":"4066","label":"Procurement investigations recommendations","desc":"In considering how to comply with the requirements of this Act, a relevant contracting authority must have regard to a section 109 recommendation issued to it.A relevant contracting authority to which a section 109 recommendation has been issued must, where the recommendation so specifies, submit a progress report to the appropriate authority at such intervals as may be specified.A \"progress report\" is a report setting out\u2014(a) what action (if any) the relevant contracting authority has taken as a result of the recommendation, or(b) if the authority has taken no such action, a statement to that effect.Where the relevant contracting authority has taken no action as a result of the section 109 recommendation, or has taken different action to that recommended, the progress report must also include the authority's reasons for doing so.The contracting authority must also have regard to Guidance published under section 110.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/4066"},{"id":"4036","label":"Procurement termination notices","desc":"This section applies if, after publishing a tender or transparency notice in respect of a public contract, a contracting authority decides not to award the contract.As soon as reasonably practicable after making the decision, the contracting authority must give notice to that effect.This section does not apply to private utilities.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/4036"},{"id":"4037","label":"Procurement \u2013 technical specifications","desc":"This section applies in relation to\u2014(a) a competitive tendering procedure;(b) an award of a public contract in accordance with a framework;(c) a process to become a member of a dynamic market.The procurement documents may not refer to design, a particular licensing model or a description of characteristics in circumstances where they could appropriately refer to performance or functional requirements.he procurement documents may not refer to a United Kingdom standard unless\u2014(a) the standard adopts an internationally-recognised equivalent, or(b) there is no internationally-recognised equivalent.If the procurement documents refer to a United Kingdom standard, they must provide that tenders, proposals or applications that the contracting authority considers satisfy an equivalent standard from another state, territory or organisation of states or territories will be treated as having satisfied the United Kingdom standard.In considering whether a standard is equivalent to a United Kingdom standard for the purposes of the above, a contracting authority may have regard to the authority's purpose in referring to the standard.A contracting authority may require certification, or other evidence, for the purpose of satisfying itself that a standard is satisfied or equivalent.Unless the contracting authority considers it necessary in order to make its requirements understood, the procurement documents may not refer to a particular\u2014(a) trademark, trade name, patent, design or type,(b) place of origin, or(c) producer or supplier.If these matters are referred to, the procurement documents must also provide that tenders, proposals or applications demonstrating equivalent quality or performance will not be disadvantaged.In this section\u2014\"procurement documents\" means\u2014(a) the tender notice or associated tender documents, including any requirements of a competitive tendering procedure, conditions of participation or award criteria;(b) documents inviting suppliers to participate in a competitive selection process under a framework, including details of the process, any conditions of participation or criteria for the award of the contract;(c) documents inviting suppliers to apply for membership of a dynamic market, including any conditions for membership;\"United Kingdom standard\" means a standard that is\u2014(a) set by the British Standards Institution, or(b) primarily developed for use in the United Kingdom, or part of the United Kingdom.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/4037"},{"id":"4064","label":"Procurement \u2013 automatic suspension of the entry into or modification of contracts","desc":"A contracting authority may not enter into a public contract, or modify a public contract or a convertible contract, if during any applicable standstill period\u2014(a) proceedings under this Part are commenced in relation to the contract, and(b) the contracting authority is notified of that fact.The court may lift or modify this restriction by order under section 102.The above restriction does not apply if\u2014(a) the proceedings at first instance have been determined, discontinued or otherwise disposed of, and(b) the court has not made an order to extend the restriction.In this section \"convertible contract\" has the meaning given in section 74.See sections 51 and 76 for provision about standstill periods.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/4064"},{"id":"4004","label":"Procurement \u2013 award criteria","desc":"\u201cAward criteria\" means criteria set in accordance with this section against which tenders may be assessed for the purpose of awarding a public contract under section 19 (award following competitive tendering procedure).In setting award criteria, a contracting authority must be satisfied that they\u2014(a) relate to the subject-matter of the contract,(b) are sufficiently clear, measurable and specific,(c) do not break the rules on technical specifications in section 56, and(d) are a proportionate means of assessing tenders, having regard to the nature, complexity and cost of the contract.In setting award criteria, a contracting authority must\u2014(a) describe how tenders are to be assessed by reference to them and, in particular, specify whether failure to meet one or more criteria would disqualify a tender (the \"assessment methodology\"), and(b) if there is more than one criterion, indicate their relative importance by\u2014(i) weighting each as representing a percentage of total importance,(ii) ranking them in order of importance, or(iii) describing it in another way.In setting award criteria for the assessment of tenders by reference to lots, a contracting authority\u2014(a) may limit the number of lots that may be awarded to any one supplier, and(b) in doing so, must provide an objective mechanism for supplier selection in circumstances where a supplier would otherwise exceed the limit.The reference to the subject-matter of a contract includes a reference to\u2014(a) the goods, services or works to be supplied under the contract, including in respect of any aspect of their production, trading or other stage in their life-cycle;(b) how or when those goods, services or works are to be supplied;(c) the qualifications, experience, ability, management or organisation of staff where those factors are likely to make a material difference to the quality of goods, services or works being supplied;(d) price, other costs or value for money in all the circumstances.In the case of a light touch contract, the reference to the subject-matter of the contract also includes a reference to\u2014(a) the views of an individual for whose benefit the services are to be supplied (a \"service recipient\"), or of a person providing care to a service recipient, in relation to\u2014(i) who should supply the services, and(ii) how and when they should be supplied;(b) the different needs of different service recipients;(c) the importance of proximity between the supplier and service recipients for the effective and efficient supply of the services.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/4004"},{"id":"4000","label":"Procurement \u2013 award of contracts following a competitive tendering procedure","desc":"A contracting authority may award a public contract to the supplier that submits the most advantageous tender in a competitive tendering procedure.The \"most advantageous tender\" is the tender that the contracting authority considers\u2014(a) satisfies the contracting authority's requirements, and(b) best satisfies the award criteria when assessed by reference to\u2014(i) the assessment methodology under section 23(3)(a), and(ii) if there is more than one criterion, the relative importance of the criteria under section 23(3)(b).In assessing tenders for the purposes of this section a contracting authority\u2014(a) must disregard any tender from a supplier that does not satisfy the conditions of participation;(b) may disregard any tender from a supplier that\u2014(i) is not a United Kingdom supplier or treaty state supplier, or(ii) intends to sub-contract the performance of all or part of the contract to a supplier that is not a United Kingdom supplier or treaty state supplier;(c) may disregard any tender that offers a price that the contracting authority considers to be abnormally low for performance of the contract;(d) may disregard any tender which breaches a procedural requirement set out in the tender notice or associated tender documents.Before disregarding a tender under for the reason of abnormally low price, a contracting authority must\u2014(a) notify the supplier that the authority considers the price to be abnormally low, and(b) give the supplier reasonable opportunity to demonstrate that it will be able to perform the contract for the price offered.If the supplier demonstrates to the contracting authority's satisfaction that it will be able to perform the contract for the price offered, the authority may not disregard the tender for the reason of abnormally low price.The reference to a tender breaching a procedural requirement includes a reference to a supplier breaching a procedural requirement in relation to the tender.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/4000"},{"id":"4016","label":"Procurement \u2013 competitive award by reference to dynamic markets","desc":"NOTE - this is a power with duties.A competitive flexible procedure may provide for the following suppliers to be excluded from participating in, or progressing as part of, the procedure\u2014(a) suppliers that are not members of an appropriate dynamic market, or(b) suppliers that are not members of an appropriate part of an appropriate dynamic market.In relation to the award of a public contract under section 19 if the competitive flexible procedure provides for the above suppliers to be excluded.In assessing tenders under section 19, a contracting authority must disregard any tender from a supplier that is not a member of\u2014(a) the appropriate dynamic market, or(b) the appropriate part of the appropriate dynamic market.A contracting authority must, before excluding suppliers or disregarding tenders under this section, consider any applications for membership of the market or part of the market from suppliers that have submitted a request to participate in the competitive flexible procedure, or submitted a tender as part of the competitive flexible procedure.The above does not apply in relation to an application for membership if, due to exceptional circumstances arising from the complexity of the particular procurement, a contracting authority is unable to consider the application before\u2014(a) the deadline for submitting a request to participate in the procedure, or(b) where there has been no invitation to submit such requests, the deadline for submitting a first or only tender.A dynamic market or part of a dynamic market is \"appropriate\" for the purposes of this section if its terms permit the award of the contract by the contracting authority.This section does not apply in relation to the award of a concession contract, unless the concession contract is also a utilities contract.In this Act\u2014\"dynamic market\" means arrangements established under section 35(1); references to a contract being awarded by reference to suppliers' membership of a dynamic market are references to a contract being awarded in reliance on this section; references to suppliers' membership of a dynamic market are references to suppliers' participation in arrangements established under section 35(1).","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/4016"},{"id":"4001","label":"Procurement \u2013 competitive tender procedures","desc":"Before awarding a public contract under section 19, a contracting authority must carry out a competitive tendering procedure in accordance with a tender notice and any associated tender documents.A \"competitive tendering procedure\" is\u2014(a) a single-stage tendering procedure without a restriction on who can submit tenders (an \"open procedure\"), or(b) such other competitive tendering procedure as the contracting authority considers appropriate for the purpose of awarding the public contract (a \"competitive flexible procedure\").A contracting authority must ensure that the procedure is a proportionate means of awarding the public contract, having regard to the nature, complexity and cost of the contract.A competitive flexible procedure\u2014(a) may limit the number of participating suppliers, generally or in respect of particular tendering rounds or other selection processes;(b) may provide for the refinement of award criteria in accordance with section 24;(c) may not permit the participation of suppliers that did not submit a tender in the first round of tendering or that were excluded following an earlier round.A competitive flexible procedure may provide for the exclusion of suppliers\u2014(a) by reference to conditions of participation (see section 22);(b) by reference to an intermediate assessment of tenders;(c) that are not United Kingdom suppliers or treaty state suppliers;(d) that intend to sub-contract the performance of all or part of the contract to a supplier that is not a United Kingdom supplier or treaty state supplier.The reference in subsection (5)(b) to an intermediate assessment of tenders is a reference to an assessment of which tenders\u2014(a) satisfy the contracting authority's requirements, and(b) best satisfy the award criteria at the point of exclusion, when assessed by reference to\u2014(i) the assessment methodology under section 23(3)(a), and(ii) if there is more than one criterion, the relative importance of the criteria under section 23(3)(b), in each case, at the point of assessment.A competitive tendering procedure may, if a contract is being awarded by reference to lots, limit the number of lots in respect of which any one supplier can submit a tender.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/4001"},{"id":"4003","label":"Procurement \u2013 conditions of participation","desc":"A contracting authority may set conditions of participation in relation to the award of a public contract under section 19 only if it is satisfied that the conditions are a proportionate means of ensuring that suppliers have\u2014(a) the legal and financial capacity to perform the contract, or(b) the technical ability to perform the contract.A \"condition of participation\" is a condition that a supplier must satisfy if the supplier is to be awarded the public contract.A condition set under subsection (1)(a) may not\u2014(a) require the submission of audited annual accounts, except from suppliers who are, or were, required to have the accounts audited in accordance with Part 16 of the Companies Act 2006 or an overseas equivalent;(b) require insurance relating to the performance of the contract to be in place before the award of the contract.A condition set under subsection (1)(b) may relate to suppliers' qualifications, experience or technical ability, but may not\u2014(a) require suppliers to have been awarded a contract by a particular contracting authority,(b) break the rules on technical specifications in section 56, or(c) require particular qualifications without allowing for their equivalents.When considering whether a condition is proportionate for the purposes of subsection (1), a contracting authority must have regard to the nature, complexity and cost of the public contract.A condition of participation may require the provision of evidence that is verifiable by a person other than the supplier.If a supplier does not satisfy a condition of participation, the contracting authority may exclude the supplier from participating in, or progressing as part of, the competitive tendering procedure.A supplier is to be treated as satisfying a condition of participation to the extent that a supplier associated with the supplier satisfies the condition.For the purposes of this section, a supplier is associated with another supplier if\u2014(a) the suppliers are submitting a tender together, or(b) the contracting authority is satisfied that the suppliers will enter into legally binding arrangements to the effect that\u2014(i) the supplier will sub-contract the performance of all or part of the contract to the other, or(ii) the other supplier will guarantee the performance of all or part of the contract by the supplier.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/4003"},{"id":"4055","label":"Procurement \u2013 conflict assessments","desc":"A Before publishing a tender or transparency notice in relation to a covered procurement, a contracting authority must prepare a conflicts assessment in relation to the procurement.Before publishing a dynamic market notice in relation to the establishment of a dynamic market, a contracting authority must prepare a conflicts assessment in relation to the establishment.A conflicts assessment must include details of\u2014(a) conflicts or potential conflicts of interest identified in accordance with section 81 (duty to identify), and(b) any steps the contracting authority has taken or will take for the purposes of section 82 (duty to mitigate).If a contracting authority is aware of circumstances that it considers are likely to cause a reasonable person to wrongly believe there to be a conflict or potential conflict of interest, a conflicts assessment must also include details of any steps the contracting authority has taken or will take to demonstrate that no such conflict or potential conflict exists.A contracting authority must\u2014(a) keep any conflicts assessment under review,(b) revise the assessment as necessary, and(c) when publishing any relevant notice, confirm that a conflicts assessment has been prepared and revised in accordance with this section.unless\u2014(a) a contracting authority has given notice of its decision not to award the contract (under section 55),(b) a contract termination notice is published in relation to the procurement, or(c) a dynamic market notice is published in relation to the market ceasing to operate.In the case of a contracting authority that is a private utility\u2014(a) the reference in this section to notice of a decision not to award a contract is a reference to the decision;(b) the reference in this section to a contract termination notice being published in relation to a procurement is a reference to the contract being terminated;(c) the reference in this section to a dynamic market notice being published in relation to a market ceasing to operate is a reference to the market ceasing to operate.In this section\u2014\"conflict of interest\" has the meaning given in section 81;\"relevant notice\" means\u2014(a) a tender notice,(b) a transparency notice,(c) a dynamic market notice in relation to the establishment of a dynamic market,(d) a contract details notice relating to a public contract, or(e) a contract change notice;\"terminated\" is to be understood by reference to section 80(3).","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/4055"},{"id":"4053","label":"Procurement \u2013 conflicts of interest: duty to identify","desc":"A contracting authority must take all reasonable steps to identify, and keep under review, in relation to a covered procurement any\u2014(a) conflicts of interest, or(b) potential conflicts of interest.There is a conflict of interest in relation to a covered procurement if\u2014(a) a person acting for or on behalf of the contracting authority in relation to the procurement has a conflict of interest, or(b) a Minister acting in relation to the procurement has a conflict of interest.A person who influences a decision made by or on behalf of a contracting authority in relation to a covered procurement is to be treated as acting in relation to the procurement.In this section\u2014\"interest\" includes a personal, professional or financial interest and may be direct or indirect;\"Minister\" means\u2014(a) a Minister of the Crown;(b) a member of the Welsh Government;(c) the First Minister, deputy First Minister or a Northern Ireland Minister;\"member of the Welsh Government\" means a person referred to in section 45 of the Government of Wales Act 2006.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/4053"},{"id":"4054","label":"Procurement \u2013 conflicts of interest: duty to mitigate","desc":"A contracting authority must take all reasonable steps to ensure that a conflict of interest does not put a supplier at an unfair advantage or disadvantage in relation to a covered procurement.Reasonable steps may include requiring a supplier to take reasonable steps.The provision below applies if a contracting authority considers that\u2014(a) a conflict of interest puts a supplier at an unfair advantage in relation to the award of a public contract, and(b) either\u2014(i) the advantage cannot be avoided, or(ii) the supplier will not take steps that the contracting authority considers are necessary in order to ensure it is not put at an unfair advantage.The contracting authority must in relation to the award\u2014(a) treat the supplier as an excluded supplier for the purpose of\u2014(i) assessing tenders under section 19 (competitive award), or(ii) awarding a contract under section 41 or 43 (direct award), and(b) exclude the supplier from participating in, or progressing as part of, any competitive tendering procedure.In this section, \"conflict of interest\" has the meaning given in section 81.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/4054"},{"id":"4039","label":"Procurement \u2013 considering whether a supplier is excluded or excludable","desc":"In considering, for the purposes of section 57(1)(a) or (2)(a), whether the circumstances giving rise to the application of an exclusion ground are continuing or likely to occur again, a contracting authority may have regard to the following matters\u2014(a) evidence that the supplier, associated person or connected person has taken the circumstances seriously, for example by paying compensation;(b) steps that the supplier, associated person or connected person has taken to prevent the circumstances continuing or occurring again, for example by changing staff or management, or putting procedures and training in place;(c) commitments that such steps will be taken, or to provide information or access to allow verification or monitoring of such steps;(d) the time that has elapsed since the circumstances last occurred;(e) any other evidence, explanation or factor that the authority considers appropriate.Before determining whether a supplier is an excluded supplier under section 57(1)(a) or an excludable supplier under section 57(2)(a), a contracting authority must give the supplier reasonable opportunity to\u2014(a) make representations, and(b) provide evidence as to whether exclusion grounds apply and whether the circumstances giving rise to any application are likely to occur again (including information of a kind referred to in subsection (1)).But a contracting authority may not require particular evidence or information unless the authority is satisfied that the requirements are proportionate in the circumstances, having regard to\u2014(a) the nature and complexity of the matters being assessed, and(b) where relevant, the preliminary nature of a consideration under section 27(3).NOTE - this is a duty and a power.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/4039"},{"id":"4031","label":"Procurement \u2013 contract award notices and assessment summaries","desc":"Before entering into a public contract, a contracting authority must publish a contract award notice.A \"contract award notice\" means a notice setting out\u2014(a) that the contracting authority intends to enter into a contract, and(b) any other information specified in regulations under section 95.Before publishing a contract award notice in respect of a contract awarded under section 19 (award following competitive tendering procedure), a contracting authority must provide an assessment summary to each supplier that submitted an assessed tender.An \"assessment summary\" means, in relation to an assessed tender, information about the contracting authority's assessment of\u2014(a) the tender, and(b) if different, the most advantageous tender submitted in respect of the contract.In this section, an \"assessed tender\" is a tender which\u2014(a) was submitted in respect of the contract and assessed for the purposes of determining the most advantageous tender under section 19(1), and(b) was not disregarded in the assessment of tenders.This section does not apply in relation to\u2014(a) a defence and security contract awarded under a defence and security framework;(b) a contract awarded under section 41 by reference to paragraph 15 of Schedule 5 (direct award: user choice contracts).","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/4031"},{"id":"4047","label":"Procurement \u2013 contract change notices","desc":"Before modifying a public contract or a convertible contract (see section 74(1)), a contracting authority must publish a contract change notice.The above does not apply if\u2014(a) the modification increases or decreases the estimated value of the contract by\u2014(i) in the case of a contract for goods or services, 10 per cent or less,(ii) in the case of a contract for works, 15 per cent or less, or(b) the modification increases or decreases the term of the contract by 10 per cent or less of the maximum term provided for on award, unless the modification is a permitted modification under paragraph 9 of Schedule 8 (novation or assignment on corporate restructuring).A \"contract change notice\" is a notice setting out\u2014(a) that the contracting authority intends to modify the contract;(b) any other information specified in regulations under section 95.The provision below applies if, on making a modification within subsection (2)(a) or (2)(b), a contracting authority considers that\u2014(a) the modification could reasonably have been made together with an earlier modification of the contract, and(b) the above would have applied to that single modification.Then the above is to be treated as applying to the modification.This section does not apply in relation to a modification of a contract that\u2014(a) is a defence and security contract,(b) is a light touch contract,(c) was awarded by a private utility,(d) was awarded by a transferred Northern Ireland authority, unless it was awarded as part of a procurement under a reserved procurement arrangement or a devolved Welsh procurement arrangement, or(e) was awarded as part of a procurement under a transferred Northern Ireland procurement arrangement.A Minister of the Crown or the Welsh Ministers may by regulations amend this section for the purpose of changing the percentage thresholds.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/4047"},{"id":"4034","label":"Procurement \u2013 contract details notices and publication of contracts","desc":"A contracting authority that enters into a public contract must publish a contract details notice\u2014(a) if the contract is a light touch contract, before the end of the period of 120 days beginning with the day on which the contract is entered into;(b) otherwise, before the end of the period of 30 days beginning with the day on which the contract is entered into.A \"contract details notice\" means a notice setting out\u2014(a) that the contracting authority has entered into a contract, and(b) any other information specified in regulations under section 95.A contracting authority that enters into a public contract with an estimated value of more than \u00a35 million must publish a copy of the contract\u2014(a) if the contract is a light touch contract, before the end of the period of 180 days beginning with the day on which the contract is entered into;(b) otherwise, before the end of the period of 90 days beginning with the day on which the contract is entered into, but this does not apply in relation to a contract\u2014(a) awarded by a devolved Welsh authority or a transferred Northern Ireland authority, unless it is awarded under a reserved procurement arrangement, or(b) awarded under a devolved Welsh procurement arrangement or a transferred Northern Ireland procurement arrangement.This section does not apply\u2014(a) to private utilities, or(b) in relation to a contract awarded under section 41 by reference to paragraph 15 of Schedule 5 (direct award: user choice contracts).","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/4034"},{"id":"4052","label":"Procurement \u2013 contract termination notices","desc":"Before the end of the period of 30 days beginning with the day on which a public contract is terminated, a contracting authority must publish a contract termination notice.A \"contract termination notice\" is a notice setting out\u2014(a) that the contract has been terminated, and(b) any other information specified in regulations under section 95.In this section, a reference to termination includes a reference to\u2014(a) discharge,(b) expiry,(c) termination by a party,(d) rescission, or(e) set aside by court order (whether or not under Part 9).This section does not apply\u2014(a) to private utilities, or(b) in relation to a contract awarded under section 41 by reference to paragraph 15 of Schedule 5 (direct award: user choice contracts).","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/4052"},{"id":"3993","label":"Procurement \u2013 covered procurements - objectives","desc":"In carrying out a covered procurement, a contracting authority must have regard to the importance of\u2014(a) delivering value for money;(b) maximising public benefit;(c) sharing information for the purpose of allowing suppliers and others to understand the authority's procurement policies and decisions;(d) acting, and being seen to act, with integrity.In carrying out a covered procurement, a contracting authority must treat suppliers the same unless a difference between the suppliers justifies different treatment.If a contracting authority considers that different treatment is justified in a particular case, the authority must take all reasonable steps to ensure it does not put a supplier at an unfair advantage or disadvantage.In carrying out a covered procurement, a contracting authority must\u2014(a) have regard to the fact that small and medium-sized enterprises may face particular barriers to participation, and(b) consider whether such barriers can be removed or reduced.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3993"},{"id":"3991","label":"Procurement \u2013 determination of value in mixed procurement","desc":"The contract is to be treated as having an estimated value of not less than the threshold amount for the type of contract if,on award of a below-threshold contract other than a framework, a contracting authority considers that\u2014(a) certain of the goods, services or works to be supplied under the contract could reasonably be supplied under a separate contract, and(b) that contract would have an estimated value of not less than the threshold amount for a contract of its type.or, on award of a below-threshold contract that is a framework, a contracting authority considers that\u2014(a) certain of the goods, services or works to be supplied under contracts awarded in accordance with the framework could reasonably be supplied under a contract not awarded in accordance with the framework, and(b) that contract would have an estimated value of not less than the threshold amount for a contract of its type.In considering whether goods, services or works could reasonably be supplied under a separate contract, a contracting authority may, for example, have regard to the practical and financial consequences of awarding more than one contract.A \"below-threshold contract\" means\u2014(a) a contract for the supply, for pecuniary interest, of goods, services or works to a contracting authority,(b) a framework, or(c) a concession contract,that has an estimated value of less than the threshold amount for the type of contract.But, this section does not apply to a contract awarded in accordance with a framework.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3991"},{"id":"4022","label":"Procurement \u2013 direct award in special cases","desc":"If a direct award justification applies, a contracting authority may award a public contract directly\u2014(a) to a supplier that is not an excluded supplier, or(b) in accordance with belowA contracting authority may award a contract to a supplier that is an excluded supplier if the contracting authority considers that there is an overriding public interest in awarding the contract to that supplier.A contracting authority may carry out a selection process or take such other preliminary steps as it considers appropriate for the purpose of awarding a contract under this section.Before awarding a contract to a supplier under this section, a contracting authority must consider whether the supplier is an excludable supplier.There is an overriding public interest in awarding a public contract to an excluded supplier if\u2014(a) it is necessary in order to construct, maintain or operate critical national infrastructure,(b) it is necessary in order to ensure the proper functioning of a sector on which the defence, security or economic stability of the United Kingdom relies,(c) failure to do so would prejudice the conduct of military or security operations, or the effective operation of the armed forces or intelligence services, or(d) the contract is being awarded by reference to paragraph 13 of Schedule 5 (extreme and unavoidable urgency) and cannot be awarded to, or performed by, a supplier that is not an excluded supplier within the necessary time frame.The direct award justifications are set out in Schedule 5.In this section, \"intelligence services\" means the Security Service, the Secret Intelligence Service and the Government Communications Headquarters.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/4022"},{"id":"3999","label":"Procurement \u2013 duty to consider lots","desc":"Before publishing a tender notice in respect of a public contract, a contracting authority must consider\u2014(a) whether the goods, services or works to be supplied under the contract could reasonably be supplied under more than one contract, and(b) whether such contracts could appropriately be awarded by reference to lots.If the contracting authority considers that the goods, services or works could reasonably be supplied under more than one contract and such contracts could appropriately be awarded by reference to lots, the authority must\u2014(a) arrange for the award of the contract or contracts by reference to lots, or(b) provide reasons for not doing so.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3999"},{"id":"4021","label":"Procurement \u2013 dynamic market notices","desc":"A notice under this section is called a \"dynamic market notice\". Before establishing a dynamic market, a contracting authority must publish a notice setting out\u2014(a) that the authority intends to establish a dynamic market, and(b) any other information specified in regulations under section 95.As soon as reasonably practicable after establishing a dynamic market, the contracting authority must publish a notice setting out\u2014(a) that the dynamic market has been established, and(b) any other information specified in regulations under section 95.As soon as reasonably practicable after modifying a dynamic market, the contracting authority must publish a notice setting out\u2014(a) the modifications made to the market, and(b) any other information specified in regulations under section 95.As soon as reasonably practicable after a dynamic market ceases to operate, the contracting authority that established the market must publish a notice setting out\u2014(a) that the dynamic market has ceased to operate, and(b) any other information specified in regulations under section 95.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/4021"},{"id":"4017","label":"Procurement \u2013 dynamic markets: establishment","desc":"A contracting authority may establish arrangements for the purpose of a contracting authority awarding public contracts by reference to suppliers' participation in the arrangements.In this Act a \"utilities dynamic market\" means a dynamic market established only for the purpose of the award of utilities contracts by utilities.If arrangements established by any person comply with the requirements of this Act that apply in relation to a utilities dynamic market established by a private utility\u2014(a) the arrangements are to be treated for the purposes of this Act as a utilities dynamic market established
