support and attendance","desc":"A local authority in England may support or facilitate, or make arrangements to be represented at, any of the following\u2014(a) a religious event,(b) an event with a religious element,(c) an event connected with a religious or philosophical belief, or(d) an event with an element connected with such a belief.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/3003"},{"id":"1499","label":"Removal of obstructions from private sewers","desc":"A local authority may by notice require the removal of an obstruction from a private sewer and in certain circumstances may clear the obstruction itself and charge for the removal.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/1499"},{"id":"4083","label":"Remuneration and Terms and Conditions of Social Care Workers \u2013 Duty to keep records","desc":"A local authority must keep records as required by Regulations regarding the remuneration and terms and conditions of those proving social care for adults.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/4083"},{"id":"4081","label":"Remuneration and Terms and Conditions of Social Care Workers \u2013 General Duty","desc":"A local authority must comply with Regulations regarding the remuneration and terms and conditions of those proving social care for adults.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/4081"},{"id":"4082","label":"Remuneration and Terms and Conditions of Social Care Workers \u2013 Regulations and Guidance","desc":"A local authority must comply with Regulations and Guidance regarding the remuneration and terms and conditions of those proving social care for adults.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/4082"},{"id":"2554","label":"Renewable energy - sale of electricity","desc":"LAs can sell electricity which is produced from the following renewable sources: wind, solar, aero thermal, geothermal, hydrothermal and ocean energy, hydropower, biomass, landfill gas, sewage treatment plant gas, and biogases.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2554"},{"id":"3924","label":"Rental Auctions","desc":"A local authority may arrange for a rental auction to be carried out in respect of qualifying high-street premises in certain circumstances and in compliance with Regulations.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/3924"},{"id":"3458","label":"Rented housing - duty to enforce treatment of holding deposit","desc":"The local weights and measures authority must enforce legislation relating to the treatment of a holding deposit for a proposed housing tenancy as detailed in Schedule 2 of the Tenant Fees Act 2019","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3458"},{"id":"3461","label":"Rented housing - power to enforce treatment of holding deposit","desc":"A district council which is not a local weights and measures authority may enforce legislation relating to the treatment of a holding deposit for a proposed housing tenancy as detailed in Schedule 2 of the Tenant Fees Act 2019","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/3461"},{"id":"1652","label":"Restaurants - establishment","desc":"A local authority may establish and carry on restaurants and otherwise provide for the supply to the public of meals and refreshments, and may carry on such activities as are reasonably incidental or ancillary to the activities aforesaid.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/1652"},{"id":"1635","label":"Riding establishments - inspections","desc":"A local authority may, subject to the provisions of this section, authorise in writing any such person as the following, namely, an officer of theirs, an officer of any other local authority, a veterinary surgeon and a veterinary practitioner, to inspect a riding establishment.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/1635"},{"id":"1634","label":"Riding establishments - licensing","desc":"A local authority may in certain circumstances and for payment of a fee licence a riding establishment.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/1634"},{"id":"1636","label":"Riding establishments - prosecutions","desc":"A local authority may prosecute proceedings for breach of the Riding Establishments Act 1964.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/1636"},{"id":"2176","label":"Riding establishments - provisional licence","desc":"A local authority may grant a provisional riding establishment licence in certain circumstances.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2176"},{"id":"2278","label":"Rights of way - agreements relating to improvements for benefit of persons with mobility problems","desc":"With respect to any relevant structure, a competent authority may enter into an agreement with the owner, lessee or occupier of the land on which the structure is situated which provides for the carrying out by the owner, lessee or occupier of any qualifying works and the payment by the competent authority of the whole or any part of the costs incurred by him in carrying out those works, or for the carrying out by the competent authority of any qualifying works at their own expense or subject to the payment by the owner, lessee or occupier of the whole or any part of the costs incurred in carrying out those works.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2278"},{"id":"2203","label":"Rights of way - compulsory powers for creation of footpaths and bridleways","desc":"Where it appears to a local authority that there is need for a footpath bridleway or restricted byway over land in their area and they are satisfied that it is expedient that the path or way should be created, the authority may by order made by them and submitted to and confirmed by the Secretary of State, or confirmed by them as an unopposed order, create a footpath bridleway or restricted byway over the land.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2203"},{"id":"2202","label":"Rights of way - creation of footpath or bridleway by agreement","desc":"A local authority may enter into an agreement with any person, with the necessary authority, for the dedication by that person of a footpath, bridleway or restricted byway over land in their area.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2202"},{"id":"2264","label":"Rights of way - diversion of certain highways for purposes of crime prevention, etc","desc":"Where it appears to a council that for the purpose of preventing or reducing crime, the line of the highway, or part of that line should be diverted (whether on to land of the same or another owner, lessee or occupier), the line of the highway, or part of that line, should be diverted (whether on to land of the same or another owner, lessee or occupier.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2264"},{"id":"2262","label":"Rights of way - diversion of footpaths and bridleways","desc":"Where it appears to a council as respects a footpath, bridleway or restricted byway in their area that, in the interests of the owner, lessee or occupier of land crossed by the path or way or of the public, it is expedient that the line of the path or way, or part of that line, should be diverted the council may create, any such new footpath, bridleway or restricted byway as appears to the council requisite for effecting the diversion","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2262"},{"id":"2263","label":"Rights of way - diversion of footpaths and bridleways crossing railways","desc":"Where it appears to a council expedient in the interests of the safety of members of the public using it or likely to use it that a footpath, bridleway or restricted byway in their area which crosses a railway, otherwise than by tunnel or bridge, should be diverted, the council may by order made by them and submitted to and confirmed by the Secretary of State, create any such new path or way as appears to the council requisite for effecting the diversion, and","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2263"},{"id":"2312","label":"Rights of way - expenses incurred in connection with footpaths, bridleways and restricted byways","desc":"A council or a local planning authority may defray or contribute towards, or undertake to defray or contribute towards, the expenses incurred or to be incurred by any other council or local planning authority for the creation of footpaths, bridleways and restricted byways by means of public path creation agreements or public path creation orders, to the making up of footpaths, bridleways and restricted byways and to the payment of compensation for loss caused by a public path creation order; and relating to the making of public path extinguishment orders and public path diversion orders, to the making up of footpaths, bridleways and restricted byways and to the payment of compensation for loss caused by any such order.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2312"},{"id":"465","label":"Rights of way - improvement plans","desc":"A local authority must prepare rights of way improvement plans in accordance with the requirements of the Act.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/465"},{"id":"2211","label":"Rights of way - maintenance by parish and community councils","desc":"The council of a parish or community may undertake the maintenance of any footpath, bridleway or restricted byway within the parish or community which is a highway maintainable at the public expense;","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2211"},{"id":"2214","label":"Rights of way - maintenance of privately maintainable footpaths and bridleways","desc":"The council of a non-metropolitan district, parish or community may undertake by virtue of this subsection the maintenance of any footpath or bridleway within the district, parish or community whether or not any other person is under a duty to maintain the footpath or bridleway","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2214"},{"id":"2277","label":"Rights of way - maintenance of stiles","desc":"Any stile, gate or other similar structure across a footpath, bridleway or restricted byway shall be maintained by the owner of the land in a safe condition. If it appears to the appropriate authority that the duty imposed is not being complied with, they may, after giving to the owner and occupier not less than 14 days' notice of their intention, take all necessary steps for repairing and making good the stile, gate or other works.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2277"},{"id":"2204","label":"Rights of way - making up of new footpaths and bridleways","desc":"On the dedication of a footpath, bridleway or restricted byway in pursuance of a public path creation agreement, or on the coming into operation of a public path creation order, the highway authority shall survey the path or way and shall certify what work (if any) appears to them to be necessary to bring it into a fit condition for use by the public as a footpath, bridleway or restricted byway. There are also expenses provisions.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2204"},{"id":"2215","label":"Rights of way - non-repair of privately maintainable highways","desc":"Where a person is liable to maintain a footpath or bridleway and the highway authority for the highway repair it in the performance of their duty to maintain it, they may recover the necessary expenses of doing so from that person in any court of competent jurisdiction.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2215"},{"id":"2205","label":"Rights of way - regard to agriculture, forestry and nature conservation","desc":"In the exercise of functions re making public path creation agreements and public path creation orders it shall be the duty of councils to have due regard to the needs of agriculture and forestry, and the desirability of conserving flora, fauna and geological and physiographical features.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2205"},{"id":"2265","label":"Rights of way - register of applications for stopping up or diversion","desc":"Every council shall keep a register of applications for the stopping up or diversion of rights of way. The manner in which the register is kept and the information to be held should be as prescribed by regulations. Wales - every council shall keep a register containing such information as may be prescribed with respect to applications this Act. Every register kept under this section shall be available for inspection by the public free of charge at all reasonable hours.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2265"},{"id":"1578","label":"Rights of way - signposting of footpaths and bridleways","desc":"A local authority may erect a signpost on a footpath, bridleway or restricted byway in certain circumstances","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/1578"},{"id":"2261","label":"Rights of way - stopping up of certain highways for purposes of crime prevention, etc.","desc":"Where it appears to a council that it is expedient for the purpose of preventing or reducing crime which would otherwise disrupt the life of the community, that the highway should be stopped up, the council may, subject to confirmation by the Secretary of State, extinguish the public right of way over the highway.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2261"},{"id":"2259","label":"Rights of way - stopping up of footpaths, bridleways and restricted byways","desc":"Where it appears to a council as respects a footpath, bridleway or restricted byway in their area that it is expedient that the path or way should be stopped up on the ground that it is not needed for public use, the council may by order made by them and submitted to and confirmed by the Secretary of State, or confirmed as an unopposed order, extinguish the public right of way over the path or way.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2259"},{"id":"2260","label":"Rights of way - stopping up of footpaths, bridleways and restricted byways crossing railways","desc":"Where it appears to a council expedient in the interests of the safety of members of the public using it or likely to use it that a footpath, bridleway or restricted byway in their area which crosses a railway, otherwise than by tunnel or bridge, should be stopped up, the council may by order made by them and submitted to and confirmed by the Secretary of State, or confirmed as an unopposed order, extinguish the public right of way","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2260"},{"id":"2285","label":"Rights of way - surface repairs","desc":"Where the surface of a footpath, a bridleway, or any other highway which consists of or comprises a carriageway other than a made-up carriageway, has been so disturbed as to render it inconvenient for the exercise of the public right of way, a competent authority may make good the surface to an extent not less than the minimum width nor greater than the maximum width.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2285"},{"id":"2266","label":"Rights of way - temporary diversion where highway about to be repaired or widened","desc":"A highway authority who are about to repair or widen a highway, and a person who is about to repair or widen a highway maintainable by him by reason of tenure, enclosure or prescription, may, subject to the provisions of this section, construct on adjoining land a temporary highway for use while the work is in progress.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2266"},{"id":"1095","label":"Road traffic - reports on levels of road traffic","desc":"It shall be the duty of every principal council to prepare, at such time or times as the Secretary of State may direct, a report containing an assessment of the levels of local road traffic in their area, and a forecast of the growth in those levels. Additional requirements for the report are as detailed in regulations.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1095"},{"id":"3130","label":"Road traffic - school crossing patrols","desc":"A local traffic authority may establish school crossing patrols","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/3130"},{"id":"3900","label":"Roads - alteration of street names","desc":"A local authority may having had regard to Regulations and Guidance from the Secretary of State in certain circumstances alter street names.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/3900"},{"id":"3137","label":"Roads - bollards","desc":"A local authority may place bollards in a road in certain circumstances to enforce a local traffic order","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/3137"},{"id":"1323","label":"Roads - bridge works","desc":"A local authority must take certain steps with regard to bridge works.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1323"},{"id":"1303","label":"Roads - concession agreements","desc":"A local authority must comply with provisions relating to concession agreements.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1303"},{"id":"2365","label":"Roads - entering land in connection with traffic signs","desc":"A local traffic authority may enter any land and exercise such other powers as may be necessary for the purpose of the exercise and performance of their powers and duties of placing, replacing, converting and removing traffic signs","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2365"},{"id":"2042","label":"Roads - installation of apparatus etc. for driver information systems","desc":"The holder of an operator's licence shall have power to install system apparatus in, upon, under, over, along or across a public road and inspect, maintain, adjust, repair, alter, renew or remove any system apparatus so installed The powers conferred shall not be exercisable by fixing system apparatus to a structure or attachment to a structure belonging to another person or authority without the written consent of that other person or authority; and a local authority shall have power to give its consent upon such terms (including such terms as to payment) as it thinks appropriate","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2042"},{"id":"3134","label":"Roads - loading areas","desc":"A local authority may provide loading areas","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/3134"},{"id":"1189","label":"Roads - local charging schemes","desc":"A local charging scheme or a joint local charging scheme may be put into operation by certain local authorities in certain circumstances.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/1189"},{"id":"3132","label":"Roads - off-street parking","desc":"A local authority may designate and control off-street parking","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/3132"},{"id":"1981","label":"Roads - offences for which local authorities may institute proceedings","desc":"An authority institute proceedings for offences relating to safety equipment for children in motor vehicles, helmets and other head-worn appliances for motor cyclists, dogs on roads, parking places provided by the council, designated parking place controlled by the council or designated parking place in the council's area.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/1981"},{"id":"3136","label":"Roads - parking attendants","desc":"A local authority may provide parking attendants","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/3136"},{"id":"3133","label":"Roads - pay parking on highways","desc":"A local authority may designate and control pay parking on highways","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/3133"},{"id":"2360","label":"Roads - pedestrian crossings","desc":"A local traffic authority may establish crossings for pedestrians on roads for which they are the traffic authority, and may alter or remove any such crossings.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2360"},{"id":"2364","label":"Roads - placing of traffic signs","desc":"The traffic authority may cause or permit traffic signs to be placed on or near a road, subject to and in conformity with such general directions as may be given by the Ministers acting jointly or such other directions as may be given by the Secretary of State.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2364"},{"id":"2361","label":"Roads - prohibition of traffic on roads to be used as playgrounds","desc":"For the purpose of enabling a road for which they are the traffic authority to be used as a playground for children, a local traffic authority may make an order prohibiting or restricting the use of the road by vehicles, or by vehicles of any specified class, either generally or on particular days or during particular hours","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2361"},{"id":"1322","label":"Roads - prospectively maintainable highway","desc":"A local authority must take certain steps with regard to a prospectively maintainable highway.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1322"},{"id":"3131","label":"Roads - provision of parking and schemes of traffic control","desc":"A local authority may provide on and off road parking and traffic control schemes","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/3131"},{"id":"2362","label":"Roads - provision of parking places by local authority","desc":"Where for the purpose of relieving or preventing congestion of traffic it appears to a local authority to be necessary to provide within their area suitable parking places for vehicles, the local authority may provide off-street parking places or may by order authorise the use as a parking place of any part of a road within their area, not being a road the whole or part of the width of which is within Greater London.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2362"},{"id":"2363","label":"Roads - provision of parking places by parish or community councils","desc":"Where for the purposes of relieving or preventing congestion of traffic or preserving local amenities it appears to the council of a parish or a community in Wales to be necessary to do so, the council may provide within their area and maintain suitable parking places for bicycles and motor cycles, or provide within their area and maintain suitable parking places, otherwise than on roads, for vehicles of other descriptions or for vehicles generally.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2363"},{"id":"1191","label":"Roads - quiet lane or home zone","desc":"A local authority may designate any road a quiet lane of home zone by order and must comply with regulations","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/1191"},{"id":"2366","label":"Roads - signs erected by parish or community councils","desc":"The local highway authority may authorise a parish or community council, subject to any conditions imposed by that authority, to provide on or near any road, other than a footpath or bridleway, or to contribute, either wholly or in part, towards the cost of providing on or near any such road, traffic signs indicating signs indicating a stopping place for public service vehicles, a warning of the existence of any danger; or the name of the parish or community or of any place in it.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2366"},{"id":"3135","label":"Roads - stands and racks for cycles and motorcycles","desc":"A local authority may provide stands and racks for cycles and motorcycles","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/3135"},{"id":"1304","label":"Roads - toll orders","desc":"A local authority may issue toll orders in certain circumstances.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/1304"},{"id":"2367","label":"Roads - traffic signs for indicating speed restrictions","desc":"The local traffic authority is responsible for erecting and maintaining traffic signs in such positions as may be requisite indicating speed restrictions for all roads for which they are the traffic authority.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2367"},{"id":"1190","label":"Roads - workplace parking levy","desc":"A local work place levy licencing scheme or joint scheme may be put into operation by certain local authorities in certain circumstances.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/1190"},{"id":"2843","label":"Roadworks - charges for prolonged occupation (England)","desc":"A local authority must, where acting as a highway authority, collect the prescribed charges for undertaking works set out by the Regulations.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2843"},{"id":"2871","label":"Roadworks - collection of charges for prolonged works (Wales)","desc":"A local authority must, where acting as a highway authority, collect the prescribed charges for undertaking works set out by the Regulations.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2871"},{"id":"2870","label":"Roadworks - use of fees (England)","desc":"A local authority must, after deducting its expenses utilise the fess raised form undertakers, undertaking work in a highway for the purpose of developing or implementing policies for the promotion and encouragement of safe, integrated, efficient and economic transport facilities and services to, from and within its area. It must also keep accounts of how these fees are used.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2870"},{"id":"2872","label":"Roadworks - use of fees (Wales)","desc":"A local authority must, after deducting its expenses utilise the fess raised form undertakers, undertaking work in a highway for the purpose of developing or implementing policies for the promotion and encouragement of safe, integrated, efficient and economic transport facilities and services to, from and within their area and It must also keep accounts of how these fees are used.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2872"},{"id":"404","label":"Safeguarding vulnerable people - provide information to the Disclosure and Barring Service","desc":"A local authority must provide information to the Disclosure and Barring Service if requested to do so.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/404"},{"id":"403","label":"Safeguarding vulnerable people - referral to the Disclosure and Barring Service","desc":"A local authority may refer information to the Disclosure and Barring Service if they have reason to think that the person has engaged in conduct which may result in the risk of harm or actual harm to a child or vulnerable adult.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/403"},{"id":"1961","label":"Safety of stands at sports grounds - amendment, cancellation etc. of certificates","desc":"The local authority who have issued a safety certificate for a regulated stand at a sports ground can cancel, amend or replace the certificate","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/1961"},{"id":"3091","label":"Safety of stands at sports grounds - application for safety certificate","desc":"The local authority may, by notice, require an applicant for a safety certificate for a stand at a sports ground to furnish them, within such reasonable time as they may specify in the notice, with such information and such plans of the ground as they consider necessary for the purpose of discharging their functions in respect of the issue of safety certificates for the regulated stands at the ground.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/3091"},{"id":"1962","label":"Safety of stands at sports grounds - enforcement","desc":"It shall be the duty of every local authority to enforce within their area the safety provisions in respect of places of sport and to arrange for the periodical inspection of sports grounds at which there are regulated stands","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1962"},{"id":"1960","label":"Safety of stands at sports grounds - issue of certificates","desc":"The local authority shall in respect of any stand at a sports ground in their area make a preliminary determination whether or not that stand is a regulated stand and, if they determine that it is, they shall serve a notice on the person who appears to them to qualify for the issue of a general safety certificate stating their determination and the effects of it. It shall also be their duty to determine whether an applicant for a safety certificate qualifies for the issue of the certificate. The local authority shall notify the relevant bodies The local authority may, by notice, require an applicant for a safety certificate to furnish them within such reasonable time as they may specify in the notice with such information and such plans of the ground as they consider necessary for the purpose of discharging their functions in respect of the issue of safety certificates for the regulated stands at the ground.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/1960"},{"id":"1963","label":"Safety of stands at sports grounds - powers of entry and inspection","desc":"A person authorised by the local authority may enter a sports ground at any reasonable time, and make such inspection of the stands and such inquiries relating to them as he considers necessary for the purposes of safety, and in particular may examine records of the number of spectators accommodated, and the maintenance of safety, in the regulated stands at the ground, and take copies of such records.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/1963"},{"id":"2642","label":"School - premises","desc":"Maintained schools/local authorities must provide suitable toilet and washing facilities, medical accommodation and more generally, maintain the premises to a standard to maintain the health, safety and welfare of all pupils with specific reference to acoustics, lighting, drinking water and outside space.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2642"},{"id":"3499","label":"School admission appeals - appeal hearing and decision timing","desc":"All appeals which have been lodged, whether in time or not, must be heard and determined by an appeal panel as soon as reasonably practicable.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3499"},{"id":"3500","label":"School admission appeals - appeals regarding excluded children","desc":"Where the governing body of a school receives a written decision to admit to the school a child to whom, at the time when the decision is made section 87(2) of SSFA 1998 applies, any appeal must be made within 21 days from\u2014(a) the date of notification of the decision where that date is on or after 24th April 2020; or(b) the 24th April 2020 where\u2014(i) the decision was notified before 24th April 2020,(ii) no appeal has been lodged in response to the decision before 24th April 2020, and(iii) an existing appeal deadline relevant to the decision has not already expired before 24th April 2020.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3500"},{"id":"3494","label":"School admission appeals - conditions for appeal deadline","desc":"Where the admissions authority must review the existing deadline for an appeal and, where the conditions in sub-paragraph (3) are satisfied, the authority must set a new deadline for the appeal which must be\u2014(a) at least 28 days from the date of the notification of the new deadline, and(b) expressed by reference to a fixed date or a number of calendar days.(3) The conditions are that\u2014(a) no appeal has already been lodged in response to the admission decision,(b) the existing deadline refers to school days, or the admission authority otherwise considers that the existing deadline is unclear in all the circumstances; and(c) the existing deadline has not already expired.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3494"},{"id":"3492","label":"School admission appeals - deadlines for appeal submission","desc":"Where the admission authority or local authority sends an admission decision the deadline for an appeal specified in that admission decision must be\u2014(a) at least 28 days from the date of the notification of the admission decision, and(b) expressed by reference to a fixed date or a number of calendar days.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3492"},{"id":"3491","label":"School admission appeals - decision based on written evidence","desc":"(2) Where any of the conditions prescribed with regard to remote appeal hearings are not met, an appeal panel may make their decision on the appeal based on the written information submitted.(3) Where sub-paragraph (2) applies, the appeal panel must ensure that the parties are able to present fully their case, in order for the panel to make a decision on the appeal which is fair and transparent.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/3491"},{"id":"3501","label":"School admission appeals - decision regarding excluded children","desc":"All appeal hearings to which sub-paragraph (1) applies must be held, and appeals determined, as soon as reasonably practicable.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3501"},{"id":"3498","label":"School admission appeals - issue of decision letter","desc":"An appeal panel must send decision letters on appeals to the parties within 7 days of the hearing, or finalisation of the determination of the appeal, wherever possible.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3498"},{"id":"3495","label":"School admission appeals - notification of revised deadline","desc":"Where a new deadline has been set in accordance with sub-paragraph (2), notification of the new deadline must be sent to the recipient of the original admission decision within 28 days of 24th April 2020 or seven days from the date of an admission decision which does not comply with the requirements of sub-paragraph (1) whichever is later.(5) The notification of the new deadline must be sent by\u2014(a) the admission authority where that admission authority sent the relevant admission decision, or(b) the local authority where that authority sent the relevant admission decision on behalf of another admission authority.(6) The requirement in sub-paragraph (5)(b) only applies once the local authority has been informed of the new deadline by the relevant admission authority.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3495"},{"id":"3496","label":"School admission appeals - notification to appellant of appeal","desc":"The admission authority must provide appellants with at least 14 days' written notice of an appeal hearing.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3496"},{"id":"3490","label":"School admission appeals - remote appeal hearings","desc":"An appeal panel may decide to hold an appeal hearing using remote access provided\u2014(a)the parties are able to present fully their case;(b)each participant has access to the electronic means to allow them to hear and be heard and (where using a live video link) see and be seen, throughout the appeal hearing; and(c)the panel considers that the appeal is capable of being heard fairly and transparently.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/3490"},{"id":"3493","label":"School admission appeals - review of appeal deadline","desc":") In respect of an admission decision sent after 28th February 2020 which contains a deadline for an appeal that is not in accordance with the requirements of sub-paragraph (1)(a) or (b), the admission authority must review the existing deadline for the appeal","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3493"},{"id":"3497","label":"School admission appeals - revised deadline for submission of documents","desc":"The admission authority may set new or revised reasonable deadlines for\u2014(a) an appellant to submit additional evidence;(b) the admission authority to submit their evidence; and(c) the clerk to send relevant appeal papers to the appeal panel and the parties.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/3497"},{"id":"3489","label":"School admission appeals - withdrawal of panel chair due to Coronavirus","desc":"Where a member of an appeals panel has to withdraw due to Coronavirus, and the member withdrawing is the panel Chair, the admission authority must appoint (or arrange for the clerk to the appeal panel to appoint) one of the remaining members of the panel as the Chair.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3489"},{"id":"3488","label":"School admission appeals - withdrawal of panel members due to Coronavirus","desc":"Where one or more members of an appeal panel has to withdraw from membership of the panel as a result of a coronavirus exception, the appeal panel may continue to consider and determine the appeal provided there remains a panel of at least two members, regardless of whether those members meet the requirements of paragraph 1(2) of Schedule 1.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/3488"},{"id":"2693","label":"School admissions - common offer date","desc":"Decisions in relation to secondary school admissions for 2015/6 are to be communicated to parents on 1 March (or the next working day) and decisions in relation to primary school admissions for 2018/9 and subsequent academic years are to be communicated to parents on 16 April (or the next working day).","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2693"},{"id":"2694","label":"School admissions - infant class sizes","desc":"Save for prescribed exceptions, the limit on infant class sizes in Wales is 30 pupils.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2694"},{"id":"3718","label":"School admissions - information to be provided to Secretary of State","desc":"Information regarding the. number of schools and number of pupils at each school maintained by a local authority is to be provided to the Secretary of State after 1st June and before 4th August each year.Information to be provided is as specified in these Regulations.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3718"},{"id":"2695","label":"School admissions - variation of arrangements","desc":"A local authority (admission authority) may vary the admission arrangements that they have determined for any relevant age group where such a variation is necessary to give effect to the School Admissions Code; the implementation of approved proposals; or a correction to any omission or misprint in the admission arrangements and the procedures for changing admission arrangements in section 89(5) to (7) of the SSFA 1998 do not apply.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2695"},{"id":"2336","label":"School buses - fare-paying passengers on school buses","desc":"A local authority may use a school bus, when it is being used to provide free school transport, to carry as fare-paying passengers persons other than those for whom the free school transport is provided; use a school bus belonging to the authority, when it is not being used to provide free school transport, to provide a local service","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2336"},{"id":"3716","label":"School finance - budget for excluded pupils","desc":"Where a pupil is permanently excluded from a school maintained by a local authority (\u201cthe excluding school\u201d) the authority must redetermine the excluding school\u2019s budget share in accordance with Regulations. This also applies where an excluded pupil is admitted to another school maintained by a local authority during the budget period or where the excluded pupil is subsequently reinstated.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3716"},{"id":"885","label":"School transport - direction on complaint regarding sixth form transport","desc":"A local authority must revise a statement prepared under section 509AA to change certain arrangements if, as a result of a sixth form transport complaint, the Secretary of State has directed them to do so.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/885"},{"id":"879","label":"School transport - direction on complaints about young adult transport","desc":"A local authority must change its statement prepared under 508G in certain circumstances when directed to do so by the Secretary of State as result of a young adult complaint.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/879"},{"id":"886","label":"School transport - discretionary changes resulting from a complaint about sixth form transport","desc":"A local authority may revise a statement prepared under section 509AA to change certain arrangements as a result of a sixth form transport complaint.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/886"},{"id":"880","label":"School transport - discretionary changes resulting from a complaint on young adult transport","desc":"A local authority may change its statement prepared under 508G in certain circumstances as result of a young adult complaint.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/880"},{"id":"881","label":"School transport - early years transport","desc":"A local authority in England may provide a child with assistance if they are satisfied that, without such assistance, the child would be prevented from attending at any premises, which are not a school or part of a school, but at which relevant early years education is provided.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/881"},{"id":"874","label":"School transport - guidance on home to school travel arrangements","desc":"A local authority in England must consider any guidance issued by the Secretary of State when exercising their duty/power under sections 508B and 508C.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/874"},{"id":"878","label":"School transport - guidance on policy statements for adults and young adults","desc":"A local authority must when exercising its duties/powers under sections 508F and G have regard to guidance from the Secretary of State.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/878"},{"id":"872","label":"School transport - home to school travel arrangements for eligible children","desc":"A local authority in England must in the case of an eligible child in the authority's area make such travel arrangements as they consider necessary in order to secure that suitable home to school travel arrangements, for the purpose of facilitating the child's attendance at the relevant educational establishment in relation to him, are made and provided free of charge in relation to the child.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/872"},{"id":"873","label":"School transport - home to school travel arrangements for non-eligible children","desc":"A local authority in England may make such school travel arrangements as they consider necessary, in relation to any child in the authority's area to whom this section applies, for the purpose of facilitating the child's attendance at any relevant educational establishment in relation to the child.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/873"},{"id":"882","label":"School transport - policy on arrangements for persons of sixth form age","desc":"A local authority must prepare (and publish) for each academic year a transport policy statement specifying the arrangements for the provision of transport or otherwise that the authority consider it necessary to make for facilitating the attendance of persons of sixth form age receiving education or training at various institutions. The statement must meet various requirements.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/882"},{"id":"877","label":"School transport - policy statements for young adults subject to learning difficulty assessment","desc":"A local authority must when making arrangements, or proposing to pay travelling expenses, under section 508F in relation to relevant young adults, consult various parties and prepare a transport policy statement for young adults subject to learning difficulty assessment which must comply with various requirements.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/877"},{"id":"884","label":"School transport - regard to religion or belief in exercise of travel functions","desc":"A local authority in England must have regard to a parent's or a pupil's (where aged 16 or over) religion or belief when exercising its travel functions.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/884"},{"id":"870","label":"School transport - sustainable modes of travel strategy","desc":"A local authority in England must prepare for each academic year a document containing their strategy to promote the use of sustainable modes of travel to meet the school travel needs of their area (a sustainable modes of travel strategy), publish the strategy in such manner and by such time as may be prescribed, and promote the use of sustainable modes of travel to meet the school travel needs of their area.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/870"},{"id":"876","label":"School transport - transport for adult learners","desc":"A local authority must make such arrangements for the provision of transport and otherwise as they consider necessary, or as the Secretary of State may direct to facilitate the attendance of adults receiving education at institutions maintained or assisted by the authority and providing further or higher education (or both), or within the further education sector and to facilitate the attendance of relevant young adults receiving education or training at institutions outside both the further and higher education sectors, but only in cases where the have secured for the adults in question the provision of education or training at the institution in question, and the provision of boarding accommodation under section514A. Any transport provided must be provided free of charge.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/876"},{"id":"875","label":"School transport- school travel schemes","desc":"A local authority in England must give effect to a school travel scheme when one is in force.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/875"},{"id":"24","label":"Schools - academy board and lodging","desc":"A local authority must pay an Academy for the full cost of board and lodging at a child registered there if suitable education cannot be provided elsewhere and the whole or a suitable proportion of those charges where the payment of the charges would involve financial hardship to the child's parent.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/24"},{"id":"2649","label":"Schools - academy conversion surplus","desc":"The LA must determine the surpluses in federated schools which are converting to Academies according to a prescribed calculation; notify the proprietor (as prescribed) within four months of conversion; follow the procedure set out in the event of a review by the Secretary of State and pay any surplus determined as a result of the review within one month.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2649"},{"id":"23","label":"Schools - academy property transfer scheme","desc":"A local authority must comply with a transfer scheme made by the Secretary of State in respect of property, rights and liabilities of a former maintained school which is becoming an Academy.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/23"},{"id":"3840","label":"Schools - access to pupils for post 16 education providers","desc":"The proprietor of a school must allow post 16 education providers access to registered pupils on at least two occasions during each of the first, second and third key phase of their education and ensure that the provider provides required information to the pupil.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3840"},{"id":"2623","label":"Schools - admissions","desc":"Local authorities must adhere to prescribed matters in relation to the content of the admission arrangements determined each year; the proportion of selective admissions, the prescribed subjects for selection by aptitude; and the priority to be given to looked after children (who have to be looked after at the time of their application to the school). They must consult with prescribed bodies for at least 8 weeks up to 1 March, including with the school's governing body where they propose to increase or keep the same number, and publish their proposed admission arrangements on their website and send copies as prescribed. For admission arrangements for academic year 2014-2015 and subsequent years\u2019, consultation must commence no earlier than 1st November 2012.Local authorities must publicise information about local schools\u2019 admission arrangements and explain the right to refer an objection to the adjudicator. Local authorities must also follow procedures regarding the variation, referral to the schools adjudicator, the co-ordination of admission arrangements, formulation and publication of substantially different schemes where it is 7 years since the last consultation.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2623"},{"id":"2624","label":"Schools - admissions appeals","desc":"A local authority must constitute an appeal panel as prescribed for appeals brought under the School Standards and Framework Act 1998","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2624"},{"id":"2697","label":"Schools - alterations and changes of category","desc":"Local authorities/Governing bodies of maintained schools may publish and determine their own change of category and other prescribed alterations in the prescribed manner of publication, determination and implementation.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2697"},{"id":"3787","label":"Schools - annual publication of information","desc":"The local authority must publish information stipulated in these regulations, regarding schools in their area. Information is to be published during the offer year and within the timescales specified.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3787"},{"id":"257","label":"Schools - appointment of additional governors","desc":"A local authority may appoint additional governors to the governing body of a maintained school eligible for intervention.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/257"},{"id":"919","label":"Schools - approval etc. of school premises and boarding hostels","desc":"A local authority must obtain the Secretary of State's approval for certain new or altered schools or boarding hostels.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/919"},{"id":"903","label":"Schools - arrangements for cleansing of pupils","desc":"A local authority must make arrangements for any cleansing of a pupil or his or her clothing that may be required.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/903"},{"id":"2664","label":"Schools - assessments","desc":"Schools must follow prescribed assessment arrangements for reading and numeracy for pupils who attend schools maintained by the local authority.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2664"},{"id":"2654","label":"Schools - careers guidance","desc":"Schools must provide pupils with independent careers guidance from school year 8 to 13","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2654"},{"id":"22","label":"Schools - ceasing maintenance on conversion to academy status","desc":"A local authority must cease to maintain a school on the date upon which it converts to Academy status.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/22"},{"id":"2793","label":"Schools - change of category","desc":"The governing body and the local authority must secure by the end of the implementation period that a new instrument of government is made for the school in accordance with the 2005 Regulations or the 2014 Regulations and must secure that, as soon as reasonably practicable after the commencement of the implementation period (and in any event within a period of 3 months beginning on the implementation date), the governing body is reconstituted in accordance with the new instrument of government and the 2005 Regulations or the 2014 Regulations. They must also adhere to the provisions regarding Governor surplus.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2793"},{"id":"28","label":"Schools - change of land use","desc":"A local authority must inform the Secretary of State in respect of a proposed change of use with regard to land held for school or Academy purposes.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/28"},{"id":"2527","label":"Schools - changing of session times","desc":"A local authority in Wales may change school session times (start and end times of the school day) in accordance with the procedure set out in the Regulations","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2527"},{"id":"890","label":"Schools - charging for provision of meals","desc":"A local authority may charge for school meals provided.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/890"},{"id":"2677","label":"Schools - clerk to governing body","desc":"A local authority must provide the governing body of a maintained school with a suitable clerk (a governor support officer or someone who has completed the clerk training) within 16 weeks of being requested by the governing body to do so and may charge a fee to cover the cost of providing the clerk.A Governing body must remove the clerk if the training has not been completed within 1 year.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2677"},{"id":"249","label":"Schools - closure of a community or a foundation special school","desc":"A local authority must close a community or a foundation special school when directed to do so by the Secretary of State on the grounds of health, safety or pupil welfare.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/249"},{"id":"248","label":"Schools - closure of a maintained school","desc":"A local authority may publish proposals to close a maintained school and must follow guidance published by the Secretary of State in so doing.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/248"},{"id":"260","label":"Schools - closure on direction of Secretary of State","desc":"A local authority must comply with the direction of the Secretary of State under section 68 to close a maintained school.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/260"},{"id":"912","label":"Schools - co-operation of governing body for provision of school meals","desc":"A governing body of a school maintained by local authority must co-operate with a local authority in relation to the local authority's duty to provide school meals.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/912"},{"id":"269","label":"Schools - co-operation with Chief Inspector for investigation of a complaint","desc":"The governing body of a school and/or the local authority must provide the Chief Inspector with such information as he requires and co-operate as required where a qualifying complaint is made to the Chief Inspector by a person who is a registered parent of a registered pupil at the school to which the complaint relates.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/269"},{"id":"3750","label":"Schools - composite prospectus (England)","desc":"No later than 12th September in the offer year a local authority must publish a composite prospectus in relation to all maintained schools, Academies, city technology colleges and city colleges for the technology of the arts.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3750"},{"id":"2597","label":"Schools - composite prospectus (Wales)","desc":"Local authorities must publish a composite prospectus annually containing information relating to all maintained schools in the prospectus area no later than 1 October each year or not later than 6 weeks before parents may express a preference for a school and make it available on request, at the local authority\u2019s libraries and on its website. It m must detail SEN provision and any exceptional provision of education in schools or elsewhere and miscellaneous information as prescribed.Governing bodies must make information available to local authorities and publish a school prospectus. Information must be provided in translation in English or Welsh without charge.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2597"},{"id":"902","label":"Schools - compulsory cleansing of pupil","desc":"A local authority may issue a notice requiring a parent to cleanse a pupil and carry out that task itself if the parent is in default.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/902"},{"id":"26","label":"Schools - consent of Secretary of State to transfer","desc":"A local authority must not dispose of land held for a school or Academy without the consent of the Secretary of State.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/26"},{"id":"2766","label":"Schools - control and use of premises","desc":"A local authority or the Governing body, depending on the type of maintained school, must comply with Regulations regarding the use of school premises.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2766"},{"id":"920","label":"Schools - control of potentially harmful materials or apparatus","desc":"A local authority must comply with regulations relating to the use of potentially harmful materials or apparatus on school premises.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/920"},{"id":"271","label":"Schools - distribution and charges for maintained school inspection reports in England","desc":"The governing body of a school and/or the local authority must make available and distribute the Chief Inspector's report in accordance with regulations. In prescribed cases a charge may be made which should not exceed the cost of supply.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/271"},{"id":"274","label":"Schools - distribution and charges for maintained school inspection reports in Wales","desc":"The governing body of a school in Wales and/or the local authority must make available and distribute the Chief Inspector's report with a supplementary power to charge in some cases.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/274"},{"id":"926","label":"Schools - duration of school day and school year","desc":"A local authority or the governing body of a school maintained by a local authority must comply with regulations regarding the duration of the school day and school year.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/926"},{"id":"2750","label":"Schools - early years funding","desc":"Local authorities must determine budget shares for schools maintained by them and the amounts to be allocated in respect of early years provision in their areas, in accordance with the prescribed formulae. Local authorities must ensure they meet the minimum funding guarantee and requirements in relation to their own schemes under the Act.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2750"},{"id":"266","label":"Schools - education for excluded pupil","desc":"The governing body of a maintained school must make arrangements for the provision of education to pupils excluded on disciplinary grounds.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/266"},{"id":"281","label":"Schools - educational performance targets","desc":"A local authority must comply with regulations published by the Secretary of State relating to annual targets in schools.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/281"},{"id":"2696","label":"Schools - establishment and discontinuance","desc":"Local authorities must have regard to prescribed procedures and matters during the establishment and discontinuance of schools pursuant to the provisions contained in Part 2 of the Education and Inspections Act 2006.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2696"},{"id":"242","label":"Schools - establishment of an academy","desc":"A local authority must, if they believe a new school is required for their area, seek proposals for the establishment of an Academy and notify the Secretary of State.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/242"},{"id":"901","label":"Schools - examination of pupils for cleanliness","desc":"A local authority may direct a medical officer that a pupil or his/her clothing must be examined for cleanliness.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/901"},{"id":"2643","label":"Schools - exclusion from school","desc":"A head teacher must inform the parent of the excluded pupil or the pupil (if over 18), the governing body of the details of an exclusion and the LA if the exclusion is permanent, if the exclusion will result in the pupil missing a public examination or a National Curriculum test, or if the exclusion takes the total exclusions for that pupil to more than 5 school days in any term. The Governing Body, or the Management Committee of a Pupil Referral Unit, must consider reinstatement in prescribed circumstances. An LA must make arrangements for a review by a review panel of decisions not to reinstate a pupil permanently excluded, if the relevant person applies for a review. Regard must be had to guidance given by the Secretary of State.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2643"},{"id":"3110","label":"Schools - exit or dissolution of federation","desc":"The responsible LA must establish a temporary governing body and issue and review an instrument of government in respect of a school which wishes to exit a federation or where a federation is to dissolve.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3110"},{"id":"2645","label":"Schools - federation and appointment of governors","desc":"A maintained school may federate and appoint governors in accordance with the procedure set out and may make, review and vary a federation's instrument of government and the contents of that instrument which must conform to the School Governance (Constitution) (England) Regulations 2012.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2645"},{"id":"2724","label":"Schools - federation of maintained schools","desc":"Schools may federate in the prescribed circumstances (at least two schools, but no more than six) according to the prescribed procedure","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2724"},{"id":"21","label":"Schools - financial or other assistance to academy","desc":"A local authority may provide financial or other assistance in respect of the Academy, including by (a) making payments in respect of some (but not all) of the expenses of maintaining the Academy, (b) providing premises, goods or services for the Academy, or (c) by making premises, goods or services available to be used for the purposes of the Academy.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/21"},{"id":"30","label":"Schools - formation of company for academy","desc":"The Governing Body of a maintained school may form a company to enter into Academy arrangements or do anything incidental.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/30"},{"id":"2765","label":"Schools - formation of company for governing body","desc":"A governing body of a school maintained by a local authority may form a governing body company to deliver certain prescribed functions and services.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/2765"},{"id":"891","label":"Schools - free school meals","desc":"Where a local authority provides school lunches or milk they must be provided free of charge to those entitled to free school meals.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/891"},{"id":"2644","label":"Schools - governing bodies","desc":"A maintained school/local authority must follow prescribed arrangements for the constitution of governing bodies of maintained schools, (which includes maintained nursery schools) including the appointment of parent, staff, LA, foundation and partnership governors, their term of office and removal and provide copies of the instrument of government to every member of the governing body, the head teacher and others as prescribed and applicable","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2644"},{"id":"2678","label":"Schools - governor training","desc":"The chair of a governing body and newly appointed governors must complete chair and induction training respectively within prescribed time limits failing which they must cease to hold office or be suspended respectively until completed. Subject to prescribed exceptions, governors are also required to complete school performance data training within a prescribed time period failing which they must be suspended until completed. 6 months suspension will lead to disqualification from office.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2678"},{"id":"2596","label":"Schools - governors reports","desc":"Governors' reports must contained prescribed informationIf a parents\u2019 meeting is held under s94 of the School Standards and Organisation (Wales) Act 2013\u2014the date and place the meeting was held and reasons for the meeting, attendees\u2019 names, a brief description of matters discussed and any action to be taken in consequence of the matters discussed at the meeting; (and if not held under that section, a statement to that effect or confirming that no meeting was held). It must also contain particulars of the governing body, any information about: forthcoming elections of parent governors, a financial statement, school performance (as prescribed), absence, community links, targets, participation in sports, policy reviews, term dates, prospectus changes, an education statement (including on SEN arrangements), the language, Welsh, toilet and cleaning provision and a summary of the development plan. A governing body must determine the language(s) in which such reports must be produced and ensure parents are provided with copies of such reports","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2596"},{"id":"899","label":"Schools - governors travel and subsistence allowances","desc":"A local authority may pay in accordance with a scheme travelling and subsistence allowance to governors in certain circumstances.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/899"},{"id":"264","label":"Schools - guidance of the Secretary of State regarding schools causing concern","desc":"A local authority must have regard to the guidance of the Secretary of State when exercising their functions in relation to schools causing concern.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/264"},{"id":"3802","label":"Schools - guidance regarding school uniforms","desc":"A relevant school must have regard to guidance, in respect of costs, issued by the Secretary of State under this section when developing and implementing a school uniform policy for the school.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3802"},{"id":"3646","label":"Schools - Head Teacher's annual report","desc":"Prior to the end of the summer term of every school year, the head teacher shall prepare a head teacher\u2019s report in respect of every registered pupil at the school.The annual report written by the Head teacher for every pupil must include information as specified in Schedule 1 of these Regulations.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3646"},{"id":"2669","label":"Schools - healthy school meals","desc":"Local authorities and governing bodies of maintained schools and nurseries that provide food and drink to pupils, whether on school premises or not, and to other persons on school premises must comply with the prescribed types of food and drink that can, and cannot, be provided during the school day and define the nutrient content of school lunches.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2669"},{"id":"864","label":"Schools - improperly constituted governing body","desc":"A local authority or the governing body of a school maintained by them must comply with directions from the Secretary of State in relation to a situation where a governing body is improperly constituted.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/864"},{"id":"2637","label":"Schools - infant class sizes","desc":"A School/local authority may not exceed a maximum of 30 pupils in an infant class at any time while an ordinary teaching session is conducted by a single school teacher (or, where the session is conducted by more than one school teacher, a maximum of 30 pupils for every teacher. Certain types of children are excepted as prescribed for counting purposes.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2637"},{"id":"3762","label":"Schools - information for training of school workforce","desc":"A local authority must give the Secretary of State in England, or HEFCW in Wales such information as the Secretary of State or HEFCW may require for the purpose of the exercise of the Secretary of State's functions relating to training for members of the school workforce.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3762"},{"id":"3720","label":"Schools - information to be published","desc":"A local authority must publish information as specified in Schedule 3 of these regulations regarding schools in the authority area. Information must be published in accordance with these regulations.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3720"},{"id":"276","label":"Schools - inspection of religious education in England","desc":"The governing body of schools with religious character to comply with prescribed procedure for denominational inspection. Inspection reports must be made available in accordance with regulations.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/276"},{"id":"277","label":"Schools - inspection of religious education in Wales","desc":"The governing body of schools in Wales with religious character to comply with prescribed procedure for denominational inspection.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/277"},{"id":"273","label":"Schools - inspections in Wales","desc":"The Governing Body of a maintained school in Wales and the authority responsible for maintaining that school must comply with the requirements laid down with regard to inspections in Wales.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/273"},{"id":"258","label":"Schools - interim executive members on governing body","desc":"A local authority may provide for a governing body of a maintained school eligible for intervention to consist of interim executive members.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/258"},{"id":"243","label":"Schools - invitation for proposal for establishment of new school","desc":"A local authority may, with the consent of the Secretary of State, invite proposals for the establishment of a new foundation or voluntary school or an Academy having regard to guidance from the Secretary of State in the process.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/243"},{"id":"261","label":"Schools - issue of standards warning notice on direction of Secretary of State","desc":"A local authority must comply with the direction of the Secretary of State to issue a performance standards and safety warning notice.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/261"},{"id":"262","label":"Schools - issue of teachers pay and conditions warning notice on direction of Secretary of State","desc":"A local authority must comply with the direction of the Secretary of State to issue a teachers' pay and conditions warning notice.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/262"},{"id":"278","label":"Schools - LEA inspection of maintained schools in England","desc":"Where for the purpose of enabling them to exercise any function of theirs, a local education authority require information about any matter in connection with a school which is maintained by them, and it is not reasonably practicable for them to obtain the information in any other manner,they may cause an inspection of the school to be made by one or more of their officers for the purpose of obtaining the information.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/278"},{"id":"279","label":"Schools - LEA inspection of schools in Wales","desc":"Any local education authority in Wales may provide a school inspection service for schools within their area. Any school inspection service provided by a local education authority in Wales may, in addition to providing for the inspection of schools which are maintained by them, provide for the inspection of schools which are not maintained by them. The authority must comply with the directions of the Assembly when so doing.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/279"},{"id":"2545","label":"Schools - maintaining a register","desc":"LAs/Schools are required to include pupils\u2019 names in the admissions register and may only mark them as absent or remove names in certain specified circumstances. Computer stored records must be backed up not less than once a month.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2545"},{"id":"900","label":"Schools - medical and dental inspections","desc":"A local authority must make arrangements for encouraging and assisting pupils to take advantage of the provision for medical and dental inspection and treatment, unless a parent directs otherwise.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/900"},{"id":"400","label":"Schools - medical inspection of children in Wales","desc":"A local authority must co-operate with Welsh ministers in carrying out the Welsh minister's functions of making arrangements for the medical inspection of children in Wales.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/400"},{"id":"389","label":"Schools - medical inspection of pupils at maintained schools","desc":"A local authority must carry out the medical inspection of pupils at maintained schools or receiving education otherwise than at school in its area.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/389"},{"id":"390","label":"Schools - medical inspection of pupils at other schools","desc":"A local authority may make arrangements to carry out the medical inspection of pupils at educational establishments not maintained by it in its area with a limited power to charge.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/390"},{"id":"3733","label":"Schools - moderating KS1 teacher assessments","desc":"Local authorities must make provision for moderating teacher assessments at key stage 1 in respect of the schools which they maintain in relation to at least 25% of all relevant schools.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3733"},{"id":"3788","label":"Schools - monitoring of key stage 2 assessments","desc":"In any school year the local authority should visit 10% of the schools for which they are responsible to monitor the assessment arrangements for the national curriculum key stage 2.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/3788"},{"id":"2737","label":"Schools - National Curriculum assessment","desc":"Local authorities/Headteachers of maintained schools must make arrangements for all pupils in the foundation, second and third stage to be assessed throughout the year by a teacher for the purpose of monitoring and supporting the pupils educational progress","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2737"},{"id":"2665","label":"Schools - national curriculum attainment targets","desc":"Schools have a duty to follow the National Curriculum attainment targets for core and other foundation subjects at all four key stages (except that there are no attainment targets atkey stage 4). The current programmes of study and attainment targets are revoked save for prescribed exceptions.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2665"},{"id":"922","label":"Schools - no right to give corporal punishment","desc":"A local authority or the governing body of a school maintained by a local authority may not administer corporal punishment.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/922"},{"id":"2721","label":"Schools - notification of term dates","desc":"A local authority must notify the Welsh Ministers of all term dates which have been determined for the maintained schools in its area no later than the final working day in August in the year two years immediately preceding the beginning of the first school year for which the term dates have been determined","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2721"},{"id":"921","label":"Schools - nuisance or disturbance on school premises","desc":"An officer authorised by a local authority may, in certain circumstances, remove someone causing a nuisance or annoyance from a school premise and may in certain circumstances bring proceedings against such a person.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/921"},{"id":"2749","label":"Schools - nutritional requirements","desc":"Local authorities or Governing Bodies of maintained schools, nurseries and PRUs must comply with prescribed nutritional requirements whenever they provide food or drink on, or in certain circumstances outside of, school premises.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2749"},{"id":"2543","label":"Schools - off-site provision for behaviour improvement","desc":"LAs/Governing bodies of maintained schools must give notice containing prescribed information to a person they have imposed a requirement under s29A(1) of the Education Act on to attend off site provision to improve behaviour. They are required to keep the provision under review and have regard to guidance in force","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2543"},{"id":"439","label":"Schools - parenting contracts","desc":"A local authority or a school governing body may enter into parenting contract with the parent of a child who has misbehaved at school or is involved in truancy.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/439"},{"id":"440","label":"Schools - parenting orders","desc":"A local authority or a school governing body may apply for a parenting order in respect of the parents of a child who has been excluded from school.","type":"power","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/power/440"},{"id":"268","label":"Schools - payment of annual fee to Chief Inspector","desc":"A local authority must pay an annual fee to the Chief Inspector as specified by regulations.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/268"},{"id":"2698","label":"Schools - penalty notices for non-attendance","desc":"A school must include prescribed information in a penalty notice (operated under section 444A of the Education Act 1996) and provide a copy to the local authority. A local authority may issue a notice in prescribed circumstances and may withdraw a penalty notice where it determines that it ought not to have been issued or contains material errors. It must draw up and consult on a code of conduct for the issuing of penalty notices and keep records as detailed. It must provide information to the Welsh Ministers if required and spend sums received as prescribed.","type":"duty","uri":"http://id.esd.org.uk/duty/2698"},{"id":"2589","label":"Schools - performance information","desc":"Head teachers of maintained schools must make information available to governing bodies to enable them to comply.
